articles.title: Lebanon front heats up as Iran warns Israel over strategic ridge
articles.body:
Lebanese media reported Saturday morning that seven people were killed and two others wounded in overnight Israeli strikes in the Ali al-Taher ridge area and the villages of Ansar and Nabatieh al-Fawqa.
The IDF confirmed that it had struck Hezbollah infrastructure, saying the strikes came “In response to an action by the Hezbollah terrorist organization against IDF soldiers in the Ali al-Taher Ridge, which is located in the Security Zone where IDF soldiers are operating.”
The strikes came a day after Lebanese reports said Iran had warned that an Israeli attack on the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge could draw Tehran directly into the escalating confrontation.
Official sources told Lebanon’s Al-Jadeed television Friday that “Tehran conveyed a direct message to the relevant parties that an Israeli attack in the Ali al-Taher area would be met by Iran entering the cycle of escalation.”
According to the report, Israel is refusing to withdraw from the area under terms that would allow it to be transferred to the Lebanese army, while Hezbollah insists the ridge cannot be handed over without a full Israeli withdrawal.
The report came amid growing concern in Lebanon over a possible Israeli operation to seize the strategic ridge.
A senior security official told the Lebanese newspaper Al-Joumhouria that authorities in Beirut had received messages indicating that Israel was preparing to launch an operation to capture Ali al-Taher. The official said Israel was ready to act and was awaiting a green light from the United States.
The official claimed Washington had informed Lebanese authorities that it could not completely prevent an Israeli operation but had asked that any action be a precise, surgical operation with minimal civilian casualties and that it not undermine the framework agreement between Jerusalem and Beirut.
“The Israelis need this achievement and will not back away from it,” the official said.
Attention, he added, was now focused on Hezbollah’s response and whether the group would enter the fighting.
“This battle has become a matter of time, and it is a race against the approaching U.S.-Iran agreement, which will undoubtedly affect the front in southern Lebanon,” he said.
Lebanese television channels have in recent days carried widespread speculation about Israel’s next move in southern Lebanon, with particular attention focused on the Ali al-Taher ridge.
Hezbollah operatives are trapped in an underground facility there as Israeli forces tighten a siege and cut water supply lines to the site. Hezbollah operatives have been attempting to break the siege by using drones to transport equipment and supplies.
Operating in the West Bank, preparing for Lebanon
Israeli troops who were operating deep inside Lebanon only about three months ago are now conducting intensive operations in the West Bank while simultaneously preparing for the possibility of renewed fighting on Israel’s northern front.
Soldiers from the 931st Battalion of the Nahal Brigade are currently operating under the Ephraim Regional Brigade in the northern and central West Bank. Between nighttime arrests in Tulkarm and searches for weapons in Palestinian villages, the troops are being required to maintain combat readiness with an eye toward Lebanon.
This week, the battalion completed an intensive two-day exercise in Nahal Kana, a rugged valley in the West Bank chosen to simulate fighting in the dense, mountainous terrain of southern Lebanon.
Despite the demands of its ongoing operational deployment, the unit conducted a full battalion-level exercise.
The terrain, characterized by deep ravines, steep ridges and dense vegetation, was used to replicate the challenging conditions troops could encounter in Lebanon.
“We took advantage of the terrain that best simulates Lebanon,” the battalion commander, identified only as Lt. Col. N. in accordance with IDF rules, told ynet.
“It was a full battalion exercise, despite the manpower constraints of holding an operational sector, with all the supporting capabilities — firepower, drones and a complete operational command structure surrounding us, along with simulated enemy forces and FPV drones,” he said.
“The terrain of the ravines and dense vegetation required commanders and soldiers to analyze the ground all over again,” he added. “That is a central lesson from the fighting: Everything begins with terrain analysis, especially in a place like Lebanon, which is unlike any other sector.”
One of the major threats Israeli forces have faced in Lebanon is Hezbollah’s use of explosive-laden fiber-optic first-person-view (FPV) drones, which can be difficult to disrupt through conventional electronic warfare because they are controlled through physical cables rather than radio signals.
The battalion commander acknowledged that the military initially struggled to respond to the threat.
“It’s no secret that there was frustration in the military over the threat at the beginning,” he said. “But today we are preparing for the war that will be, not the war that was.”
The military has since developed standardized procedures, defensive measures and technological solutions for protection and interception in cooperation with civilian companies, he said.
“During the exercise, all of our systems were networked, and the soldiers practiced a precise response procedure,” he said.
Katz vows long-term Israeli presence, drawing US criticism
Defense Minister Israel Katz visited Lebanon on Wednesday and declared that Israeli troops would remain in security zones in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza for the long term.
“The IDF is here to stay in the security zones in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza,” Katz said. “I have instructed the IDF to take all necessary steps to prepare for a long-term presence in the area.”
His remarks drew criticism from Washington. A U.S. State Department official later said the United States “expects all parties to act in any manner consistent with the framework they agreed to, and Israel clearly stated that it has no territorial ambition in Lebanon.”
“A permanent military presence in south Lebanon is not consistent with the commitments made in the framework or the long-term peace and security of both states,” the official said.
The United States fully supports Lebanon’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, the official added, saying the framework explicitly provides for a conditions-based, phased Israeli redeployment tied to the verified disarmament of Hezbollah and dismantling of its infrastructure.
During his visit, Katz referred to the Beaufort ridge, a strategically important high ground overlooking northern Israel and large areas of southern Lebanon.
“We see the Beaufort Ridge here after the tunnels there were destroyed,” Katz said. “The IDF maneuvered here across the Litani. With extraordinary courage and skill, it defeated Hezbollah and captured the Beaufort, which protects Metula, the northern communities and IDF soldiers, and threatens all of Hezbollah’s territory on the horizon.”
Katz said Israel had no intention of withdrawing from the security zone.
“As the prime minister and I have made unequivocally clear, we are not withdrawing from this security zone,” he said. “I am standing here in the heart of the security zone, from the western coastline to the Beaufort area and the approaches to Mount Hermon in the east.”
“The IDF is here to protect the northern communities and its forces,” Katz continued. “We will clear this area and ensure the security of the residents of the north — and under no circumstances will we withdraw from the security zones: not in Lebanon, not in Syria and not in Gaza.”
Katz said the policy reflected lessons Israel learned from the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, which triggered the Gaza war and subsequent fighting across the region.
“The lesson of Oct. 7 is that we protect residents by having the IDF here, in these places, protecting them from raids, gunfire and everything else,” he said. “That is our policy, that is our approach.”
Katz said the Beaufort fortress demonstrated the logic of the strategy.
“We are up here, they are down there, the residents are protected,” he said. “The IDF is inside; 200,000 residents are outside. We are destroying the underground infrastructure and all the terrorist infrastructure they built with Iranian backing to invade the Galilee, and destroying all the homes in the area.”
Negotiations expected to resume after summer
Earlier this week, a diplomatic source told the Hezbollah-aligned Lebanese television network Al Mayadeen that there were no plans for another round of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel next month.
If another round takes place, it will likely be after the summer, the source said.
According to the report, Israel and the United States rejected expanding pilot zones before progress was made in two previously designated areas. Both Israel and Washington also demanded that Hezbollah withdraw from the Ali al-Taher ridge in the Nabatieh area.
The source said the Lebanese delegation rejected Israel’s assertion that explosions in southern Lebanon were the result of strikes on military infrastructure.
The Hezbollah-aligned Lebanese newspaper Al-Akhbar separately reported that Israel had proposed an exchange involving civilians during talks with Lebanon and raised the issue of Lebanon’s historic Jewish community.
According to the report, Israel noted that Jews who left Lebanon years ago were seeking to transfer the remains of relatives from Jewish cemeteries in Lebanon for reburial in Israel.
The report said Israeli negotiators referred to “a significant number of remains” in Jewish cemeteries in Beirut and Sidon.
Thousands of Jews lived in Lebanon until the period surrounding the 1967 Six-Day War, continuing a Jewish presence in the country that stretched back centuries. Estimates suggest that Lebanon’s Jewish population reached between 12,000 and 20,000 at its peak.
The issue of Jewish remains in Lebanon was also raised over the weekend by the Saudi newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat.
Sources told the newspaper that “the Israeli negotiating delegation demanded the return of the remains of Lebanese Jews who were killed during the civil war, and information about the fate of Lebanese Jews who disappeared during Lebanon’s civil war, particularly in the 1980s.”
According to the report, Israel also sought information about Ron Arad, an Israeli air force navigator who went missing after his aircraft was shot down over Lebanon in 1986, or the return of his remains if he is dead.
Sources quoted by the newspaper described the Israeli demands as “impossible,” saying the Lebanese state “knows nothing about the remains of the Jews, nor about Ron Arad.”
Asharq Al-Awsat reported that the issues had also been raised during the U.S.-mediated negotiations that led to the 2022 maritime border agreement between Israel and Lebanon. The parties understood at the time, according to the report, that Lebanon lacked the ability to determine what had happened to the missing people.
Lebanon’s LBCI television network reported last week, citing sources, that preliminary lists concerning prisoners and missing people had been exchanged.
“The Lebanese side submitted preliminary lists regarding prisoners and missing persons, while the Israeli side presented a list of names of missing and deceased Lebanese Jews,” the report said.
Lebanon’s Jewish community was historically concentrated in Beirut’s Jewish quarter, Wadi Abu Jamil. The community gradually dispersed during and after Lebanon’s 1975-1990 civil war, with many members emigrating abroad.
Moshe Zafrani, who left Lebanon at age 14, has previously said communities of Lebanese Jews and their descendants can now be found in France, Mexico, New York and Brazil, as well as across Israel, including in Bat Yam, Holon and Haifa.

articles.title: Palestinian voter registration begins ahead of 1st legislative elections in 20 years
articles.body:
Hosni Nedim and Rania Abushamala
15 August 2026•Update: 15 August 2026
Voter registration and data updates began across the occupied West Bank on Saturday ahead of Palestinian legislative elections scheduled for Nov. 28, the first such vote in nearly 20 years.
Registration centers opened to the public Saturday morning, with the process set to continue until Wednesday evening, according to the timetable announced by the Central Elections Commission.
The commission called on eligible citizens whose names are not on the electoral register to sign up and urged registered voters to update their information if necessary, stressing that registration is a key stage of the electoral process.
It said the elections would be held in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, including Jerusalem, and that Palestinians aged 17 and above are eligible to register.
The data update process is limited to the West Bank, while Gaza residents are automatically registered based on the Palestinian civil registry, the commission added.
The vote will be the first Palestinian legislative elections since 2006. Coming after years of internal Palestinian division and the Gaza war, the elections are seen as a test of efforts to rebuild Palestinian institutions and renew their legitimacy.
Hamas political bureau member Husam Badran said Wednesday that the group would participate in the elections “within the broadest possible national coalition.”
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree on July 9 setting Nov. 28 as the date for the legislative elections.
The date of the presidential election will be announced later, with voting planned for the first quarter of 2027.
According to the commission, candidate registration will run from Sept. 26 to Oct. 7, while campaigning will begin on Nov. 6 ahead of the general vote on Nov. 28.

articles.title: Handball captain confident of medal chances at 2026 Asian Games
articles.body:
Handball captain confident of medal chances at 2026 Asian Games
TEHRAN - Iran men’s national handball team captain Ali Rahimi Kazerooni believes the national side can fight for a medal at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, despite a difficult group and the absence of several overseas-based players.
Speaking to reporters ahead of Iran’s departure for a training camp in Serbia, Rahimi Kazerooni said the team had completed their third training camp and praised new head coach Nenad Kljaic for bringing fresh ideas to the squad.
“We have almost gone through a generational change in the national team, and I hope we can achieve the best possible result at the Asian Games in Nagoya,” the captain said.
Rahimi Kazerooni added that the team’s physical preparation was progressing well, while the tactical sessions had also been productive.
“The strength and conditioning sessions are going well, and the tactical camps have been good too. The draw for the Asian Games is difficult, but I hope we can deliver our best performance in Nagoya. We will not go into the competition without a fight.”
The Iran captain also acknowledged that the absence of the team’s foreign-based players could have a significant impact on their campaign. According to Rahimi Kazerooni, overseas-based players bring valuable international experience and play important roles within the national team.
“They have more experience, and their absence in Nagoya will make things more difficult because they are key players. I hope we can make sure their absence is not felt too much,” he said.
The men’s handball tournament at the 2026 Asian Games will be held in Nagoya, Japan, from Sept. 19 to 28.
Iran have been drawn in Group B, alongside South Korea, Kuwait, Bahrain and Kazakhstan.

articles.title: Intel. Min. warns France against meddling in Iran's affairs
articles.body:
The ministry also stressed that Tehran will take appropriate action if such activities are repeated.
In a statement released on Saturday, the ministry said its forces discovered the presence of two French diplomats at the location of a secret meeting while carrying out a judicial order to arrest two suspects in a major case involving foreign infiltration and interference.
The ministry said the two diplomats had extensive records of violations and conduct inconsistent with Iranian laws and their diplomatic obligations. After verifying their identities, the matter was reported to Iran’s Foreign Ministry, and the diplomats were subsequently handed over to the Iranian ambassador to France in the presence of diplomatic police, according to the statement.
The Intelligence Ministry said it initially refrained from publicly disclosing the diplomats’ violations while investigating the suspects and examining documents and evidence recovered from the meeting site.
It lashed out at French officials for subsequently launching a media campaign aimed at “covering up their established violations” and deflecting attention from the case.
The ministry said a preliminary examination of the documents recovered during the search has revealed a “sinister project,” shedding light on France’s concerns following the discovery.
According to the statement, initial investigations point to the planning of an extensive operation involving infiltration, foreign interference and efforts to pave the way for French action against Iran’s independence. It said the project involved identifying targeted individuals, establishing covert contacts inside and outside Iran, and building networks while observing secrecy measures.
The ministry further said contracts discovered as part of the project bore the signature of France’s former ambassador to Iran, adding, “France must be held accountable for its illegal and interventionist actions and explain this ill-conceived scheme.”
The Intelligence Ministry stressed that the activities had taken place during wartime and described them as a clear violation of Iranian law and diplomatic norms.
“Given the infiltration and overt interference in Iran’s internal affairs, particularly during wartime, and the blatant violation of the country’s laws and departure from diplomatic frameworks that have been conclusively established in this project, the Intelligence Ministry warns that it will not allow its diplomatic guests to engage in illegal and interventionist behavior,” the statement said.
It added that if such conduct is repeated, those responsible would face “appropriate action against the perpetrators.”
The ministry also pointed to France’s adoption in 2024 of a law aimed at preventing foreign interference, based on claims contained in a French Senate investigative commission’s report, saying Paris is therefore clearly familiar with the principle of prohibiting foreign intervention.

articles.title: Summer campaign has led to capture of 19 settlements in southeast Ukraine, Russia says
articles.body:
Summer campaign has led to capture of 19 settlements in southeast Ukraine, Russia says
Aug 15 - Russian troops have taken control of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions over their summer campaign, the Russian defence ministry said on Saturday.
In a statement, the ministry cited a report by Pyotr Bolgarev, commander of the eastern group of forces. It did not name the settlements.
Separately, the ministry said its forces had recently taken control of the settlement of Rybalskoye in Zaporizhzhia region, news agency Interfax reported.
Reuters could not independently verify the battlefield reports.
Russian advances on the frontline have slowed this year even as Moscow has intensified its ballistic strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.
On Wednesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said his forces had recaptured 745 square km (288 square miles) of Russian-held land this year across the southeastern front. REUTERS

articles.title: US trains Taiwan Coast Guard as Chinese patrols increase
articles.body:
TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The US Coast Guard is training its Taiwan counterparts in small-boat operations, team coordination, and maritime patrols as Chinese vessels increase their activities around the nation, the Coast Guard Administration confirmed in a press release Friday.
The two-week course began Monday at the Coast Guard Training and Evaluation Center, in Taoyuan City’s Luzhu District, and is scheduled to continue through Aug. 21, the administration said. The program is focused on improving the nation’s maritime law-enforcement capabilities in complex operational environments.
The administration did not disclose the number of US instructors or Taiwanese personnel involved, citing operational considerations. The course includes vessel handling, emergency response and rescue procedures.
The training comes as China has expanded coast guard activity around Taiwan. Even so, the US training is publicly described as maritime law-enforcement cooperation, rather than a military exercise.
Furthermore, it is not a new initiative, as the US and Taiwan signed a memorandum of understanding in 2021 to strengthen cooperation between their coast guard agencies.

articles.title: First new N700ST high-speed train arrives in Taiwan from Japan
articles.body:
TAIPEI (Taiwan News) – The first N700ST high-speed train arrived in Kaohsiung on Saturday, on a ship from Japan.
Taiwan High Speed Rail Corporation ordered 12 sets of the train from Japan’s Hitachi Toshiba Supreme Consortium. The first train is expected to start service on July 1, 2027, with delivery of all trains scheduled for completion by the end of September 2028.
The departure of the first train from Japan had been scheduled for Aug. 6, but Typhoon Dolphin and Typhoon Chan-hom caused a delay until Tuesday, per Liberty Times. The disembarkation of the train set from the ship will take two days, to be followed by three nights of road transportation to the depot in the Kaohsiung district of Yanchao.
A wide range of safety tests will prepare the train for its inauguration next year. The first phase of tests inside the depot will take until November, the report said. The second phase will cover 69 items, including traction, braking, and general service, with completion expected in April 2027.
At the arrival ceremony in Kaohsiung Saturday, THSRC Chair Shih Che (史哲) said that following the launch of the first new train next year, the first fare increase in 20 years would come up for discussion.
Enhanced safety and comfort were preconditions for a change in fares, he said. Even if the company decided to hike fares, the increase would only take effect after all N700ST had started service in September 2028, Liberty Times reported.

articles.body:
Earthquake occurred in the Poltava region

articles.title: Ukrainian press gang conscripts Red Cross driver during evacuation (VIDEO)
articles.body:
Ukrainian press gang conscripts Red Cross driver during evacuation (VIDEO)
A Ukrainian Red Cross driver was detained by police and then conscripted while evacuating two vulnerable families from a dangerous area near the front line on Friday, the organization reported.
Kiev has increasingly relied on violently enforced mandatory conscription amid battlefield losses and Russian advances on the front lines. Reports and videos of what has now been sardonically dubbed ‘busification’ crop up almost daily, showing draft officers ambushing men in the streets and dragging them into vans, often brawling with relatives and passersby.
According to the Ukrainian Red Cross, one of its vehicles was stopped at a police checkpoint in the Nikolaev Region. A police officer took the driver into custody for a blood alcohol test but instead delivered him to a local branch of the Territorial Center of Recruitment and Social Support (TCK), the body tasked with overseeing Ukraine’s mobilization, the Red Cross said in an Instagram statement.
Nikolaev regional police said that it has launched an investigation into the incident but stressed that the driver had no draft exemption and was subject to conscription.
The incident has spurred a reaction from Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmitry Lubinets. “The law must be the same for everyone,” he wrote on Telegram, while stressing that it was “unacceptable” for state authorities to endanger civilian evacuations from high risk areas.
The incident came a day after the head of Nikolaev Region’s TCK was arrested on corruption charges. The official took bribes up to $10,000 per person to take men off the national conscription tracking register, Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko said in a statement on Thursday.
Kiev’s forced conscription campaign has led to escalating tensions within Ukrainian society. Many citizens see it as disproportionately targeting poor people, with richer Ukrainians can afford to bribe corrupt officials in order to dodge the draft.
Russia has long accused Kiev’s foreign backers of pushing it to fight “to the last Ukrainian” in what Moscow describes as a NATO-led proxy war using Ukraine’s population armed with Western weapons and technology.

articles.title: German citizens advised against travelling to Ukraine due to risk of increased attacks ahead of Independence Day
articles.body:
Travel to Ukraine is strictly advised against for German citizens due to the risk of Russian shelling ahead of Ukraine’s Independence Day and attacks on railway infrastructure and rolling stock, according to a statement published on the website of the German Federal Foreign Office.
"Military action continues in Ukraine. Russian airstrikes using missiles, cruise missiles, and drones are occurring almost daily; all parts of the country could be affected. In connection with Independence Day on August 24, 2026, increased attacks on both infrastructure (e.g., energy infrastructure, transport hubs) and civilian targets cannot be ruled out," according to updated travel recommendations for Ukraine published on the agency’s website. The report notes that transport in Ukraine is slowed due to damage and checkpoints, and entry and exit are only possible by land, as Ukrainian airspace is closed.
"All rail connections have been severely damaged by the conflict. Ukrainian rail infrastructure is the target of Russian airstrikes aimed at disrupting supply routes. This damage is usually promptly repaired, but significant delays in passenger rail travel are common. Travelers should be prepared for delays, especially in cold weather. In January 2026, a Ukrainian passenger train was attacked for the first time in the frontline zone of Kharkiv region," the German Federal Foreign Office notes.
Earlier, a warning about possible Russian strikes on railway facilities and trains ahead of Ukraine’s Independence Day was sent by mail and was later added to the general list of all warnings on the agency’s website. It is noted that the German Embassy currently provides only limited consular services, and its ability to support German citizens is currently very limited.
"If you need to travel to Ukraine for unavoidable business reasons, despite travel warnings, be aware of the significant risks and ensure you have a carefully and professionally developed security plan… Strictly observe any curfews imposed," the message reads.

articles.title: 100GW of nuclear power by 2047, 5 reactors this decade: Inside PM Modi's energy self-reliance plan
articles.body:
100GW of nuclear power by 2047, 5 reactors this decade: Inside PM Modi's energy self-reliance plan
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 15, 2026, 15:27 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
Target of 100 GW of nuclear energy by 2047, 5 new nuclear reactors to be operational within 6-7 years: PM Modi
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced an expansion of India's ambitious nuclear power programme, setting a target of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047.PM Modi said five new nuclear reactors would be operationalised during this decade as the country seeks greater energy security and self-reliance.Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India had taken an important step towards self-reliance in nuclear energy with the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu attaining first criticality in April this year.PM Modi said nuclear power would be an important component of India's energy security as demand for electricity rises with the expansion of technologies such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence and data centres. He also referred to the government's nuclear policy reforms and the SHANTI Act, enacted in December 2025, as part of efforts to expand the sector.“The new world cannot run without energy. Whether they are (semiconductor) chips, AI or data centres, the country needs lots of electricity … That’s why we have already taken strong steps to ensure energy security,” he added.
PM Modi said India had set the goal of reaching 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, with five new reactors expected to become operational in the current decade.
India enters second stage of three-stage nuclear programme
The PFBR at Kalpakkam marks India's entry into the second stage of its three-stage nuclear power programme, originally conceived by Homi J Bhabha.The 500 MWe reactor, developed and built indigenously at the Kalpakkam Nuclear Complex, attained first criticality on April 6, 2026. It is being built by Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited, or BHAVINI, under the Department of Atomic Energy, with technology developed by the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research.The first stage of India's nuclear programme relies on Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors, or PHWRs, which use natural uranium as fuel and produce plutonium as a byproduct.The second stage uses this plutonium in fast breeder reactors. The PFBR uses uranium-plutonium mixed oxide, or MOX, fuel and is designed to produce more fissile material than it consumes.The third stage of the programme is aimed at using India's large thorium reserves to produce uranium-233 for nuclear power generation.The PFBR is therefore intended to serve as a bridge between India's existing uranium-based nuclear programme and its longer-term thorium-based energy strategy.
Why PFBR matters for India's nuclear expansion
The PFBR is a 500 MWe sodium-cooled fast breeder reactor designed to use plutonium-based fuel while breeding additional fissile material.A blanket of uranium-238 around the reactor core can be converted into plutonium-239 through the action of fast neutrons. This allows the reactor to generate electricity while producing additional fuel.The reactor's technology is particularly relevant to India's nuclear strategy because the country has relatively limited uranium resources but substantial thorium reserves.The Department of Atomic Energy has said the PFBR will eventually help lay the foundation for the third stage of India's nuclear programme, in which thorium would be used to produce uranium-233.PM Modi had earlier described the PFBR milestone as a major development in India's civil nuclear programme.“Today, India takes a defining step in its civil nuclear journey, advancing the second stage of its nuclear programme.”PM Modi had also said, “This advanced reactor, capable of producing more fuel than it consumes, reflects the depth of our scientific capability and the strength of our engineering enterprise. It is a decisive step towards harnessing our vast thorium reserves in the third stage of the programme.”
Nuclear power seen as key to meeting rising electricity demand
In his Independence Day address, PM Modi linked India's nuclear expansion with the country's rapidly increasing demand for electricity.He pointed to the growing power requirements of semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence and data centres, saying energy security would become increasingly important as India expands its technology and manufacturing sectors.“It is difficult to build a new world. That is why, whether it is a chip, AI, or data centre, we need electricity in large quantity. The new era demands energy.”PM Modi said India had taken steps to strengthen energy security by expanding both nuclear and renewable energy capacity.He said nuclear energy was vital for ensuring a stable supply of electricity while the country simultaneously expands solar, wind and other renewable sources.
India targets 500 GW renewable energy by 2030
Alongside the nuclear expansion, PM Modi highlighted the growth of India's renewable energy capacity.He said India's solar energy capacity had risen from 2 GW in 2014 to 160 GW, while the country had set a target of 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.PM Modi also referred to the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, saying around 50 lakh households had been covered under the rooftop solar programme.Thousands of consumers, he said, were also earning through electricity generated from rooftop solar systems.Beneficiaries under the scheme can receive a subsidy of up to Rs 80,000 per household for installing rooftop solar systems.PM Modi also said India's railway electrification had expanded sharply, helping reduce diesel consumption and imports.He said India had also started work on a hydrogen train as part of its broader clean-energy transition.
SHANTI Act seeks to reshape India's nuclear power framework
PM Modi also referred to the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India, or SHANTI Act, enacted in December 2025.The legislation is intended to modernise India's nuclear legal framework and facilitate greater participation in the nuclear sector under regulatory oversight.The law forms part of the government's broader effort to expand nuclear power capacity and bring new investment and technology into the sector.The Union Budget 2025-26 had also announced a Nuclear Energy Mission with an allocation of Rs 20,000 crore for the design, development and deployment of Small Modular Reactors.The government has set a target of having at least five indigenously designed small modular reactors operational by 2033.
India’s nuclear capacity to expand from 8.78 GW
India's installed nuclear power capacity currently stands at around 8.78 GW, according to government data.Nuclear power accounted for about 3.1% of India's electricity generation in 2024-25, when nuclear plants generated 56,681 million units of electricity.The government has projected that India's nuclear capacity could reach around 22.38 GW by 2031-32 through the development of indigenous 700 MW reactors and larger reactors being developed through international cooperation.The 100 GW target by 2047 would therefore require a substantial expansion in both the number and scale of nuclear power projects over the next two decades.
Five reactors to be operationalised this decade
PM Modi said India would operationalise five nuclear reactors during the current decade as part of its push towards greater nuclear capacity.The expansion is expected to involve multiple reactor technologies, including India's indigenous PHWR designs and advanced reactor technologies.The government is also developing small modular reactor designs, including the 200 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor and the 55 MWe SMR-55, as well as other advanced reactor concepts.The expansion is aimed at increasing the contribution of nuclear energy to India's electricity mix while maintaining the country's broader clean-energy and net-zero commitments.
The expansion of nuclear power is also linked to India's commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2070.Unlike solar and wind power, nuclear reactors can provide continuous electricity and are not dependent on weather conditions. This makes nuclear generation a potential source of firm, low-carbon electricity alongside renewable energy.The government has therefore positioned nuclear power as part of a wider energy mix that includes solar, wind, hydrogen and other clean-energy sources.PM Modi's announcement of the 100 GW target marks a substantial increase in India's long-term nuclear ambitions and places nuclear power at the centre of the country's energy security strategy as it works towards the Viksit Bharat 2047 goal.

articles.title: Iran Rejects US Talks Resumption, Cites Violated Peace Agreement
articles.body:
Iran has not made a decision to resume negotiations with the US, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated, and as reported by the Mehr agency.
Araghchi indicated that the US violated the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, which he said was intended to conclude the conflict rather than serve as a temporary pause in fighting.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“We did not have a ceasefire to extend; we had an end to the war, which has now entered a new situation,” Araghchi said.
He acknowledged that Qatar and Pakistan are exchanging messages as mediators and remain in contact with Tehran, but he emphasized that this does not constitute formal negotiations.
Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi reported ongoing technical discussions with Oman focused on establishing new maritime routes for vessel traffic.
He stated that previous routes are no longer operational and a temporary path is currently being designed by specialists and armed forces representatives.
Araghchi specified that these technical talks are separate from any decision to reopen the strait to general transit.
“Whether the Strait of Hormuz reopens or not depends on the fulfilment of other conditions to which America must adhere,” he stated.
Strait of Hormuz blockade and US position
On Aug. 14, US President Donald Trump announced intentions to declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory following the conclusion of the military conflict with Iran. Speaking at the David S. Mack Training and Intelligence Center, Trump stated the US currently maintains a blockade of the waterway.
US Backs Japan After Putin’s Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands
Commercial traffic through the strait largely ceased on Aug. 14 following attacks on two additional vessels. The US government indicated it is prepared to maintain the maritime blockade indefinitely.
An Iranian source stated that previous negotiations to extend a June ceasefire agreement yielded no results. Following the breakdown of that ceasefire, Iran resumed attacks on vessels it claims are attempting to navigate the strait without authorization from Tehran.
Prior to this, on Aug. 2, Trump announced a temporary suspension of planned US military strikes to allow for diplomatic negotiations, stipulating the immediate opening of the strait as a primary condition for any agreement.

articles.title: Ukraine's General Staff confirms strikes on Progress rocket and space centre and Savasleika airfield
articles.body:
Ukraine's General Staff confirms strikes on Progress rocket and space centre and Savasleika airfield
Ukraine's defence forces struck the Rocket and Space Centre Progress in Samara and the Savasleika airfield in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod Oblast on the night of 14-15 August. Fires broke out at both facilities following the strikes.
Source: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
Details: The General Staff reported that Rocket and Space Centre Progress is one of the key enterprises in Russia's rocket and space industry, manufacturing Soyuz-family launch vehicles.
These are used to launch Russian military, reconnaissance and communications satellites. In particular, the Soyuz-2.1b is used to deploy the Rassvet satellite constellation, which Russia positions as an answer to Starlink.
The plant also produces Earth remote sensing satellites, which, according to the General Staff, Russia uses for reconnaissance.
Ukraine's defence forces also struck the Savasleika airfield, where a fire was also recorded.
The airfield is used, in particular, as a base for MiG-31K interceptor aircraft capable of carrying Kinzhal aeroballistic missiles.
Background: Explosions and strikes were reported in the Russian city of Samara following an attack, with the Rocket and Space Centre Progress potentially among the targets.

articles.title: Modi rolls out free coaching drive to win over young Indians
articles.body:
Modi rolls out free coaching drive to win over young Indians
Prime Minister Narendra Modi made an overture to win over India’s youth on Saturday, as he led 80th Independence Day celebrations of the world’s largest democracy. 
Addressing the nation after hoisting the national flag at the historic Red Fort in Delhi, he noted that the “biggest beneficiaries” of India’s development will be the youth. 
Modi announced that his government would set up free online coaching networks for various competitive examinations, leveraging India’s robust digital public infrastructure and freeing families from the heavy financial burden they incur from sending their children to private coaching institutes.
The government will also train 11 million young people in artificial intelligence skills to prepare them for the new jobs that are opening up.
India, the world’s most populous nation with 1.4 billion people, also has the world’s largest youth population, with the average age around 29.
#WATCH | Delhi: From the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, "The race for coaching classes has become a massive burden for our middle-class families. Every parent feels that if they don't send their child to a coaching class, they aren't considered a… pic.twitter.com/Qq74edZTl2
— ANI (@ANI) August 15, 2026
The country recently saw widespread youth protests over the leaks of the questions for a national medical entrance test, ultimately forcing the then federal education minister to resign. The fiasco, and the police violence against the protesting students in the national capital and other cities, stoked anger in the country, especially among the middle class.
Modi earlier announced a panel of experts to suggest reforms in the conduct of competitive exams, and pushed through a law mandating stricter punishment for those who tamper with exam integrity.
The prime minister’s online coaching initiative would be a blow to the country’s thriving private coaching networks, some of which have been blamed for the exam scams in recent years. The industry is valued at up to $15 billion.
India achieved independence from British rule on August 15, 1947 through largely non-violent means. Most of Britain’s other colonial possessions and those of other European powers would follow suit in the coming decades.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke speaks to the media alongside CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das and national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka (ANI)
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Saturday announced its plans to launch a statewide campaign to assess the condition of public hospitals in Maharashtra. articles.title: Puerto Rico Is Rationing Water. It Could’ve Avoided It by Harvesting Rainwater
articles.body:
Puerto Rico is experiencing a historic drought that’s led to water rationing following the driest month on record in July.
Yet one ready-made solution is barely being tapped: the normally copious rainfall. Anywhere from 30 to 169 inches of precipitation falls on the territory annually, but the government doesn't require US citizens in Puerto Rico to install catchment systems to take advantage of the free resource—unlike some other island states. As climate change increases the odds of more intense droughts on the island, that type of decentralized infrastructure may be just what Puerto Ricans need in an emergency.
“One of the best unused reservoirs of water in Puerto Rico are the roofs of the houses,” says Fernando Abruña, a partner at local firm Abruña & Musgrave Architects.
The drought has exacerbated a water crisis that was already in motion due to ruptured water pipes and other decrepit infrastructure. For the past week, Puerto Rico governor Jenniffer González has ordered municipal governments to shut off water two days at a time for people in the northeast to conserve local supplies, leaving 180,000 households with limited access. The problems began well before that, though: Many families have been without consistent water for more than 100 days.
While the drought is a factor, the biggest issue isn’t a lack of water, says environmental lawyer Ruth Santiago, but rather the government’s mismanagement of it.
“Even with the climate crisis and these droughts, we still have abundant water,” says Santiago, who works with the local group Comité Diálogo Ambiental (the Environmental Dialogue Committee). “We could be harvesting rainwater right now,” she says as a storm erupts mid-conversation.
The most resilient harvesting systems rely on gravity, using gutters to divert rainwater from a roof to a canister that connects to indoor pipes like a faucet or showerhead. Bigger systems can help collect water to cool power plants and other industrial uses.
Abruña, who is also a fellow with the American Institute of Architects, estimates the island could gather 30 billion gallons of water a year if just 1 million households used rainwater collection technology. The average resident uses 62 gallons a day, amounting to just over 72 billion gallons of residential water use a year.
The Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority loses about 60 percent of the island’s drinking water before any arrives at customers’ homes due to leaking pipes and failing infrastructure. The ongoing emergency was caused, in part, by a series of ruptures in the 72-inch Superaqueduct water pipe, a main artery that services major cities on the northern coast. Repairing and updating the island’s aging water distribution system is most urgent, Santiago says, but rainwater harvesting is a cost-effective solution that can be quickly implemented.
The practice is not widespread in Puerto Rico, where the government has prioritized centralized grids fed by freshwater, but these systems are popular in other island communities. Roughly 90 percent of homes in the US Virgin Islands have a cistern to collect rainwater, and the territory has building codes that require many new developments to include this infrastructure. (Barbados has similar codes.) In Hawaii, Honolulu County even offers a limited number of free rain barrel installations to residents.
“There is nothing that can help the Caribbean region as quickly and as reliably as rainwater harvesting,” says Farah Nibbs, an assistant professor at the University of Maryland Baltimore County’s Department of Emergency and Disaster Health Systems, noting governments should treat it “as part of the national water supply.”
She also says governments should help cover the costs to avoid putting onerous “economic and financial burdens on households.” Yet in Puerto Rico, the government offers no incentives or financial assistance. That’s left small organizations attempting to meet demand.
Since 2010, local environmental nonprofit Plenitud Puerto Rico has donated and installed 73 rainwater harvesting systems for neighbors in Las Marías, a mountainous municipality on the western side of Puerto Rico. Executive codirector Owen Ingley estimates that the technology costs the group $500 to $2,000 for small, simple units and up to $5,000 for larger, more advanced ones with electric pumps. There are also additional costs to maintain the system, especially if a bad storm damages it, and to monitor water quality.
The team recently installed a unit for a man in his eighties who lives alone and regularly experiences disruptions to his water supply. The system doesn’t provide drinking water, but it helps him meet other household needs such as flushing the toilet or filling his dog’s water bowl. “He’s a really sweet and talkative guy with gray hair and a big smile,” Ingley says.
José Pérez Cordero, an at-large legislator in the Puerto Rico House of Representatives, introduced a resolution in June that would order the Puerto Rican Natural Resources Committee to conduct a feasibility study on rainwater harvesting. That would include looking at how other Caribbean islands have made it work and adopting similar models for Puerto Rico. The proposal has gone nowhere, even as water insecurity mounts.
“We are, right now, in the perfect moment to do it, because we are in the middle of a crisis,” Pérez Cordero says. “Sadly, we always wait for the reaction.”
He points to a 2024 law that mandated all public agencies to implement rainwater collection systems on government buildings. That, too, has gone nowhere: Agencies aren’t following the law, nor is it being enforced. Pérez Cordero’s New Progressive Party is in power, but he says his peers have often lacked the political will to be proactive and prioritize the environment.
Rainwater harvesting won’t solve all of Puerto Rico’s water problems, particularly in urban locations where it’s hard to install them in large apartment complexes. They also aren’t sustainable if the wet season isn’t rainy enough—a prospect that’s likely to increase as burning fossil fuels heats up the planet. But that doesn’t mean they can’t play a role in shoring up a dysfunctional system.
“Facing climate change, every year is going to be harder,” Pérez Cordero says. “Every year, the dry season is going to be longer. Every year, the rainy season is going to be harder too.”

articles.title: Parmelin defends government support for Swiss farmers amid drought
articles.body:
Parmelin defends government support for Swiss farmers amid drought
With drought-related losses in agriculture expected to reach record levels, Swiss Agriculture Minister Guy Parmelin has defended the government's response. He argues that existing laws provide sufficient tools to support farmers and that there is no need to declare a state of emergency.
Harvests of crops in Switzerland including potatoes, sugar beet and maize are expected to be poor, while livestock farmers face shortages of fodder. The drought is adding to pressures already weighing on the sector and could lead to higher food prices.
Speaking to Swiss public radio RTS on Friday, on the sidelines of the inauguration of a new Agroscope building in Posieux, canton Fribourg, Parmelin said the government had been preparing measures since June.
“We have put in place everything possible under current legislation to ease the burden on farmers,” he said, warning that many would face liquidity problems.
“We have abolished customs duties on hay and fodder imports,” and then on corn starting Saturday. He also pointed to “interest-free loans and accelerating direct payments to help farmers get through this difficult period”.
More
Swiss farmers fear worse drought losses than 2003
Importing fodder
Importing animal feed is “one of the concerns,” said Parmelin as drought conditions are affecting all of Europe. He added: “We’ll have to see how we can bridge the gap until winter and, above all, hope that the situation improves and that we don’t have a dry winter; otherwise, we risk having even bigger problems next spring.”
But there is no question of declaring a state of emergency, because “the situation can be managed within the current legal framework. Which doesn’t mean we’re doing nothing.” He highlighted the army’s efforts to supply water to Alpine pastures in canton Fribourg.
More
Swiss farmers call for financial support during drought
A strategy for water
Looking ahead, the minister said water management would be a key challenge for Swiss agriculture in the coming years. He underlined that infrastructure support has already been developed and will be further expanded. “There is a whole water strategy that has been in preparation for some time now by my colleague [Environment Minister Albert] Rösti.
Parmelin also highlighted the need to modernise ageing water supply networks and stressed that water policy should take a holistic approach rather than prioritising any single sector.
+ Swiss agriculture adapts to climate change
“We’ve been seeing this climate change for several years now,” he said. As a former winegrower, he noted that grape varieties such as Merlot and Malbec can now be grown in parts of the country. articles.title: Ukraine strikes key Roscosmos facility with Flamingo missiles

Ukraine strikes key Roscosmos facility with Flamingo missiles
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced this on Telegram, according to Ukrinform.
“Today we have new significant results from our precision strikes. In Russia’s Samara region, one of Roscosmos’s key facilities—the Progress Center, which was involved, among other things, in the production of electronics—has been struck. ‘Flamingo’ missiles were used; this is a great achievement. The distance from our border is about 900 kilometers,” the head of state said.
Zelensky also added that Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” reached the “Savasleika” airfield, where Russian missile launchers based there are used to strike cities and villages in Ukraine.
“This is about 700 kilometers from Ukraine. We have also confirmed the damage we needed to inflict on an oil facility in the town of Ust-Luga. The distance is over 800 kilometers from our border,” Zelensky noted.
The head of state thanked all the units involved for their precision.
“Our plan for ‘long-range sanctions’ against Russia for this war is being carried out, and it is important that Russia’s war potential be reduced. Peace is needed, and this must be visible in Russia—through concrete damage to specific targets,” he emphasized.
As reported by Ukrinform, the General Staff confirmed the strike on a production complex belonging to the gas company “Novatek” in the Leningrad region.

articles.title: Zelensky Confirms Flamingo Missile Strikes Deep in Russian Territory
articles.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Saturday, Aug. 15, that Ukrainian forces executed long-range strikes targeting strategic facilities in Russia, including the use of “Flamingo“ missiles against an aerospace plant in the Samara region.
In a statement on Telegram, Zelensky detailed the outcomes of what he termed deep strikes into Russian territory.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
He confirmed that the Progress Space Rocket Centre, a key enterprise within the Russian state corporation Roscosmos involved in electronics production, was struck in the Samara region.
Zelensky explicitly stated that “Flamingo” missiles were utilized for this attack, noting the facility is located approximately 900 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.
The president also reported that long-range weapons struck the Savasleyka airfield in the Nizhny Novgorod region. He specified that the base, situated roughly 700 kilometers from Ukraine, hosts aircraft used as carriers for Russian missiles targeting Ukrainian cities and villages.
Furthermore, Zelensky confirmed an attack on an oil facility in the port of Ust-Luga in the Leningrad region, located over 800 kilometers from the border, stating that the necessary damage to the target was recorded.
According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the “Progress” Rocket and Space Center in Samara. A direct hit on the target was confirmed, followed by a fire on the facility’s grounds.
Romania Reports Fourth Discovery of Drone Debris in 24 Hours
The “Progress” Rocket and Space Center is one of the key enterprises in the Russian Federation’s rocket and space industry, producing launch vehicles of the “Soyuz” family. These are used to launch Russian spacecraft for military, reconnaissance, and communications purposes into orbit.
In particular, the “Soyuz-2.1b” is used to deploy the Russian “Rassvet” satellite constellation – a broadband satellite communications system that Russia positions as an analogue to Starlink.
The Progress Rocket and Space Center also manufactures Earth observation satellites, which the enemy uses for reconnaissance purposes.
The extent of the damage is being assessed.
In addition, the Savasleika airfield in the Nizhny Novgorod region of the Russian Federation was struck. A direct hit on the target was recorded, followed by a fire on the airfield grounds.
“Savasleika” is used, in particular, to base and deploy MiG-31K interceptor fighters – carriers of the Kh-47M2 “Kinzhal” aeroballistic missiles.
Prior reports of Samara aerospace plant strikes
The presidential confirmation followed reports from earlier on Saturday regarding explosions at industrial aerospace enterprises in Samara.
Following the initial blasts, Denis Shtilerman, chief designer at the Ukrainian defense company Fire Point, published footage depicting the launch of an FP-5 “Flamingo” missile.
Samara region Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev reported a missile strike on an unnamed industrial facility, while Mayor Ivan Noskov stated that the city’s industrial infrastructure sustained localized damage.
Open-source intelligence analysts reviewing images of the site identified the location as the shared industrial zone of the Aviakor aviation plant and the Progress Space Rocket Centre. Progress manufactures Soyuz-2 carrier rockets and space satellites, while Aviakor produces and maintains aircraft.
Concurrent drone activity in Crimea
The strikes on Russian territory coincided with reports of drone activity in occupied Crimea on Saturday morning.
Local residents reported explosions in Sevastopol and the Bakhchysarai district. Following the blasts, local Telegram channels reported power outages in Sevastopol and a fire in the Balaklava area.
Russian occupation authorities did not issue an immediate statement regarding the incidents.

articles.title: Ukrainian arms manufacturers warned of the risk of disruptions to supplies to the front and proposed solutions
articles.body:
Ukrainian arms manufacturers warned of the risk of disruptions to supplies to the front and proposed solutions
Kyiv • UNN
The Ukrainian Council of Arms Manufacturers stated that contracting is insufficient due to the slow development of technical and tactical specifications, which could cause delays in weapons deliveries. Manufacturers forecast a real supply gap in six months if processes are not accelerated.
The new defense procurement model could cause a pause in the supply of weapons to the front. The Ukrainian Council of Arms Manufacturers issued a statement about the insufficient level of contracting in the domestic arms market, all because of the almost complete halt in the procurement of Ukrainian weapons, UNN writes.
What the Council of Arms Manufacturers says
The statement by the Ukrainian Council of Arms Manufacturers emphasizes the conflict between the pace of procurement reform and the pace of the war:
"The Council of Arms Manufacturers supports competitive and transparent procurement. But any model must operate at the pace of war. There is time between the decision to procure and the actual delivery for procedures, the procurement of components, production, testing, and acceptance. Therefore, a delay in contracting today means the risk of a supply gap in several months."
The reason for the statement was the new defense procurement model, which envisages a transition from direct contracts to competitive tender procedures.
How the new competitive procurement model is supposed to work
The model that the Ministry of Defense officially began implementing at the beginning of this year is based on competence centers established under the Ministry of Defense. One of the tasks of these centers is to formulate the relevant tactical and technical specifications (TTS) for products. These TTS are the basis for conducting procurements of specific weapons systems, and without them the Defense Procurement Agency cannot announce a tender.
And this is where a failure occurred — in the five months since the process of transitioning to competitive procurement began, the competence centers have managed to develop TTS for an extremely small number of items.
"More than five months have passed since then, yet a critically insufficient number of TTS have still been developed for the existing nomenclature," explained Ihor Fedirko, executive director of the Ukrainian Council of Arms Manufacturers.
In July, the Defense Procurement Agency reported the announcement of the first tenders for the procurement of FPV drones according to TTS worth more than UAH 3.3 billion. The Agency reported that since then it has announced and conducted procedures in all categories for which TTS had been received.
At the same time, funding for the old direct procurement procedures is extremely limited — the main funds have already been allocated to procurement through competitive tender procedures, the implementation of which arms manufacturers generally support.
"This is a transparent approach that corresponds to European practice and one toward which we genuinely need to move," Fedirko emphasized.
What risks this poses for the front
As stated by the association of arms manufacturers Technological Forces of Ukraine:
"The potential shortage of contracting for weapons and military equipment for the Defense Forces of Ukraine, which key stakeholders are currently discussing, could call into question both the army's ability to conduct active combat on the front and the capacity of enterprises in the national defense industry to operate systematically."
In simple terms, the procurement of weapons has stopped, and the military will not be able to receive what it needs on time. Even if the TTS are transferred to the Defense Procurement Agency in the near future and the Agency launches tender procedures within a short timeframe, a pause in supplies is almost inevitable.
"The price of this pause is weapons that the front may not receive," Fedirko believes.
According to him, in six months there is a real threat of a disruption in supplies to the front: "This is already a question of what the Ukrainian army will fight with six months from now."
Even if all processes can be launched tomorrow, apart from the tender procedure itself, there is a certain production cycle: after contracting, the manufacturer must receive advance funding, then purchase components (the delivery of which for some items may take up to three months), and only then manufacture the product.
"Several more months are needed for production, testing, and the transfer of finished products. Therefore, a pause in contracting today means the risk of an actual disruption in supplies in six months," Fedirko says.
Most manufacturers today have contracts covering only 15–25% of their capacity. The market forecasts that supplies of the volumes of weapons that should have been contracted through procurements that have not yet been announced will begin no earlier than December 2026, and possibly as late as March 2027.
Other complications
Against the backdrop of the pause in tenders, the situation has also become more complicated with the alternative supply channel — the digital DOT-Chain Defence platform, through which military units directly ordered drones, ammunition, electronic warfare equipment, and robotic systems from manufacturers’ warehouses in a matter of weeks rather than quarters. Funding for procurement through this platform is currently limited.
The fact that the Defense Ministry’s pilot project, launched in parallel under the name “Basic Level,” is also adding to the problems. Under the project, units were supposed to be supplied continuously with a minimum predictable level of UAVs, unmanned ground systems, and other systems, but it has not yet demonstrated its effectiveness.
Manufacturers emphasize that the coincidence of the pause in tenders and disruptions in funding for DOT-Chain Defence is particularly dangerous because Ukrainian weapons have only now begun to give the front a tangible advantage for the first time — long-range systems are striking the enemy’s logistics, while drone units are holding back infantry assaults. In the industry’s view, halting production at this particular moment threatens not only the loss of this advantage but also far broader consequences for the country’s defense capability.
Long-term consequences for the industry
Manufacturers have other concerns as well. Companies that expanded production, hired people, relocated enterprises, and ordered components at their own expense during the full-scale invasion risk being left without domestic orders for months.
“No exports are currently capable of replacing state defense orders for Ukrainian manufacturers. Foreign contracts can support the development of the industry, but they will not utilize all the capacity that has been created or ensure the production volumes required by the Defense Forces,” Fedirko says.
In addition to the reduction in production capacity, modernization is also at risk: manufacturers will be unable to upgrade existing weapons systems and develop new ones. This is critical because certain types of weapons become obsolete within a few weeks and require continuous improvement.
What manufacturers propose
One option for mitigating the crisis mentioned in the market is to restore broad funding for direct procurement through the DOT Chain Defence mechanism. Only verified manufacturers are connected to this platform, while units can choose weapons according to their own needs. The mechanism has already proven effective and, in the industry’s view, is capable of mitigating the shortcomings of the transition period.
Other proposals include:
-  promptly reallocating funds to finance critical needs; 
-  reformatting and strengthening centers of expertise where necessary; 
-  establishing clear deadlines and assigning responsibility for developing technical and tactical characteristics; 
-  accelerating the announcement of procurements based on specifications that are already prepared; 
-  introducing a transitional mechanism until the new model is fully launched. 
The industry emphasizes that, regardless of which procurement mechanism the state ultimately uses, it must meet two basic criteria — supplying the front with weapons on time and guaranteeing uninterrupted production at Ukrainian enterprises. Market participants call everything else merely a form that can be improved without limitation, whereas, in their view, these two criteria cannot be sacrificed.
Manufacturers separately draw attention to the personnel aspect of the problem. In their view, the defense procurement system cannot depend on personnel decisions: a change of minister should not halt contracts that have already been concluded, and discussions about a possible replacement of the head of the Defense Procurement Agency should not slow down the conduct of tenders. If every personnel rotation leads to a pause in supplies, this, the industry believes, indicates not the existence of a system but manual management of the process.
Against this backdrop, market participants do not rule out that some of the public pressure on the head of the Defense Procurement Agency, Arsen Zhumadilov, is an attempt to shift responsibility onto the executor — whereas the DPA objectively cannot announce tenders without the technical and tactical characteristics that were not provided to it, or contract resources that were not allocated to it. Therefore, market participants urge that the problem not be politicized and that the chair under the head of the DPA not be destabilized; instead, they call for procedural decisions that would enable the agency to conduct procurements as quickly as possible and contract the maximum number of manufacturers.

articles.title: Iran tells US to ‘accept defeat’ amid Strait of Hormuz blockade
articles.body:
Iran called on the United States to accept defeat Saturday as President Donald Trump described Tehran as “very evil” and warned Americans to brace for continued high fuel prices as the war drags on.
Progress toward peace talks and the resumption of oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz remained stalled, with no clear indication that either side was moving toward ending the conflict launched by the U.S. and Israel on Feb. 28.
“This strait will be opened and closed only under Iran’s command, and so long as you do not accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in fantasies, Iran will continue to enforce the blockade,” Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a post on X early Saturday.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran had not decided whether to resume negotiations with Washington.
In an interview with Iranian news outlet Shahrara News published Saturday, he said the U.S. would have to meet Iran’s conditions regarding the Strait of Hormuz before shipping could resume through the vital waterway, which handled about one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies before the war.
Trump, meanwhile, urged Americans to accept higher gasoline prices as the conflict continues, warning that the disruption caused by the war could keep fuel costs elevated.
He told a political rally in Garden City, New York, on Friday that paying “a tiny little bit more for your gasoline” was worth the cost of ensuring “a very evil country” could not have a nuclear weapon, one of the president’s stated rationales for the war.
In a trend that has fueled inflation and disappointed voters, the average U.S. price of a gallon of gasoline was about $4.08 on Friday, up 29% from a year earlier, according to the American Automobile Association.
Trump, a Republican, campaigned for reelection on a promise to lower energy costs, and Democrats are seeking to make the war’s fallout an issue in November’s congressional elections.
Crude oil futures rose $1 a barrel Friday. Benchmark Brent futures were on track for a weekly gain of 6%, while West Texas Intermediate was up 5.4%.
“The Strait of Hormuz cannot be seized by a tweet or an aircraft carrier, by issuing an order or by delivering an election speech,” Gharibabadi said.
Despite Iran’s defiant tone, though, there were signs of an economic toll there as well.
President Masoud Pezeshkian, in remarks on state television, blamed high inflation on a U.S. blockade of Iranian ports and sanctions on Iran’s oil exports.
Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent each pledged to inflict more financial damage on Iran. Bessent told Newsmax’s “Rob Schmitt Tonight” program Thursday that announcements of additional measures against Iran were coming next week.
Tehran calls its enforcement of strait traffic a blockade, the term Washington uses for its threat against Iranian vessels leaving their ports.
“What we’re doing is a great service for the world, not only for ourselves ... and we’re really doing a great job,” Trump said, adding that a 260-day deployment by a U.S. aircraft carrier supporting the war effort was “not nearly long enough.”
Only two vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz Friday, with no crude oil shipments visible, according to an analysis by ship-tracking firm Kpler. Some ships may cross the strait undetected with their transponders turned off, but the figures are nowhere near the more than 130 ships that traversed it daily before the war.
Vessels that navigate the strait without Iranian permission risk missile or drone strikes. The United Arab Emirates’ Abu Dhabi National Oil Company said two of its vessels were attacked while transiting the strait Thursday evening, and the Emirati state news agency WAM reported that another vessel came under attack Friday.
A bulk carrier was struck in the hull by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre said Saturday, adding that the crew was safe, no damage assessment had been reported and the environmental impact was unknown.
A tentative June deal to end the war is in tatters.
“We did not have a ceasefire in the first place that we would now want to extend,” Araqchi said. “We had ‘the end of the war,’ and now there is a new situation.”
Attacks by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen renewed concerns about a widening regional war. Yemen’s internationally recognized government said the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha on Friday, killing four civilians.
The Houthi-run SABA news agency cited a military source as saying the group had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi city of Najran with a drone.

articles.title: Iran fires back at Trump’s threat to declare Hormuz a US territory
articles.body:
Iran fires back at Trump’s threat to declare Hormuz a US territory
- Iran insists the Strait of Hormuz remains under its control and rejects US President Trump's claim to declare it US territory.
- Attacks on vessels linked to the UAE highlight ongoing tensions and risks to regional shipping in the strait.
- Diplomatic efforts falter as Iran demands sanctions relief and compensation before reopening the strait, while US maintains a blockade on Iranian ports.
AI generated
TEHRAN - Iran on Aug 15 fired back at US President Donald Trump’s claim that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz part of US territory, saying the crucial energy waterway it has blockaded “will remain Iranian”.
Trump has repeatedly said the strait, which Tehran effectively closed at the start of the Middle East war in late February, is under US control – an assertion the Islamic republic denies.
“The Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian,” Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on X.
“This strait will only be closed and opened under Iran’s command.”
Trump told a political rally in New York state on Aug 14 that after the US defeats Iran, “pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States”.
“It’s true,” he added.
An unnamed White House official later clarified that Trump was joking, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Last week, a top Iranian official laid out a laundry list of conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to the “war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq”.
Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr also demanded the end of crippling sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage.
As diplomacy stalls between the decades-long foes, attacks in the Hormuz strait have continued, highlighting the continued risks to regional shipping.
United Arab Emirates’ state-owned oil giant ADNOC said on Aug 15 one of its vessels came under attack the night before.
On Aug 14, the Gulf nation blamed Iran for other attacks on two vessels linked to ADNOC as they passed through the strait.
Such attacks led to the collapse of an April ceasefire between the United States and Iran.
As Iran throttles traffic in Hormuz, its Houthi allies in Yemen have also declared a parallel maritime blockade on Saudi ports in the Red Sea, the oil-exporting giant’s only other maritime route.
A June deal between Washington and Tehran – meant to serve as a jumping-off point for negotiations on a permanent settlement – had said Iran and Oman would hash out future arrangements for the strait in discussion with other Gulf countries and “in line with the applicable international law”.
Before the war, Hormuz carried around a fifth of the world’s oil and LNG exports, and prices have repeatedly surged since the dispute over the waterway erupted, piling economic and political pressure on Washington.
Iran wants to control the strait and charge tolls, powers it did not exercise before the war and a development that the US would fiercely oppose.
The closure of Hormuz has driven up prices for American voters, creating a political headache for Trump as November’s midterm elections near.
US vice-president J.D. Vance said this week that Washington’s top priority in the Iran war was keeping energy prices low for Americans, with preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon ranking second.
Tehran signalled last week that it had agreed with Oman a route for ships to transit the strait and were finalising arrangements to jointly manage the waterway.
The US has imposed its own retaliatory blockade of Iranian ports in an attempt to cripple its economy.
“We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to,” Trump said to a cheering crowd of supporters on Aug 14. AFP

articles.title: Macao's MICE participants rise 16 pct in H1 2026
articles.body:
MACAO, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- The number of participants and attendees at meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) events in Macao rose 16.0 percent year-on-year to 494,000 in the first half of 2026, according to the Statistics and Census Service (DSEC) on Friday.
A total of 918 MICE events were held during the period, broadly unchanged from a year earlier, while MICE-driven receipts of the non-gaming industries increased 44.8 percent year-on-year to about 2.43 billion patacas (about 301 million U.S. dollars).
In the second quarter, 499 MICE events were held, unchanged from a year earlier, with participants and attendees surging 37.6 percent to 314,000, the DSEC said.
MICE-driven receipts in the non-gaming industries reached 1.59 billion patacas in the second quarter, up 54.8 percent year-on-year, driven by more non-local participants and attendees and higher per-capita spending by MICE visitors. ■
