articles.title: Istanbul office rents reach record high in post-pandemic rebound
articles.body:
Prime office rents in Istanbul climbed to a record 52 dollars per square meter per month in the second quarter of 2026, up 13 percent from a year earlier in dollar terms, according to a new report.
Cushman & Wakefield TR International’s Türkiye MarketBeat Half Year 2026 report attributed the rise to limited prime office supply, low vacancy rates in the central business district and sustained demand for well-connected, high-quality buildings.
In lira terms, prime rents reached 2,359 liras per square meter per month, an annual increase of 32.6 percent.
Levent-Etiler recorded the highest rate at 52 dollars, followed by Maslak at 40 dollars.
Prime rents stood at 35 dollars in Esentepe-Gayrettepe-Zincirlikuyu and on the Asian side, 25 dollars in Ankara and 22 dollars in İzmir.
New leases in Istanbul’s Grade A office market totaled 86,202 square meters in the first half of the year, rising 57 percent from the same period of 2025.
The market has recovered from the pandemic-era shift to remote work, while limited development and the conversion of some offices to housing have reduced the supply of modern, centrally located space.

articles.title: Malaysia’s Anwar vows to boost anti-corruption drive after state poll defeats
articles.body:
Malaysia’s Anwar vows to boost anti-corruption drive after state poll defeats
The prime minister says the country’s economic data is ‘not winning the hearts of the people’ but adds ‘reforms cannot be rushed’
Anwar acknowledged shortcomings by his administration that had led to frustration among Malaysians. While the economy grew 6 per cent last quarter and unemployment was low, Anwar said he “won’t deny” that Malaysians faced higher living costs.
“The economic numbers are not winning the hearts of the people,” Anwar said at the annual congress of his People’s Justice Party, or PKR. “I know some people are demanding, but reforms cannot be rushed, it has to be done in stages” and must take into account other parties in the ruling coalition, he said.
PKR and the Pakatan Harapan coalition led by Anwar have fared poorly in three consecutive state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan. The party lost control of Negeri Sembilan this month, going from holding the chief minister’s office to just two seats in the 36-seat assembly. Barisan Nasional, Anwar’s federal government partner and electoral rival, and its allies won supermajorities in Johor and Negeri Sembilan at Pakatan’s expense.
“The message of the people has been clear” following losses in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, Anwar said in Malacca state, which is due to hold its local election by January.
Anwar, 79, who was earlier reported to be considering calling a snap general election as soon as October this year, has indicated he is not in a rush to go to the polls after the recent setbacks. The national poll is due by February 2028.

articles.title: Ukraine strike hits Russia’s main space rocket maker
articles.body:
- Russian officials confirmed a missile strike on an industrial facility in Samara overnight Aug. 15, without naming the target.
- Ukrainian open-source analysts identified the likely target as Building 106A of the Progress rocket-space center.
Ukrainian long-range strikes hit an industrial site in Samara, Russia, overnight into Aug. 15, triggering a regional air raid alert and a series of explosions residents reported hearing across the city, according to Russian officials and Ukrainian open-source monitoring of the aftermath.
Samara region governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed that a missile struck an industrial enterprise in the region, saying emergency services and an operational headquarters were on site and that details on casualties were still being clarified. He did not name the facility. Samara Mayor Ivan Noskov later said a “massed attack” by enemy missiles caused localized damage to the city’s industrial infrastructure, adding that Russian air defenses had intercepted part of the attack. Neither official specified how many missiles were involved or which weapon system struck the ground.
The Ukrainian open-source analysis group CyberBoroshno, which has previously published satellite-imagery assessments of Flamingo missile strikes inside Russia, said the strike most likely used a Ukrainian FP-5 “Flamingo” cruise missile and identified the impact point as Building 106A at the Progress facility, geolocating it to coordinates 53.217623, 50.303163.
Ukrainian commentator Oleh Ponomar separately reported the same conclusion, citing the group’s “GEOINT collective” analysis. Neither Ukraine’s military nor Progress itself had publicly confirmed the specific building as of this writing, and the claim rests on CyberBoroshno’s imagery review rather than official acknowledgment from either government.
According to CyberBoroshno’s assessment, Building 106A is part of the production complex for the Soyuz launch vehicle family and operates as a cleanroom facility, where onboard electrical systems, instruments and circuit boards are installed. The group described the building’s function as producing the rocket’s guidance and control systems, cable network and instrument compartment, work that must be completed before a rocket can be considered finished even after its airframe and fuel tanks are built. CyberBoroshno said a neighboring structure, Building 106B, serves as the final assembly point for completed rockets and may also have been damaged by the blast.
Progress, formerly known as TsSKB-Progress, has produced Soviet and Russian launch vehicles since the 1950s, including the R-7-derived rocket that carried Yuri Gagarin into orbit in 1961. It is Russia’s only facility that performs series production of the Soyuz-2 family of launch vehicles, used both for crewed and uncrewed missions and for placing military and commercial satellites into orbit. The plant also builds electro-optical reconnaissance and Earth-observation satellites.
CyberBoroshno said the facility’s significance lies in that exclusivity. The group said Soyuz-2 rockets built at Progress launch and replenish Russia’s military satellite constellations, including the Liana network used for signals intelligence and targeting and the Persona and Razdan optical reconnaissance satellites, as well as the Rassvet broadband satellite constellation operated by Bureau 1440, a Russian company building a domestic answer to Starlink. Public launch records reviewed independently show that Bureau 1440’s Rassvet satellites, including test and commercial batches launched in 2023 and again in March and July 2026, have so far flown exclusively aboard Soyuz-2.1b rockets from the Vostochny and Plesetsk cosmodromes, a pattern consistent with CyberBoroshno’s characterization, though it could not be independently confirmed that no other launch vehicle has ever been used or is planned.
CyberBoroshno assessed that recovery from fire and firefighting water inside a cleanroom facility would take considerably longer than a conventional industrial repair. The group said restoring the site would require reclassifying clean-room zones, recertifying the manufacturing process and re-testing for airborne particulate contamination, work it estimated in months rather than weeks. The group also said Soyuz onboard electronics depend on imported components subject to export restrictions that Russia cannot currently readily replace, though it did not provide further detail on which specific components would be affected.
The FP-5 Flamingo, built by the Ukrainian company Fire Point, is a ground-launched cruise missile with a published range of up to 3,000 km (1,860 miles) and a warhead of roughly 1,000 to 1,150 kg (2,200 to 2,540 pounds). Ukraine first used the missile in combat in August 2025 against a Russian security service facility in Crimea, according to Ukrainian officials at the time. Fire Point told the Associated Press in 2025 that it aimed to raise production from an initial 30 units a month to 210 units a month by October of that year, though independent verification of actual output has remained limited. CyberBoroshno has previously attributed Flamingo strikes to attacks on the VNIIR-Progress electronics plant in Cheboksary, a separate facility from the Samara center that manufactures satellite-navigation receivers and antennas, and on the Antipinsky oil refinery in Tyumen in July.
The scale of damage at the Samara site remains unresolved.

articles.title: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Indonesia, killing at least 20
articles.body:
Nelly Florida Riama, a deputy director for geophysics at Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency, warned that while the tsunami warning was over, "aftershocks are still occurring."
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake hit the Southeast Asian nation of Indonesia on Saturday, killing at least 38 people.
The quake struck to the north of Flores Island in the eastern part of the country in the early hours of the morning, sparking panic as people fled into the streets amid crumbling buildings.
A tsunami warning was declared but has since been lifted, with Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency (BMKG) saying it was no longer detecting significant sea level rises that could threaten coastal communities.
"Thirty-eight people have been confirmed dead, two were seriously injured, 11 sustained minor injuries, and approximately 2,000 people have evacuated on their own," National Agency for Disaster Countermeasure (BNPB) chief Suharyanto said during a press conference, per AFP.
Nelly Florida Riama, a deputy director for geophysics at BMKG, warned that while the tsunami warning was over, "aftershocks are still occurring."
"We urge the public to remain calm, not to be swayed by irresponsible rumours, and to keep up to date with information from the BMKG’s official channels,” Nelly added.
The BNPB said tremors were reported to have been felt across the regencies of Nagekeo, Sikka, and West Manggarai in the province of East Nusa Tenggara; Bima City and Bima Regency in West Nusa Tenggara; and in the Jeneponto, Selayar Islands, and Maros Regencies in South Sulawesi.

articles.title: Polish Police Detain Two Suspects Following Assault on Ukrainians
articles.body:
Polish authorities in Poznań arrested two women on Friday in connection with an incident of aggressive behavior directed at Ukrainian citizens outside a local establishment.
Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński confirmed the detentions on X.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The incident occurred after midnight on Aug. 13 near the CastaCraftowe pub in the Old Town area of Poznań, Onet and Wirtualna Polska reported.

A video of the altercation, shared on social media by an employee of the establishment, showed two women behaving aggressively toward individuals speaking Ukrainian and Russian.
According to the employee, one of the women began shouting insults and demanding the individuals “get out to Ukraine.” The footage also showed the women throwing a street umbrella and striking the victims.
According to law enforcement, the suspects are 35 and 36 years old. Preliminary information from the police suggests the women were likely intoxicated at the time of the incident.
“Investigators from the Poznań-Stare Miasto police station and the Municipal Police Headquarters in Poznań detained two women suspected of an attack based on national hatred against a group of Ukrainian citizens,” the police statement read.
Following their detention, the suspects were transferred to a police holding facility. A decision regarding formal charges is expected on Saturday.
Nationwide rallies support minorities
The incident in Poznań follows a series of demonstrations held the previous weekend to protest violence and discrimination against minorities in Poland.
Russia Admits New Petrol Shortages as Ukrainian Strikes Hit Refineries
On Aug. 9, the Committee for the Defense of Democracy (KOD) organized rallies in 22 cities, including Warsaw, Krakow, and Gdańsk, under the slogan “Don’t be indifferent.”
Organizers stated the nationwide action was a response to an increasing frequency of verbal and physical attacks targeting individuals based on their origin, language, or appearance, and aimed to show solidarity with Ukrainians.
During the rallies, participants distributed stickers bearing the campaign’s slogan, intended for display on businesses and vehicles as a sign of support and safety for Ukrainians.
Rise in reported hate crimes
While Poland has provided extensive military and humanitarian assistance to Ukraine since 2022 and hosts nearly one million displaced individuals, recent data indicates a rise in anti-Ukrainian incidents.
A recent report stated that Polish police received 180 reports of suspected hate crimes against Ukrainians in the first half of 2026, an increase of more than 30% compared to the same period in the previous year.
Additionally, diplomatic relations between the two nations have experienced strain over differing interpretations of World War II history, particularly concerning the Volhynia massacres.

articles.title: Gallery: Ukrainian children's fairytale art from Kharkiv reaches Estonia
articles.body:
Gallery: Ukrainian children's fairytale art from Kharkiv reaches Estonia
More than a dozen works by young artists in Kharkiv are now on display in Pärnu, blending forgotten legends and untold tales with new mythologies in large, colorful scenes.
"Lost Fairy Tales" opened at the Pärnu Museum of New Art (MONA) this week, showcasing 14 monumental original works created by about 40 children and teens ages 5–17.
Kharkiv's Aza Nizi Maza art studio continues to operate from a World War II-era bomb shelter, where kids still meet, learn and create amid ongoing drone, missile and guided-bomb strikes on the city.
The exhibition grew from the idea of a "missing museum" — a world made up of forgotten legends, untold stories and new mythologies inspired by the Baroque collections of European museums.
The young artists first drew elements found in ancient frescoes, botanical atlases, medieval maps and manuscripts before developing characters and building narratives around them.
Details like rosehips, seashells, bones, bats, lions and musical instruments meet characters ranging from beggars, saints and witches to princesses, children and those who have seen it all.
The scale of the works, which measure 2.5 x 1.5 meters, allows viewers to step into these visual worlds and become part of the unfolding narratives.
Curated by Mykola Kolomiiets and Iryna Hrytska, "Lost Fairy Tales" will remain on view in Pärnu through October 4.
--
Editor: Kaspar Viilup, Aili Vahtla

articles.title: Diyarbakır could produce up to three times as much oil as Gabar: Minister
articles.body:
An unconventional oil exploration program in the southeastern province of Diyarbakır could produce two to three times as much crude as the Gabar field in neighboring Şırnak if successful, Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar has said.
Bayraktar told CNN Türk that horizontal drilling was being tested across four fields covering about 600 square kilometers north of Bismil to extract oil believed to be trapped in rock formations.
The wider prospective zone extends across more than 7,000 square kilometers, he said.
If the trials prove successful, hundreds of wells could be drilled with foreign partners.
Gabar currently produces more than 83,000 barrels a day and contributes at least $2 billion to the Turkish economy annually, according to Bayraktar.
The minister said Türkiye, which imports about two-thirds of the energy it consumes, was also preparing a plan for 2035 that envisages up to 10 million electric vehicles.
The government aims to raise installed wind and solar capacity from 45,000 megawatts to 120,000 megawatts over the next decade.

articles.title: this milan apartment is bursting with thousands of twentieth-century masterpieces
articles.body:
It’s a bit difficult to find the entrance to Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano because it’s not housed in a traditional ‘museum.’ Located in the Porta Venezia neighborhood of Milan, there is no grand museum entrance. Instead, you find it by entering one of the towering palazzos, or apartment buildings. It’s one of several of Milan’s ‘house museums,’ former residences that have been transformed to hold vast collections of art and antiquities, opening historic homes up to public view. What makes the former home of Antonio Boschi and Marieda Di Stefano special is its vast collection of twentieth-century art. In their lifetime, the socialite couple rubbed shoulders with famous artists and designers of the period, accumulating about 2,000 pieces from friends and icons alike. What results is a domestic space that holds both the memory of the family and the century alike.
in Milan, the former home of the former home of Antonio Boschi and Marieda Di Stefano now displays their collection of twentieth-century art | all images courtesy of Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano
Antonio Boschi, Marieda Di Stefano, and their cats
The entrance to their former apartment is on the second floor of a building designed by Italian architect Piero Portaluppi between 1929 and 1931. It’s an older building reminiscent of a bygone era for Milan—the floors are mosaic tiles formed in a triangular pattern, and a spiraling staircase running the circumference of the building’s interior leads you to the entrance. The walls are a trompe l’oeil of painted stone. The building was commissioned by Marieda Di Stefano’s father, who envisioned the multistory building as a series of units for his children to live in side by side.
Greeting visitors in the entrance hall of their former residence are two paintings of the couple: I coniugi Boschi (1951) and I coniugi Boschi (1947), which roughly translates to The Boschi couple, or Mr. and Mrs. Boschi. They are half-length portraits of the pair holding their cats, created four years apart by the painter Remo Brindisi. The Italian painter himself has his own house museum dedicated to his works outside of Bologna, designed by the famed Italian architect Nanda Vigo.
view of a guest room in the residence housing paintings like Arturo Tosi’s Songavazzo (1925) and Achille Funi’s Trieste (1933) among others
Donated to the Municipality of Milan
The couple was deeply situated in the Milanese community. Antonio Boschi was a longtime engineer for the high-end tire manufacturer Pirelli, known for its involvement in Formula 1 racing. Marieda Di Stefano studied ceramics and continued to practice her passion throughout her lifetime, with a few of her pieces displayed in the house. Upon their passing, their collections were entrusted to the Municipality of Milan. The collection would be exhibited at Palazzo Reale in 1974 while a more permanent exhibition space was sought.
the entrance to the house museum with a view of ceramic plates created by Marieda Boschi Di Stefano
The House before it was a museum
After some renovations, the former home of the couple was modified to accommodate the works. The house museum at Via Giorgio Jan, 15, which is beautiful, pristine, and filled with filtered natural light, was not the state of the house while it was being lived in. The couple stored a huge collection in this space. It was so vast that the entirety couldn’t possibly fit on the available wall space.
Photographs taken by Gabriele Basilico in 1982 create a kind of faithful capture of how the home would have looked when occupied by Boschi and Di Stefano. This series was commissioned by Italian Radical design figure and Domus editor Alessandro Mendini (who was also Marieda Di Stefano’s grandson). The floors were covered in a patchwork of what looks to be Persian carpets. There were huge canvases stacked upon each other and leaning against the wall. There were framed paintings puzzle-pieced together to take advantage of all the vertical surfaces that existed between floor and ceiling.
in 1982, a series of photos of the home was commissioned by Italian Radical design figure and Domus editor Alessandro Mendini (who was also Marieda Di Stefano’s grandson)
Touring the twentieth century in eleven rooms
Now, the space’s eleven rooms are arranged to take the visitor chronologically and thematically through the 20th century of art: ‘from the Novecento Italiano to Mario Sironi, from the painters of Corrente, Giorgio Morandi and Filippo De Pisis to the so-called School of Paris and the Chiaristi, from Lucio Fontana to Spazialismo and Informale.’ Although many of the works are from Italian artists, there is a section from English artist Ralph Rumney, who was a member of the avant-garde Situationist International movement in Europe. In a room of Giorgio de Chirico works, one can find The School of Gladiators: The Combat (1928). And finally, there are the famed Concetto spaziale works of Lucio Fontana, the infamous slashes through canvas that he became known for.
After making your way through a fairly ordinary apartment made extraordinary by just a sliver of the couple’s collection, there’s a sense of awe at the many functions a house could have: shelter, a meeting ground, a museum, a treasure chest for artistic marvels.
before the museum officially opened in 2003, the couple kept huge canvases stacked upon each other and leaning against the wall as their collection was too big fit on their walls
designed by Piero Portaluppi, the building was commissioned by Marieda Di Stefano’s father, who envisioned the multistory building as a series of units for his children to live in side by side

articles.title: Iran warns Trump against adventurism in Strait of Hormuz
articles.body:
Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i, head of Iran's judiciary, said that the Strait of Hormuz is "an inseparable part of Iran's territorial and border domain" and warned that any "adventurism" in the waterway would be met with a decisive response, rejecting recent claims by U.S. President Donald Trump over the strait.
Writing on social media, Mohseni-Eje'i dismissed Trump's remarks as baseless, saying Iran is the rightful owner of the strategic waterway under international law and the principles of national sovereignty.
"Trump is a full-fledged loser in the hard arena of politics and military combat," he wrote. "What consoles his troubled mind is these virtual antics and nonsense. Trump and his advisers must know that the boot of arrogance will never touch the Strait of Hormuz. What multi-billion-dollar aircraft carriers could not achieve will not be achieved with a few tweets and speeches."
MNA

articles.title: The plant in Samara was hit by Flamingo – confirmation has emerged
articles.body:
The plant in Samara was hit by Flamingo – confirmation has emerged
Kyiv • UNN
Explosions rang out in Samara on the night of August 15. Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point confirmed the strike on the missile center.
During the night of August 15, 2026, a series of explosions rang out in Samara, Russia. OSINT analysts said that the area where the Progress Rocket and Space Center and the Aviakor aircraft plant are located was hit. Ukrainian weapons manufacturer Fire Point confirmed that the Progress rocket center was hit, UNN reports.
The Progress Rocket and Space Center is one of the key enterprises in Russia’s rocket and space industry. The center develops and manufactures medium-class launch vehicles, including the Soyuz-2 family, as well as spacecraft for remote sensing of the Earth and scientific programs.
According to preliminary data, the strike hit the enterprise’s main assembly shop. A threat to a building located next to the Aviakor aircraft plant, which repairs and services Tu-95MS strategic bombers, was also reported.
As the CyberBoroshno OSINT channel indicates, this likely refers to Building 106A.
It is part of the Soyuz launch vehicle production complex. Building 106A operates under a high cleanroom standard: onboard electrical equipment, instruments, and printed circuit boards are assembled here—in effect, the launch vehicle’s “nervous system”: the control system, cable network, and instrument compartment. Without this stage, the rocket cannot be assembled, even when the body and tanks are ready.
The authorities of the Samara region confirmed that an industrial facility had been hit. At the same time, they said that the attack had been repelled. An operational headquarters was established in the region.
Denys Shtilerman, chief designer and co-founder of Fire Point, also published a video of a missile launch, apparently the same one that hit the space manufacturing facility in Samara.

articles.title: 'Broken and grateful': Alice Springs farewells Kumanjayi Little Baby
articles.body:
IN BRIEF
- Almost four months after the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, the community has gathered for her funeral service.
- The Warlpiri girl has been described as a beautiful "little princess" who loved cuddling puppies, the colour pink and music.
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.
This article may be distressing to some readers.
Alice Springs is known as the Red Centre of Australia but on 15 August, the community donned pink for the funeral of five-year-old Warlpiri girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby.
Warlpiri Elder and family spokesperson Robin Granites said pink was her favourite colour — it "reminds us of the clothes she used to wear".
"And the times when we would go in the evening, you see the sunset and even the early morning, you see the pink colour of clouds and that ... is a really good colour for us," Granites said ahead of the funeral.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
Kumanjayi Little Baby's body was found on 30 April, after she went missing from Old Timers town camp, south of Alice Springs. Her disappearance sparked a five-day search, described as one of the largest search efforts in Northern Territory history.
47-year-old Jefferson Lewis has since been charged with her alleged murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons.
Pastor Rejeili Paulo-Smith spoke on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother at the funeral service.
She requested that her daughter be remembered, "for who she was, not simply for the tragedy of how her life ended".
"Kumanjayi wasn't simply a little girl who was known by the community. She was Mum's baby too. She was a little girl whose presence filled their home and whose absence has left an enormous space," Paulo-Smith said.
Jintangka: 'We're all in one'
It's been almost four months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby. During this time, her family and Indigenous communities have engaged in the grieving period and mourning process known as Sorry Business.
In recent months, Paulo-Smith said the community had felt "both broken and grateful".
"Broken because a precious little life has been taken from us far too soon, yet grateful because Kumanjayi Little Baby was here. She was known, she was loved, she mattered," she said.
The week following Kumanjayi Little Baby's death, thousands of Australians gathered at nationwide candlelight vigils.
At a local vigil in Alice Springs, 89-year-old Maya Cifali told NITV News the outpouring of community spirit was unlike anything she had ever seen.
"It is the first time that such a community spirit is felt for all of us," Cifali said.
She has lived in Alice Springs for around 40 years.
Granites also believes the local community has displayed the Warlpiri concept of Jintangka; "which means we're all in one, everyone together".
At the funeral, he took the opportunity to thank Australians and people overseas for rallying behind his family during and in the months following the search for Kumanjayi Little Baby.
"That really helped us during those sad days, those unforgettable days," Granites said.
"We've done everything we can to help each other, so we should be all proud of each other and say thank you."
A memorial service was held for Kumanjayi Little Baby on 14 August.
Following public funeral proceedings on 15 August, there was also an intimate burial service.
'Forever five, forever young'
Liberal senator and Kumanjayi Little Baby's family member Jacinta Nampajinpa Price was in attendance at the funeral.
SBS News can confirm Minister for Indigenous Australians Malarndirri McCarthy, Sue-Anne Hunter, the National Commissioner for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children and Young People and Katie Kiss, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Justice Commissioner, attended the funeral.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese previously visited Alice Springs, where he described Kumanjayi Little Baby as a "cherished" child and offered his condolences to her grieving family.
"It's important to be able to say to the family that the nation stands with them in their grief," Albanese said in May.
There was a sombre atmosphere at Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral, with speeches punctuated by cries from the crowd. Hundreds of people visited to pay their respects, with attendees spilling beyond the funeral Chapel and onto the grass lawn.
Kumanjayi Little Baby was remembered as a "beautiful", "loved" and "treasured" child who brought joy to her family. She loved rainbows, the colour pink, music and cuddling puppies.
She was described as her mother's "little princess", who will be remembered as "forever five, forever young".
Speaking on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother, Paulo-Smith said, "Kumanjayi's earthly life was short, but her life was not without meaning".
"As Mum has said, we look to the night sky and remember the brightest star. Not because the star replaces you but because it reminds us to lift our eyes beyond what we can see."

articles.title: New car rental rules set age, mileage caps
articles.body:
Türkiye has finalized new rules for short-term car rentals, setting age and mileage limits for vehicles while introducing licensing, fleet and deposit requirements for operators.
The regulation, published in the Official Gazette on Aug. 15, will take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.
It covers consumer rentals of up to 29 days, while long-term, business-to-business, shared and camper rentals are excluded.
Except for classic cars, vehicles more than six years old may not be rented.
The mileage ceiling will be 300,000 kilometers for fully electric vehicles and 180,000 kilometers for all others.
Vehicles with a record of severe damage, an expired inspection or no compulsory motor insurance will also be barred.
Those whose periodic maintenance is overdue may be rented only after they have been serviced.
The final limits are higher than those in a draft released in February, which proposed a five-year age cap and a ceiling of 100,000 kilometers.
Rental businesses will be required to obtain authorization certificates.
Operators in metropolitan districts with more than 30,000 residents must have at least 10 vehicles, including five registered in their own name.
At least two must be hybrid or fully electric, with one produced in Türkiye.
Deposits will be capped at three days’ rent for bookings of up to six days and seven days’ rent for rentals lasting seven to 29 days.
Refund procedures must be completed within seven days of the vehicle’s return.
The Trade Ministry will establish a central information system to track rental businesses and vehicles.
Existing operators must obtain authorization certificates by July 1, 2027, and meet the new fleet and vehicle standards by Jan. 1, 2028.

articles.title: Judo World Tour: A day of firsts at the Lima Grand Prix
articles.body:
Day one in Lima delivered five thrilling champions. Assunta Scutto, Michel Augusto, Rafaela Rodrigues, Radu Izvoreanu and Pihla Salonen claimed gold, with several celebrating their first Grand Prix titles as the new Olympic qualification cycle got underway.
Welcome to Lima for the opening day of the Judo Grand Prix!
In -48kg, Assunta SCUTTO faced Maria Celia LABORDE. The reigning World Champion managed a clever turnover and held LABORDE down for victory, earning her very first Grand Prix gold medal.
IOC Member Dr Paula PARETO awarded the medals.
In the -60kg, Michel AUGUSTO faced Jonathan YANG. AUGUSTO took the lead with an ashi-waza for yuko and managed to defend the score to take home his first Grand Prix gold medal.
International Judo Federation Education & Coaching Director Mr Mohammed MERIDJA awarded the medals.
At -52kg, Rafaela RODRIGUES faced Francine ECHEVARRIA. RODRIGUES came back from a yuko down and held ECHEVARRIA for victory. A debut Grand Prix gold for the Brazilian.
Peruvian Judo Federation President Mrs Maria MARTINEZ MURCIEGO awarded the medals.
At -66kg, Radu IZVOREANU faced teammate Denis VIERU. An absolutely huge ippon from IZVOREANU left no doubt that he would stand on the top spot of the podium. A spectacular finish. Gold and silver for Moldova.
Peruvian Olympic Committee President Mr Renzo MANYARI awarded the medals.
At -57kg, Pihla SALONEN faced Adriana RODRIGUEZ SALVADOR. SALONEN took the gold medal with a brilliant ippon, finishing the contest in style after an impressive performance all day to secure Grand Prix glory in Lima.
International Judo Federation Referee Director Mr Raul CAMACHO PEREZ awarded the medals.
Thank you for joining us here in beautiful Lima! We’ll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Mogadishu sheds deadly reputation with Turkish support
articles.body:
An empty street with closed shops is seen in Mogadishu, Somalia, June 4, 2026. (AP Photo)
Türkiye has played a key role in improving security in Mogadishu, where a steep decline in al-Shabaab attacks has been accompanied by a revival in commerce and social life, The Economist has reported.
Attacks by the al-Qaeda-linked group in the Somali capital fell from 144 in the third quarter of 2022 to five in the second quarter of 2026, the weekly said.
The change is visible across the city, with new cafés remaining open past midnight, streets growing busier and construction activity increasing.
President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, who has survived several assassination attempts, addressed an Independence Day gathering at one of the capital’s frequently targeted junctions on July 1.
The Economist attributed much of the improvement to Turkish support for intelligence capabilities, security camera networks and military training.
A Western diplomat in Mogadishu also credited Türkiye with much of the progress.
Türkiye opened its largest overseas military training academy in Mogadishu in 2017 and has since trained Somali troops while supporting the national army’s operations against al-Shabaab.
Turkish companies also operate Mogadishu’s airport and port, while Ankara’s involvement in Somalia has expanded into offshore energy exploration and plans for a spaceport.
The report cautioned, however, that al-Shabaab remains entrenched outside the capital.
Analysts said the decline in attacks in Mogadishu did not necessarily mean the group had been weakened and could instead reflect a change in tactics.

articles.title: Canada, U.S. remain far apart in trade talks as tariff deadline looms
articles.body:
OTTAWA, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- Canada and the United States remain far apart in negotiations aimed at averting new 50-percent U.S. tariffs scheduled to take effect Aug. 19, Reuters reported Friday.
Canadian Minister responsible for Canada-U.S. Trade Dominic LeBlanc gave that assessment to an advisory committee after another week of negotiations in Washington, according to a source directly briefed on his remarks. LeBlanc has met U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer four times in three weeks, and talks are expected to continue through the weekend.
U.S. President Donald Trump has ordered 50-percent tariffs on nearly 20 billion U.S. dollars' worth of Canadian imports, including some goods that qualify for preferential treatment under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement.
Key disputes include Canadian measures affecting U.S. autos, dairy products and alcohol, while Ottawa is seeking relief from U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum.
Canadian Chamber of Commerce CEO Candace Laing said both sides are seeking an interim agreement covering existing tariffs and the threatened new duties. ■

articles.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak spreads to 6th province amid warnings of prolonged transmission
articles.body:
KINSHASA, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has spread to a sixth province, with confirmed cases rising to 4,727 and deaths to 2,214, according to the latest report released on Friday by the DRC's health authorities.
The report said the outbreak has affected 55 health zones across Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo provinces, with Ituri remaining the epicenter.
Buta health zone in Bas-Uele was newly affected. Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) Director-General Jean Kaseya said Thursday that one person had travelled from Isiro in neighboring Haut-Uele to Buta, and died there later.
A total of 976 people have recovered since the start of the epidemic. Health authorities, however, warned that persistent community transmission and gaps in contact tracing could prolong what is already the world's second-largest Ebola epidemic on record.
COMMUNITY TRANSMISSION CONTINUES
Kaseya said more than 63 percent of Ebola deaths were currently occurring in communities rather than treatment centers or hospitals.
Community deaths further complicate response efforts because health authorities may not know who came into contact with infected people before or after death, making contact tracing and safe and dignified burials more difficult, he said.
The latest government report put the contact follow-up rate at 82.6 percent. Africa CDC, however, said the proportion of registered contacts being followed does not by itself reflect the effectiveness of contact tracing if many contacts are never identified in the first place. The figures indicated that community-based surveillance and contact identification needed to be strengthened, Kaseya said.
World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Wednesday that a high proportion of deaths continued to occur in communities, while many new cases were being detected among people who were not on existing contact lists, indicating that some transmission chains had yet to be identified.
"It's already the second-biggest Ebola epidemic on record, and it's moving faster than any previous Ebola outbreak," Tedros told a press briefing in Geneva.
"At its current pace, it's on track to eclipse the West African Ebola outbreak of 2014 to 2016," he warned.
The 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic, the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded, infected more than 28,600 people.
TRUE SCALE UNCLEAR
The DRC formally declared the outbreak on May 15, but Kaseya said studies examined by Africa CDC suggested that transmission may have begun around February.
"We have no clue about what happened from February to May," he said, adding that figures collected since the declaration should not necessarily be regarded as a complete picture of the epidemic.
Africa CDC is now pushing for a more village-based response that would also seek to reconstruct the early stages of the outbreak.
Kaseya said communities would be asked to help identify people who died or fell ill with Ebola-like symptoms between January and May. Where laboratory confirmation is no longer possible, such information could still help authorities estimate the extent of transmission before the outbreak was formally detected.
Chikwe Ihekweazu, executive director of the WHO Health Emergencies Program, also said investigations so far suggest the virus may have been circulating for two to three months before the outbreak was formally detected, although the exact start of transmission remains under investigation.
OUTBREAK COULD LAST A YEAR
Abdirahman Mahamud, WHO director for health emergency alert and response operations, said Wednesday that response planning is currently based on a moderate scenario under which the outbreak could continue for about six months.
"There's a worst-case scenario where this outbreak may last nine months to 12 months," Mahamud said, adding that efforts were underway to shorten the duration of the epidemic.
Africa CDC has issued an even stronger conditional warning. "If we don't stop this outbreak," Kaseya warned, "it could last more than a year and ultimately become the largest Ebola epidemic ever recorded."
Kaseya said reversing the trajectory would require a combination of measures, including shifting more responsibility for surveillance and response to villages, ensuring access to essential health services, strengthening the referral of suspected cases, deploying additional medical tools and improving the coordination of response resources. ■

articles.title: Interview: Japan needs strength to face wartime history head-on, says former NHK anchor
articles.body:
TOKYO, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- "Not having gone to the battlefield to kill innocent people does not mean we bear no responsibility for history," veteran Japanese journalist and former NHK anchor Tomoyoshi Kimura said recently.
With that conviction, Kimura sat down with Xinhua ahead of the 81st anniversary of Japan's surrender in World War II. He expressed concern that Japanese society is drifting toward a dangerous historical amnesia, where many people neither understand nor wish to learn about the country's wartime past, warning that the lack of basic historical awareness has now reached a shocking level.
Having spent decades reporting for Japan's public broadcaster NHK before turning to the study of social thought, Kimura has closely observed how public perceptions of the past have evolved. He believes that, 81 years after the war, the aggressive nature of Japan's wartime actions and the country's responsibility as a perpetrator are becoming increasingly blurred.
Kimura pointed to an NHK opinion poll released in March that highlighted the seriousness of the problem. When asked whether the war had been "a war of aggression launched by Japan against its Asian neighbors," 48 percent of respondents answered that they did not know, while only about one-third agreed with the statement.
"This is an extremely serious problem. Calling it merely 'serious' is almost an understatement," Kimura said.
In his view, the decline in historical awareness stems not only from insufficient war education in Japanese schools but also from the way the war has long been narrated in Japanese society.
Kimura recalled watching a television drama about two years ago in which the narrator said, "The war had already entered its third year." Curious about the timeline, Kimura checked the setting and realized it referred to 1944.
In Japan, when people speak of "that war," many automatically think it began with the Pacific War in 1941, Kimura explained, noting that consequently, many Japanese have come to believe that Japan simply lost to the United States' "material resources, industrial capacity and economic strength."
"Little by little, this idea has been implanted into people's consciousness," he added. "People have forgotten that Japan was, in fact, defeated by China's resistance against Japanese militarist aggression."
August has become Japan's "war reporting season," according to the veteran reporter. "As August arrives, with Aug. 15 at its center, television programs, documentaries and special reports about the war increase dramatically," he said. Yet he believes these stories remain strikingly one-sided.
The reports talk about "having nothing to eat and suffering greatly during the war and the grief of losing family members," but they keep silent on the agony of the people who were subjected to aggression -- those who had their food, their homes, and their lives taken from them, according to Kimura.
This imbalance has persisted for a long time. While there are voices in Japanese public opinion attempting to directly face the wartime history, he said, regrettably, they have not coalesced into a sufficiently powerful force.
Kimura expressed particular concern over the argument that "without having experienced the war, one bears no responsibility and has no need for reflection."
He cited remarks made by current Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during a parliamentary session in 1995 while serving as a member of the House of Representatives, when Takaichi argued that, as someone belonging to a generation that was not directly involved in the war, she has not reflected on the war, nor is there any reason for her to do so.
Kimura said that while not having gone to the battlefield to kill innocent people means that one is innocent of committing those crimes, "it does not mean one bears no responsibility for this history."
"For Japanese people, being born after the war cannot become a reason to claim there is 'no need for reflection,'" he added. "Even the postwar generation has a responsibility toward history."
Kimura also drew parallels between history and Japan's current security policy, as the government continues expanding military capabilities under the banner of defense.
Japanese militarism once launched wars of aggression under pretexts such as "self-preservation and self-defense," he said, noting that "those arguments concealed enormous falsehoods and serious problems."
"Unless people examine them carefully, they cannot grasp the issue, nor will they harbor any vigilance regarding the 'defense capability buildup' that Japan is currently pushing forward," Kimura warned.
During the interview, Kimura recalled one of the unforgettable experiences of his reporting career: interviewing a South Korean "comfort woman." "Before meeting her, I had read books and knew the basic facts of the subject," he said. "But only after hearing her story in person did I truly understand the unbearable cruelty of that inhumane violence."
Perpetrators may attempt to treat the war as if it "never happened," but for victims, those memories will not vanish from history, Kimura said.
"Given Japan's current situation, we must examine our past once again," he added. "Japan needs the strength to face history directly." ■

articles.title: S. Korean president Lee calls for dialogue with DPRK to formally end Korean War, pursue peaceful coexistence
articles.body:
SEOUL, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Saturday called on South Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) to respect each other, refrain from unnecessary confrontation, and pursue peaceful coexistence and shared growth.
In his address marking the 81st anniversary of the Korean Peninsula's liberation from Japanese colonial rule, Lee unveiled a roadmap for peaceful coexistence with the DPRK, calling for dialogue among the directly concerned parties to officially end the Korean War and transform the Korean Peninsula's unstable armistice into a peace regime.
The proposal builds on Lee's pledge at last year's Liberation Day ceremony that Seoul would respect the DPRK's system, rule out unification by absorption and refrain from hostile acts. Lee said that he was setting out steps to put those principles into practice.
Lee called on the two Koreas to respect each other and avoid unnecessary confrontation, while gradually reducing hostility in their perceptions, norms and institutions. He said he hoped the two sides could sit down together to explore ways toward peaceful coexistence and shared growth.
To make coexistence sustainable, Lee said South Korea would establish mechanisms to manage tensions and conflicts and build multiple safeguards against crises and escalation. Seoul would also comprehensively assess the security environment surrounding the peninsula and pursue proactive and sustained peace measures, he said.
Lee also proposed dialogue among the directly concerned parties to formally bring an end to the Korean War and replace the current armistice with a peace regime. ■

articles.title: Deadly Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
articles.body:
AA photo.
An Israeli airstrike on a house in the southern Lebanese town of Ansar killed at least seven people and wounded three early on Aug. 15, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency (NNA) reported.
The house was destroyed, while Civil Defense teams continued searching the rubble for possible additional victims. The wounded were taken to hospitals in Nabatieh, according to NNA.
The agency also reported Israeli attacks in and around Nabatieh and Bint Jbeil.
Israeli forces blew up several homes in Bint Jbeil and opened heavy machine-gun fire toward houses near the Kounine-Saf al-Hawa road. Israeli warplanes also struck the al-Mansouri area shortly before midnight.
The Ansar strike was among the deadliest since Lebanon and Israel announced a framework agreement on June 26 setting out an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon in exchange for the disarmament of Hezbollah.

articles.title: Putin congratulates Indian president, PM on Independence Day
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 15. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin has congratulated Indian President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the country's Independence Day, the Kremlin website reported.
"Your country is achieving impressive success in economic, social, scientific, and technological spheres, and rightfully enjoys high prestige on the global stage. Relations between Russia and India are successfully developing in the spirit of a specially privileged strategic partnership.
Moscow and New Delhi cooperate fruitfully across a wide range of areas, interacting effectively within the UN, SCO, BRICS, and other multilateral structures," the telegram reads.
Putin expressed confidence that Russia and India will continue to fully expand constructive ties for the benefit of their friendly peoples, as well as to strengthen international security and stability. The Russian leader wished Modi and Murmu good health and success, as well as happiness and prosperity to all citizens of India.

articles.title: Orca Toñi in Strait of Gibraltar has 10 holes in fin from suspected shooting
articles.body:
The Ministry for Ecological Transition has opened an investigation after finding Toñi, the oldest orca in the Strait of Gibraltar, with pellet gunshot marks on her dorsal fin.
Toñi is around 60 years old and is known among researchers as the "grandmother" of the orca population that moves between the Strait of Gibraltar and the Gulf of Cádiz. This week she has appeared with as many as a dozen marks on her dorsal fin and back which, according to the organisations that monitor her, were not there in the photographs taken a few weeks earlier.
It was the conservation group WeWhale that raised the alarm after comparing the animal’s current condition with its previous photographic record. Janek Andre, founder of WeWhale and Iberian Orca Guardians, said that the wounds now visible on the fin and back are, in his view, consistent with the impact of a shotgun blast.
The Atlantic Orca Working Group has gone further in its technical assessment. According to this collective, the injuries could correspond to lead pellets of around 9 millimetres, similar to those used in buckshot cartridges for wild boar, and it notes that this type of ammunition usually spreads nine projectiles in three rows of three, a pattern they consider to match the arrangement of the marks found on the animal.
Investigation under way
The Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge learned of the case on the afternoon of 11 August, through information submitted by WeWhale (source in Spanish), an organisation authorised to operate in the area. The following day, the Directorate-General for Biodiversity, Forests and Desertification opened preliminary proceedings to clarify the facts and, if appropriate, to launch a sanctions procedure against those responsible.
The vice-president and minister for the Ecological Transition, Sara Aagesen, confirmed via the social network Bluesky that the orca showed marks consistent with pellet shots and stressed that this is a vulnerable species, so any harm caused to it constitutes a serious offence.
CIRCE, the organisation that has been carrying out scientific monitoring of Iberian orcas since 1999 and holds a photographic archive of Toñi spanning more than two decades, has also joined this work.
The organisation has pointed out that, before determining the origin of the injuries, it is necessary to examine the available images in detail, compare them with the historical series and carry out fresh direct monitoring of the animal and its group.
For the time being, none of the authorities involved has officially confirmed that the wounds were caused by a shot, although this remains the main working hypothesis.
What the law says and how to act around an orca
The orca population of the Strait of Gibraltar and the Gulf of Cádiz is listed as vulnerable in the Spanish Catalogue of Endangered Species. Article 57 of Law 42/2007 on Natural Heritage and Biodiversity prohibits any action aimed at killing, capturing, pursuing or harassing the specimens included in that catalogue.
The specific rules on cetacean protection add further restrictions: no vessel may approach closer than 500 metres, make contact with the animals, swim with them, feed them, obstruct their path, split up groups or emit loud sounds to attract or scare them.
In the critical area of the Ensenada de Barbate, Conil and the Banco Majuán, orca watching is also banned between 1 March and 31 August. Anyone who breaches these measures faces fines of up to two million euros and criminal liability, according to MITECO itself.
Since 2020 there has been an increase in interactions between these orcas and vessels sailing through the Strait and the Gulf of Cádiz. For this reason, the Ministry of Transport and MITECO recommend avoiding navigation in the area between April and August and, if there is an encounter with the animal, heading for the coast, avoiding any manoeuvre that could harm it, keeping people away from the gunwale and alerting the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre.
The case of Toñi has once again turned the spotlight on this protected population. The organisations working in the area insist that these animals need protection, not reprisals.

articles.title: Senior reshuffle announced for gendarmerie, coast guard
articles.body:
AA photo.
Promotions and appointments across Türkiye’s Gendarmerie General Command and Coast Guard Command have been published in the Official Gazette under decisions signed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.
Within the gendarmerie, seven generals and 18 colonels were promoted by one rank. The promotions will take effect on Aug. 30.
Major Generals Ünsal Bulut and Murat Bulut were promoted to lieutenant general, while Brigadier Generals Hüseyin Bekmez, Hamdi Gülpınar, Ömer Ersever, Ferruh Taraktaş and Mustafa Bakçepınar were elevated to major general.
A further 18 colonels were promoted to brigadier general.
The decisions also reassigned 78 generals and colonels.
Lieutenant General Yusuf Kenan Topcu was moved from the Istanbul Provincial Gendarmerie Command to the Van Gendarmerie Public Order Corps Command.
Ünsal Bulut and Murat Bulut were appointed deputy commanders of the Gendarmerie General Command.
Major General Metin Düz was named head of public order. Cengiz Yıldız was reassigned from Ankara to Erzurum, İdris Tataroğlu from Bursa to Istanbul and Tarık Hekimoğlu from Diyarbakır to Ankara as provincial gendarmerie commanders.

articles.title: Reform Party wants former EKRE MP as next Riigikogu Defense Committee chair
articles.body:
Reform Party wants former EKRE MP as next Riigikogu Defense Committee chair
The coalition Reform Party has proposed a former Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) MP as next chair of the Riigikogu's National Defense Committee, Postimees reported.
The move if successful may help the now-minority Reform-Eesti 200 coalition get votes passed at the Riigikogu.
The MP, Leo Kunnas, now sits as an independent, and Reform's secretary general, Kristo Enn Vaga, told Postimees his name had been discussed favorably.
However, Vaga said, Kunnas has not formally been agreed on within the party as candidate for the next Riigikogu Defense Committee chair to replace Kalev Stoicescu, who stepped down this week.
"He has served as deputy chair, has said he will not run for anything else, and his work there would be guided not by political interests but by national defense interests," Vaga said, noting it is not yet known whether Kunnas would agree to run for the post.
That a former EKRE member has been floated for the role by Reform – the parties were very much at loggerheads when EKRE was in office 2019–2021 – is likely the result of the Reform-Eesti 200 coalition now being a minority government; courting Kunnas could mean he will vote with the government on the state budget come autumn, and on other key matters.
Additionally, the current composition of the Defense Committee is such that electing a coalition MP to the post could prove complicated, while as noted Kunnas has served as deputy chair in any case. He is also a retired military officer.
The vote on the new Defense Committee chair is to take place on September 14, after parliament has reconvened from its summer break.
Kalev Stoicescu announced Sunday evening he was quitting Eesti 200, and he is stepping down as Defense Committee chief as well.
His departure and that of Meelis Kiili from the Reform Party a day later left the coalition with 50 seats at the 101-seat Riigikogu; Kiili himself told Postimees that Kunnas would make a good candidate for the Defense Committee job.
Other important votes coming up include the presidential election ballots on September 2 and 3; there are 20 independent MPs at the Riigikogu now, making them a significant demographic within parliament – 68 or more votes are required to elect a head of state.
The original Postimees piece is here.

articles.title: UAE vessel attacked again in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.body:
UAE vessel attacked again in the Strait of Hormuz
Kyiv • UNN
An ADNOC vessel was hit in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a day after two other company vessels were attacked. The UAE condemned the attacks, calling them a threat to regional stability and global energy security.
The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) said that another one of its vessels had been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Gulf News reports, citing UNN.
Details
"On Friday evening, August 14, another vessel operated by the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) was struck in the Strait of Hormuz — just one day after two vessels linked to ADNOC were attacked in the same strait," the publication writes.
These incidents, occurring one after another, highlight the growing risks faced by commercial shipping when passing through this strategic chokepoint.
ADNOC confirmed that the vessel was struck while transiting the strait on Friday. No injuries were reported, and the company said the situation had been brought under control.
The UAE condemned what it called attacks on vessels linked to ADNOC and warned that attacks on commercial shipping pose a threat to regional stability and global energy security.
The country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that attacks on commercial vessels and attempts to obstruct movement along international sea routes violate United Nations Security Council Resolution No. 2817. It also emphasized the importance of freedom of navigation and maritime security.
Previously
The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) had stated the previous day that two of its vessels had been attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday evening.

articles.title: Russian drone attacks civilian car in Kherson Oblast, injuring four people
articles.body:
Russian drone attacks civilian car in Kherson Oblast, injuring four people
Russian forces attacked a civilian car with a drone on the road between the villages of Nova Kuban and Sahaidachne in the Beryslav district of Kherson Oblast on the morning of 15 August, injuring four people.
Source: Kherson Oblast Military Administration
Details: As a result of the attack, a 23-year-old man sustained shrapnel wounds to his head, arms and legs; a 48-year-old woman suffered leg injuries; a 68-year-old woman sustained a fractured shin; and another 43-year-old man suffered a head injury.
All four people were also diagnosed with concussion, blast injuries and closed traumatic brain injuries.
The injured people are in hospital and are receiving medical treatment.
Background: Over the previous day, 28 people were injured in Russian attacks in Kherson Oblast, including a child.

articles.title: Iran’s monthly oil production up 26,000 bpd: OPEC
articles.body:
Iran’s monthly oil production up 26,000 bpd: OPEC
TEHRAN- The latest report from the OPEC Secretariat, citing secondary sources, indicates that Iran's oil production in July 2026 reached 2,478,000 barrels per day, marking an increase of 26,000 barrels compared to June.
According to Shana, the August 2026 report of the OPEC Secretariat shows that Iran's oil production in July experienced an upward trend compared to June.
Based on data from OPEC secondary sources, Iran's oil production in July rose by 26,000 barrels to reach 2,478,000 barrels per day.
Iran had produced 2,451,000 barrels per day in June.
Saudi Arabia, with a daily production of 7,352,000 barrels, remains the top producer among OPEC members.
Iraq also ranks second with a daily production of 2,621,000 barrels.
Total crude oil production by OPEC members reached 23,632,000 barrels per day in July, an increase of 1,659,000 barrels compared to the previous month.
Meanwhile, total crude oil production by countries participating in the OPEC+ cooperation declaration reached 37,655,000 barrels per day in July 2026, showing a daily increase of 1,424,000 barrels compared to June.
In the prices section, the OPEC report indicates a decline in the price of Iran's heavy crude oil in July. The price of this type of oil fell from $90.77 in June to $82.07 per barrel in July.
The OPEC basket price also declined by $6.76 in the same month, reaching $82.99 per barrel.
In its new report, OPEC has forecast that global oil demand in 2026 will rise by about 0.6 million barrels per day, reaching 105.74 million barrels per day.
The outlook for next year is even more optimistic, with OPEC expecting global oil demand to increase by about 2.2 million barrels per day in 2027. This figure has also been revised upward in the new report compared to OPEC's previous estimate.
EF/MA

articles.title: Iran says Hormuz ‘will remain Iranian’ after Trump threats
articles.body:
This US Navy handout photograph shows a fighter jet taking off from aircraft carrier USS Abrams on Aug. 4. (AFP)
Iran on Aug. 15 rejected U.S. President Donald Trump’s statement that he would declare the Strait of Hormuz U.S. territory after defeating Tehran.
Trump told a rally at a police academy on Long Island a day earlier that he would “pretty soon” declare the waterway “a territory of the United States.”
He also claimed that Washington’s naval blockade gave it control over traffic through the strait. A White House official later said the territory remark had been made in jest.
“The Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian and will remain Iranian,” Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi wrote on X, adding that Tehran alone would decide whether the route was opened or closed.
The strait is bordered by Iran and Oman and is an international shipping route through which about a fifth of the world’s seaborne oil usually passes.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran had not decided whether to resume talks with Washington.
Messages relayed through Qatar and Pakistan did not constitute negotiations, he told Shahrara News.
Araghchi said separate discussions with Oman concerned a possible shipping route through the strait, while Washington would have to meet Tehran’s conditions before traffic could resume.
Two oil tankers operated by the United Arab Emirates’ state-owned ADNOC were attacked by drones while transiting the strait, the company said.
No injuries were reported, and the UAE blamed Iran for the attacks. Tehran did not immediately respond.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would announce new financial measures against Iran next week, threatening economic isolation “like the world has never seen before.”
The USS Abraham Lincoln is also set to be relieved by the USS George Washington after more than 250 days at sea. Trump dismissed concerns about conditions aboard the carrier, saying its deployment had been “not nearly long enough,” while Navy officials denied reports of a mental health crisis.

articles.title: With Iceland vote, EU dares dream of enlargement ‘success story’
articles.body:
With Iceland vote, EU dares dream of enlargement ‘success story’
- Iceland is voting on whether to reopen EU accession talks, aiming to boost its economy and security amid geopolitical concerns.
- Iceland is already closely linked to the EU through Schengen and the European Economic Area, making it a favourable candidate.
- Negotiations will focus on fishing quotas, especially mackerel, but the EU hopes to achieve a positive outcome despite challenges.
AI generated
BRUSSELS – No meddling, but fingers crossed: as Iceland votes on whether to resume entry talks with the European Union, Brussels is watching from afar in hope the outcome can deliver a rare enlargement “success story” for the bloc.
Residents of the small volcanic island in the north Atlantic have until Aug 29 to answer a simple question: “Should Iceland reopen accession negotiations with the EU?”
The country of 400,000 people has wrestled with the issue before: Iceland applied to join in 2009 after a financial crisis devastated its economy.
Brussels and Reykjavik spent years in painstaking negotiations, before Iceland ultimately shelved its application in 2015 with a simple letter.
Dream candidate
Then came Greenland.
US President Donald Trump’s threats to take control of the autonomous Danish territory have resonated strongly in neighbouring Iceland, which relies on the US and NATO for its defence.
The Icelandic authorities have since put EU membership back on the table, making the case that joining the 27-nation bloc would be beneficial in the current geopolitical context.
A referendum proposal was launched in the spring, not on membership per se, but simply at this stage on reopening talks.
A poll conducted by newspaper DV and published in late July put the “yes” camp ahead on about 53 per cent – enough to kindle hope in EU circles that Iceland may be back on track to join the fold.
“I think they want a success story” to reinvigorate the European project, said one Brussels-based source, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The bloc last expanded in 2013 when it admitted Croatia – its ranks briefly swelling to 28 member states until Britain’s Brexit vote to leave, which it did in 2020.
The years since have been marked by halting progress among EU candidates in the western Balkans, with Montenegro and Albania seen as closest in line to join, and the opening of a vast accession process with Ukraine.
For many European capitals, Iceland looks like something of a dream candidate.
More than 2,000km from Brussels as the crow flies, the island is already closely integrated with the EU.
It belongs to the Schengen free-travel area and also participates in the European Economic Area, meaning it already applies a large share of EU legislation.
Mackerel matters
But for all that, do not expect EU officials to jump on a plane to Reykjavik waving little European flags.
The Icelandic authorities are understood to have explicitly asked Brussels to keep a low profile during the campaign to avoid accusations of interference.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot is among the European officials who have visited Iceland in recent weeks. At a joint news conference with his Icelandic counterpart, he simply stressed Reykjavik had “nothing to lose” from negotiating with Brussels.
The same message has come from the European Commission.
“Should the Icelandic people decide to resume negotiations, the European Union stands ready to engage constructively and in a timely manner,” said commission spokesman Guillaume Mercier.
As for the negotiations themselves, several diplomats say they are likely to zero in on mackerel fishing quotas.
Brussels accuses Iceland of catching too much of the species, which has migrated northward as a result of climate change.
The fishing sector is crucial to the Icelandic economy, and Foreign Minister Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir has made clear Reykjavik would insist on “a good deal” on the issue.
There is no doubt that talks, if they get going again, will be tough.
But even so, the Brussels source remained optimistic: “I don’t think anyone wants to block an accession over a question of fish.” AFP

articles.title: Six people injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv region over past day
articles.body:
Six people injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv region over past day
Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, reported this on Facebook, according to Ukrinform.
"Over the past day, Kharkiv and 19 settlements in the Kharkiv region came under enemy attack. Six people were injured as a result of the shelling," the statement said.
In the city of Lozova, two men aged 33 and 34 sustained blast injuries, while a 40-year-old woman and a 48-year-old man suffered acute stress reactions. In the village of Pisky-Radkivski in the Borova community, a 60-year-old man was injured. In Kharkiv, a 33-year-old man suffered an acute stress reaction.
Russian forces actively used various types of weapons against the Kharkiv region, including four missiles, seven guided aerial bombs, two Lancet UAVs, three Molniya UAVs, one FPV drone and 52 UAVs whose type is still being determined.
According to the regional administration, civilian infrastructure facilities were damaged or destroyed. In Kharkiv, ten apartment buildings were damaged. In the Bohodukhiv district, two warehouses, 50 tonnes of grain, a grain-cleaning machine in Murafa, three private houses, two outbuildings and a church in Krasivka, as well as two private houses, two outbuildings and two vehicles in Zolochiv, were damaged.
In the Kupiansk district, a private house was damaged in Velykyi Burluk.
In the Izium district, a preschool in Balakliia, a private house in Komarivka, a farm and an elevator in Buhaiivka were damaged, and livestock was affected.
In the Kharkiv district, a shopping center in Mala Danylivka and a private house in Ruski Tyshky were damaged.
In the Lozova district, a warehouse in Blyzniuky, an outbuilding in Lozova, two vehicles in Batiushky, a private house in Vesele and a wheat field in Orilka were damaged.
In the Chuhuiv district, a vehicle in Shestakove, as well as two buildings and two outbuildings in Vodiakhivka, were damaged.
Syniehubov said the transit evacuation center in Lozova received 275 people over the past day. A total of 52,539 people have been registered at the center since it began operating.

articles.title: Massive missile strike hits Samara Region, causing casualties — city mayor
articles.body:
SAMARA, August 15. /TASS/. A massive missile attack hit Russia's Samara Region, causing casualties, the city's mayor, Ivan Noskov, reported on his Max social media channel.
"This morning, air defense forces repelled a massive enemy missile attack on the Samara Region. Localized damage was caused to Samara's industrial infrastructure. <…> Medical assistance has been provided to the injured," he noted.
Noskov added that a crisis management center has been set up at the scene. "I am working on site alongside the enterprise's management and emergency services," he said.
The mayor emphasized that publishing photos and videos of the aftermath of the attacks is strictly prohibited. "Such publications help the enemy coordinate actions to inflict maximum damage on civilians and civilian infrastructure. Please remain calm and rely only on official information sources," he wrote.

articles.body:
'Transparent examination will be ensured': CM Hemant Soren to protesting Jharkhand students
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 15, 2026, 13:03 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
Soren reaches out to protesting students, vows changes in exam system
NEW DELHI: Amid a three-week-long protest by students demanding the cancellation of flawed examinations, Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Saturday assured that his government would bring changes to the examination system and ensure greater transparency, particularly in tests conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).Addressing a gathering at a state-level Independence Day celebration, Soren said the concerns and aspirations of the state's youth were important to his government and urged them to have faith in the steps being taken to reform the system."For me, the youth of the state are very important to me and their faith in us. We have decided to bring changes in the system. Transparent examination will be ensured," Soren said.The chief minister said the government had launched "Chhatron Ki Baat - Chhatron Ke Sath" to seek students' views on improving the education system. He said students, along with their parents and teachers, could play an important role in shaping a better education system."We will not indulge in a blame game but ensure justice. We are making changes in the system. We will come out with the academic calendar and take steps for transparency (in) exams.
We have started Chhatron Ki Baat - Chhatron Ke Sath, and I want the parents of students and their teachers to give suggestions, and we will examine them with experts and bring them as per rules and constitutional norms," Soren said.
‘Talent will not be allowed to go to waste due to mafia’
Soren also sought to reassure young aspirants that their careers and ambitions would not be derailed by irregularities or alleged examination-related malpractice. He promised that the government would work to prevent talented candidates from losing out because of a serious challenge posed by the "mafia"."I want to urge the youth that their dreams will be protected. I want to assure that talent will not be allowed to go to waste due to the mafia. This is a serious challenge before the nation. For me, the youth of the state are very important to me and their faith on us. We have decided to bring changes in the system. Transparent examination will be ensured," Soren said.
Earlier on Saturday, student leader Ravinder Paswan said the protesting students would keep their demands aside for Independence Day and instead participate in celebrations centred on the country and nationalism."Today is the 80th Independence Day. We extend our heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for Independence Day to all the students, youth, general public, and social justice advocates across the country on this occassion. We are organising a grand Tiranga Yatra to mark Independence Day. Students and young people from across Jharkhand are participating in this Tiranga Yatra to display their love for the country and their nationalism," he said.Students in Jharkhand have been protesting over irregularities in examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC. Among their key demands is the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination.
