articles.title: Hurricane poised to hit Hawaii as El Nino stirs Pacific
articles.body:
Hurricane poised to hit Hawaii as El Nino stirs Pacific
- Tropical storm Lala is strengthening and expected to hit Hawaii's Big Island with hurricane-force winds, heavy rain, and storm surge, prompting a state of emergency.
- Authorities urge residents to prepare by clearing debris, securing property, and avoiding dangerous coastal areas as rough weather persists.
- A strong El Nino in the Pacific is increasing hurricane risks, with climate change potentially amplifying extreme weather impacts across the region.
AI generated
HONOLULU - A strengthening tropical storm named Lala is set to hit Hawaii’s Big Island with hurricane force gales on Aug 15, bringing dangerous winds, rainfall and heavy surf.
The governor of the US Pacific island state declared a state of emergency as the storm barrelled towards the archipelago, packing winds that could gust up to 137kmh.
A hurricane warning was in effect for Hawaii County, which covers the Big Island, and a tropical storm warning held for the islands of Maui, Molokai and Kahoolawe to its north-west. Lower grade tropical storm watches were in place for other islands.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said rainfall of up to 30cm was expected across Maui and the Big Island, with up to 63cm in certain pockets of the latter, and storm surge of 30-90cm.
Rough conditions could persist into Aug 16.
Governor Josh Green proclaimed a state of emergency to ensure the state and its counties “have sufficient resources to clear debris, secure infrastructure, and take other measures to prepare”.
Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi said his adminstration had spent days preparing the area for the impact of the storm, and urged residents to be ready.
“I am asking everyone to finish your preparations today. Don’t wait for the weather to deteriorate,” he said on Aug 14.
“Stay informed, stay away from dangerous areas, and make sure your family knows what to do if conditions worsen.”
Hawaii’s emergency management agency recommended residents clear gutters and drains and move valuables off the ground, seal gaps in doors and remove tree limbs that threaten their properties.
“Stay away from beaches and coastal areas where rough surf and rip currents could sweep you away,” it added.
Hawaii was menaced by Hurricane Fausto last month, before the storm weakened and skirted north of the island chain.
The state was last hit by a “major” hurricane – meaning Category 3, 4, or 5 on the Saffir-Simpson scale – in 1992, when Hurricane Iniki caused at least six deaths and billions of dollars in damage.
The storm comes as a powerful El Nino has formed in the central equatorial Pacific Ocean, with temperatures already so high that NOAA now predicts a 69 per cent chance of a “historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Nino events dating back to 1950” when it peaks between October and December.
El Nino, a natural climate pattern when sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, tends to promote hurricane activity in the Pacific while suppressing it in the Atlantic.
Human-caused climate change can amplify El Nino’s impacts because a warmer ocean and atmosphere increase the availability of energy and moisture for extreme weather events, such as heat waves and heavy rainfall. AFP

articles.title: IRGC downs US-made MQ-9 drone over Iran's Hormozgan prov.
articles.body:
The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps' Public Relations Department said in a brief statement on Friday that the IRGC's new advanced defense system intercepted and destroyed an MQ-9 Reaper drone in the skies of southern Iranian province of Hormozgan, under the control of the country's integrated air defense network.
This came a day after the Washington Post reported that the United States has lost 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones since launching its war of aggression against Iran, with Iranian air defenses bringing down roughly a quarter of the US fleet and exposing the vulnerability of one of Washington’s key surveillance and strike platforms.
According to the report, the losses could cost US taxpayers more than $1.3 billion, with each Reaper estimated to be worth between $30 million and $50 million, depending on its configuration.
When the war began on February 28, the US had approximately 185 Reapers, including 165 operated by the Air Force and 20 by the Marine Corps.
Iranian air defenses accounted for a substantial share of the losses, highlighting the difficulty faced by the US military in protecting its costly drones while operating over Iranian territory.
The attrition is particularly significant because the MQ-9 Reaper is a central component of US intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance operations, as well as precision strikes. Its ability to operate without risking a pilot has made it a preferred platform for missions over heavily defended territory.
The latest round of US-Israeli attacks on Iran began on February 28, prompting Tehran to launch daily missile and drone strikes against US and Israeli military targets in the region before Tehran and Washington signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on June 17.

articles.title: Earthquake hits Spanish city of Granada, damages buildings and cars
articles.body:
Earthquake hits Spanish city of Granada, damages buildings and cars
MADRID - An earthquake of magnitude 5 struck the southern Spanish city of Granada in the early hours of Aug 15, with the regional government saying houses and cars were damaged but no injuries had been reported.
The earthquake hit the metropolitan area of Alhendin just after 1am local time.
Spanish television channel TVE showed debris strewn on the street and some damage to cars in the popular tourist city.
Andalusian emergency services rescued a number of people from damaged buildings.
Antonio Sanz Cabello, vice-president of the Andalusian regional government, said in a post on X on Aug 15 that authorities had declared an emergency.
“If you’re in Granada, you’ve felt the earthquake, you’re okay, and your home shows no damage, stay calm and avoid entering and exiting buildings unnecessarily,” he said.
“On the street, stay away from facades, cornices, balconies, walls, and other elements that could fall.” REUTERS

articles.title: Air defense neutralizes 124 drones, three Banderol munitions used by Russia to attack Ukraine overnight
articles.body:
Air defense neutralizes 124 drones, three Banderol munitions used by Russia to attack Ukraine overnight
The Ukrainian Air Force reported this on Telegram, according to Ukrinform.
Starting at 18:00 on August 14, Russian forces attacked Ukraine with 152 strike UAVs, among them Shahed-type drones, including jet-powered variants, Gerbera drones, Banderol loitering munitions and Parodiya-type decoy drones. The drones were launched from Kursk, Oryol, Millerovo and Primorsko-Akhtarsk in Russia, as well as temporarily occupied Donetsk.
The attack was repelled by Ukrainian combat aircraft, surface-to-air missile units, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of the Ukrainian Defense Forces.
According to preliminary data, as of 09:00 on August 15, air defenses had shot down or suppressed 124 drones and three Banderol munitions over northern, southern and eastern Ukraine.
Hits were recorded at 16 locations, while debris from downed targets fell at one location.
The attack is ongoing, with several enemy drones still in Ukrainian airspace.

articles.title: EDF in so-called gap year but active-duty personnel training still not underway
articles.body:
EDF in so-called gap year but active-duty personnel training still not underway
The Estonian Defense Forces accepted several times fewer conscripts this year to allow active-duty personnel to focus on further training and professional development. However, such activities have yet to begin.
2026 is a so-called gap year for the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF). While around 4,000 conscripts were previously taken into service each year, in 2026 that number is just 1,200, with many of them being young people who intend to pursue a career with the Defense Forces.
The aim is to give active-duty personnel an opportunity to undergo more extensive further training and professional development.
However, according to the Defense Forces, the intensive period of further training is only now getting underway, as all conscripts who began their service last year have now been transferred to the reserve.
"In terms of the training courses being redesigned, changes to the soldiers' basic training course have now been prepared, as have instructors who will introduce the updated course curriculum and training methods in units. To this end, instructors' training levels have been standardized and the way further training will be conducted has been established," the Defense Forces told ERR.
Broadly speaking, the EDF is focusing its training on three areas: improving soldiers' basic skills, counter-drone training and firearms training.
Basic skills refers to helping each soldier, figuratively speaking, stay alive longer — in other words, protecting personnel, weapons and equipment from detection and the effects of enemy weapons. Both drone and firearms training involve the latest expertise, which is constantly evolving in light of developments in the war in Ukraine.
Although the number of conscripts is more than three times lower than usual, the reduction has not been evenly distributed. Some units simply require the same number of conscripts to operate, meaning this year is much the same as any other for them.
With the Defense Forces hoping to take in 4,100 conscripts next year, more than in previous years, how does it plan to find enough people?
Each year, the Defense Resources Agency (KRA) assesses the health of nearly 10,000 young people between the ages of 18 and 27. To meet the target of 4,100 conscripts in 2027, the agency is focusing intensively on those who have not yet entered service.
"It is not yet known how many of the young people who did not enter conscript service this year will receive a deferment. We will only be able to assess that once school admissions have concluded and we know how many young people will continue their studies and apply for deferment. Those who do not begin their studies and have no other grounds for postponing conscript service will be assigned to service in 2027," KRA Marketing and Communications Director Daisi Želizko-Kask said.
The agency currently believes that calling up around 4,000 conscripts a year will remain realistic until 2040, when the effects of the earlier low birth rate among boys will begin to have a significant impact.
However, according to KRA, the gap year has not affected the number of active-duty personnel.
--
Editor: Märten Hallismaa, Marcus Turovski

articles.title: Polish politician claims there are "illegal excavations" taking place in Ukraine
articles.body:
Polish politician claims there are "illegal excavations" taking place in Ukraine
Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland's Law and Justice (PiS) party, has claimed that illegal excavations are allegedly being conducted at the sites of former Polish villages in Ukraine.
Source: Onet, as reported by European Pravda
Details: Kaczyński claimed that "illegal excavations" are taking place in the historical and geographical region in the west of Ukraine that Poland referred to as "Eastern Galicia".
"Illegal excavations at the sites of former Polish villages in Eastern Galicia are indeed taking place," he said.
Kaczyński claims that "disrespect for the remains of the dead and the looting of victims' valuables (...) by so-called 'black diggers' for financial gain is reportedly taking place with the tacit consent of the local Ukrainian authorities".
He said that his party would appeal "to the most important state authorities of the Republic of Poland, in particular the Ministry of Foreign Affairs".
"We will demand explanations and a response to this criminal activity," he said.
However, it is currently unclear which specific cases or incidents Kaczyński was referring to.
Background:
- On 7 August, Poland's Institute of National Remembrance announced the completion of exhumation works involving victims of the Volyn tragedy in two former villages in Volyn. [The Volyn (Volhynia) tragedy is a series of events that led to the ethnic cleansing of the Polish and Ukrainian populations in 1943. The tragedy was part of a long-standing rivalry between Ukrainians and Poles in what is now Ukraine's west.]
- Last year, after a several-year hiatus, Ukraine restored the possibility of conducting searches and exhumations of Polish victims on its territory. Since then, victims of the tragic events of the 20th century in Puzhnyky have been exhumed and reburied, as have the remains of Polish soldiers killed during the September Campaign of 1939.

articles.title: Japanese politicians' offerings, visits to war-linked Yasukuni Shrine draw opposition from peace advocates
articles.body:
TOKYO, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a ritual offering to the notorious Yasukuni Shrine, a symbol of Japanese militarism and wartime aggression, on Saturday, while several cabinet ministers and senior politicians paid visits to the controversial shrine, triggering strong criticism from peace advocates in Japan.
On the 81st anniversary of Japan's unconditional surrender in World War II, Takaichi made a "tamagushi" ritual offering to the war-linked shrine in her capacity as president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
Meanwhile, Minister of Defense Shinjiro Koizumi, Minister of State for Regional Revitalization Hitoshi Kikawada, Minister of State for Economic Security Kimi Onoda, and Minister of State for Economic and Fiscal Policy Minoru Kiuchi visited the shrine.
According to Japanese media reports, Koizumi became the first incumbent defense minister to visit Yasukuni Shrine on Aug. 15 since then Defense Minister Minoru Kihara did so in 2024. It also marked the seventh consecutive year that serving cabinet members have visited the shrine on the anniversary of Japan's surrender.
Senior executives of the LDP -- Secretary-General Shunichi Suzuki, General Council Chairperson Haruko Arimura, and Election Strategy Committee Chairperson Yasutoshi Nishimura -- visited the shrine together on Saturday. Japanese media described the joint visit by multiple senior party leaders as an unusual occurrence.
The actions were met with strong opposition from Japanese peace activists and scholars.
Atsushi Kouketsu, emeritus professor at Yamaguchi University, told Xinhua that Yasukuni Shrine is "a shrine of aggression" and a breeding ground for militarist ideology. He said Takaichi, who has visited the shrine on multiple occasions in the past, sent a dangerous political signal by making the ritual offering as LDP president, signaling the ruling establishment's endorsement of the ideological roots of Japan's past wars of aggression.
This reflects a further rightward shift in Japanese politics that warrants a high level of vigilance, Kouketsu said.
The Aichi Prefectural Peace Committee stated that the visits by Koizumi and other politicians to Yasukuni Shrine, which glorifies Japan's wars of aggression, desecrate the memory of those who died in the war. The committee urged Japanese political leaders to face up to Japan's responsibility for its wartime aggression.
Yasukuni Shrine, located in central Tokyo's Chiyoda Ward, honors 14 convicted Class-A Japanese war criminals from World War II. For a long time, visits and ritual offerings made by Japanese officials to the controversial shrine have consistently sparked criticism and opposition both at home and abroad, hurting the feelings of the people of China, South Korea, and other countries and regions brutalized by Japan during the war. ■

articles.title: China lodges protests against Japan's negative moves related to Yasukuni Shrine
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- China strongly deplores Japan's negative moves related to the Yasukuni war shrine, and has lodged serious protests against Japan, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Saturday.
The spokesperson made the remarks after Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi made a monetary offering to the Yasukuni Shrine on Aug. 15, which marks the day of Japan's unconditional surrender in the Second World War, and certain cabinet members also visited the shrine.
During WWII, Japan launched the war of aggression and committed horrendous crimes, the spokesperson said, noting that as spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism, the Yasukuni Shrine is in fact a shrine for war criminals, as it honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals responsible for the war of aggression.
No pretext whatsoever can hide the Japanese politicians' true intention, which is to change the verdict on the war criminals, cover up Japan's war crimes, distort the historical facts, and pave the way for accelerating remilitarization, the spokesperson said.
"This is an affront to historical justice, a challenge to the foundational norms of civilization, and a provocation against the postwar international order. Such behaviors have been firmly rejected by the overwhelming majority of the international community," the spokesperson said.
Noting this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, the spokesperson said to view and treat history correctly is an important prerequisite for Japan's postwar return to the international community, the political foundation for Japan's ties with neighboring countries, and more importantly, a key measure for Japan's commitment to peaceful development.
"We urge the Japanese side to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions," the spokesperson said. ■

articles.title: U.S. regulators upgrade recall of 19 mln eggs to highest risk level
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- U.S. food safety regulators have upgraded a recall of about 19 million eggs to its highest risk category over potential salmonella contamination.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Wednesday classified the recall that started last month as Class I, its highest recall classification. The agency said the designation is used when there is a reasonable probability that exposure to a recalled product could cause "serious adverse health consequences or death."
Midwest Poultry Services initiated the voluntary recall on July 22 after samples collected at its farms in Texas tested positive for salmonella. The recall covers some 1.6 million cartons of eggs, or about 19.1 million individual eggs, according to the FDA.
The recalled eggs were produced between June 6 and July 3, and were available to consumers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas, it said.
It noted that Midwest Poultry Services was not linked to all illnesses in the outbreak and that the investigation remains ongoing.
Nearly 100 salmonella cases were reported in 17 states from Nov. 21, 2025, through June 30, 2026, the FDA said last month. There had been 26 hospitalizations as of July 24, with no deaths reported, it said. ■

articles.title: Contractors suspended over ‘extremely serious’ Queen Mary Hospital lift defects
articles.body:
Contractors suspended over ‘extremely serious’ Queen Mary Hospital lift defects
Authorities say 24 of 28 lifts in the new clinical block were affected, delaying the launch of clinical services until repairs are completed
Hong Kong authorities have suspended the main contractor and lift subcontractor working on a new clinical block at Queen Mary Hospital from public works tenders after serious defects left most lifts unreliable and delayed the launch of services.
The Architectural Services Department said in a social media post late on Friday that the contractors’ poor performance had been recorded in assessment reports.
It added that the firms would be required to bear the full cost of remedial works and could face claims for losses arising from delays to the HK$15.15 billion (US$1.93 billion) redevelopment project at the Pok Fu Lam hospital.
“In accordance with contractual mechanisms, we have also reflected the contractor’s and works subcontractor’s poor performance on the project in their assessment reports and suspended their eligibility to tender for public works contracts,” the department said.
The main contractor for the first phase of the redevelopment was the Paul Y-Able Joint Venture. The lift subcontractor, Anlev Elex Elevator, is a subsidiary of ATAL Engineering Group, founded by Otto Poon Lok-to, the husband of former justice secretary Teresa Cheng Yeuk-wah.
The department said damaged electronic components, faulty wiring connections and poor installation workmanship were among the problems affecting 24 of the 28 newly installed lifts in Clinical Block 1.

articles.title: Myanmar approves 14 new investment projects, creating 3,336 jobs
articles.body:
YANGON, Aug. 15 (Xinhua) -- The Myanmar Investment Commission (MIC) has approved 14 new investment projects, the state-owned daily The Global New Light of Myanmar reported on Saturday.
At a meeting on Friday in Nay Pyi Taw, the MIC approved two new foreign investment projects from the capital increase of ongoing investments and 12 new local investment projects in the industrial, service, electricity and housing sectors, the report said.
Total investment is valued at 140.474 million U.S. dollars for foreign investments and over 1.1787 trillion kyats (about 561.3 million U.S. dollars) for local projects, and the projects are expected to create 3,336 jobs, it said.
The MIC oversees and approves investment project proposals from local and foreign investors and provides services to existing investors under the Myanmar Investment Law, it added. ■

articles.title: Urgent: 7 killed, 3 wounded in Israeli strike on S. Lebanon
articles.body:
A man inspects the damage after an Israeli airstrike on the outskirts of Ansar in the southern Nabatieh Governorate, Lebanon, Aug. 15, 2026. articles.title: Magnitude 5.0 earthquake strikes near Granada, Spain
articles.body:
MADRID, August 15. /TASS/. A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck near the Spanish city of Granada in the autonomous community of Andalusia, the kingdom's National Geographic Institute reported.
According to the institute, the earthquake was recorded at around 1:00 a.m. local time (11:00 p.m. GMT, August 14), with its focus at a depth of 2 kilometers. The epicenter was located near the town of Alendin.
Regional authorities reported that emergency services received approximately 200 calls. No casualties have been reported so far. However, the earthquake caused structural damage across the area. According to the Andalusian government, residents reported cracks in structures, minor collapses--including walls and cornices--and damage to several buildings. In response, authorities have activated the emergency phase of the regional seismic action plan.

articles.title: Forest fire in Croatia claimed one life and injured around 40 people
articles.body:
Forest fire in Croatia claimed one life and injured around 40 people
Kyiv • UNN
A forest fire in Croatia has engulfed the coast, claiming one life and injuring around 40 people. More than 1,200 people have been evacuated, and 10 are in intensive care.
At least one person was killed and around 40 others were injured as a result of a major wildfire that engulfed towns on Croatia’s coast on Thursday evening and Friday morning, UNN reports, citing the BBC.
Details
The fire broke out near the village of Lokva Rogoznica on Thursday evening and quickly spread toward the nearby tourist town of Omiš, 6 km away.
Around 1,200 residents and tourists were evacuated, while 10 people are in intensive care in hospital, Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković said. Croatia’s fire chief, Slavko Tucaković, called it "one of the worst" fires in the country’s history.
Croatia is one of several European countries affected by devastating wildfires following a summer of extreme heat and drought.
Villages near the Adriatic city of Split were affected by flames that swept across a hillside lined with pine forest, causing significant damage to homes and cars.
Tucaković said the firestorm had burned "everything in its path", as officials confirmed that flames fanned by strong winds had engulfed 1,000 hectares in just four hours.
More than 300 firefighters were deployed on Thursday night, and crews were sometimes forced to retreat as the fire advanced.
Some people were forced to jump into the sea from boats to escape the fire.
Shelters were opened in several towns along the coast, while the evacuation continued throughout the night.
On Friday, officials confirmed that a body had been found in the burned area, while emergency services continued searching the affected zones.
Later on Friday, Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković visited the affected area, where he praised the work of the rescuers. The fire spread "with lightning speed" and amid "gale-force winds", he told reporters, adding that what the firefighters had managed to save was "a real miracle".
The commander of the Omiš volunteer fire brigade, Višeslav Pešić, told Reuters that the flames were so intense that people abandoned their vehicles "right in the fire zone", making it difficult for rescuers to pass through.
According to Index.hr, a major fire also broke out on Croatia’s Dugi Otok island the previous day; it spread rapidly because of strong winds and engulfed hard-to-reach terrain covered with dense undergrowth.
In some places, the fire even reached the road, and these dramatic scenes were filmed by firefighters and local residents.
Firefighters battled the blaze throughout the night and actively protected homes and cottages scattered around the bays. The fire had still not been brought under control by morning, while efforts to extinguish it were further complicated by the steep, inaccessible terrain and dense vegetation.
Update
Firefighters across Europe are facing immense pressure and strain on resources as major wildfires continue to rage across the continent, fuelled by extreme heat.
In the town of Agios Vasileios in Greece, more than 200 people were evacuated by boat from a beach resort as wildfires raged across the country, while more than 500 residents were forced to leave their homes because of a fire in the south-western region of Landa, near an area that had already been devastated by wildfires.
More than 2,000 people were also evacuated from the village of Gey in western Germany after a wildfire spread to the village near the border with Belgium.
Meanwhile, on Friday, millions of people in England and Wales were sent an emergency wildfire alert warning of a "very high risk" of wildfires in the country, as firefighters continue to battle numerous blazes in the West Midlands.

articles.title: Ukrainian missiles attack Russian region – governor
articles.body:
Ukrainian missiles attack Russian region – governor
An industrial facility in Russia’s Samara Region was attacked by Ukrainian missiles, local governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said.
Emergency services have been deployed on site, Fedorishchev wrote in a Saturday morning post on Max.
The information regarding damage and casualties is currently being verified, he added.
In the Rostov Region, around 1,000 residents of seven villages were left without electricity after a Ukrainian drone damaged powerlines in the area, according to local governor Yury Slusar.
Around a dozen UAVs and three missiles were destroyed by air defenses in the region overnight, Slusar said. There have been no reports of injuries, he added.
Ukraine has several types of long-range missiles in their arsenal, including British-supplied Storm Shadow and homemade Flamingo munitions.
Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin wrote on Max that at least 16 incoming drones were shot down on the approach to the Russian capital during the night.
In the town of Shatura in Moscow Region, a UAV hit a private home, injuring a 9-year-old boy and a 55-year-old woman, local governor Vyacheslav Vorobyeb wrote on Telegram. The child was hospitalized in serious condition, he added.
The Russian Defense Ministry said that a total of 598 Ukrainian UAVs were shot down or intercepted by electronic warfare means above 20 of the country's regions overnight.
Moscow has condemned Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia’s civilian infrastructure and residential areas as terrorist attacks aimed at compensating for Kiev’s setbacks on the battlefield, where Russian forces continue their steady advance.
Russia has responded by intensifying long-range missile and drone strikes against Ukraine’s military-industrial facilities and logistics infrastructure. Moscow maintains that it does not target civilians and that its strikes are directed solely at military targets and infrastructure supporting Kiev’s forces.
The Defense Ministry in Moscow said on Friday that a total of 14 such strikes had been launched over the previous week, hitting drone production plants, weapons, and logistics centers, as well as fuel, energy, and transport infrastructure. Military airfields and ports where cargo used by Kiev’s troops are unloaded and stored have also been targeted.
The Russian military also struck 15 oceangoing vessels operating in the interests of the Ukrainian military, including a tanker, seven dry cargo ships, two tugboats, and five patrol boats, it added.

articles.body:
‘Sure sign of his desperation’: Congress hits back at PM Modi over ‘dimaagi Naxals’ remark
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 15, 2026, 13:44 IST

File photo: PM Modi and Congress MP Jairam Ramesh
NEW DELHI: Congress on Saturday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his Independence Day remarks on "dimaagi Naxals", with party general secretary Jairam Ramesh calling the description a "sure sign of desperation".Ramesh said PM Modi had earlier used the term "urban Naxals" for his opponents and was now referring to them as "dimaagi Naxals"."First he called his opponents 'urban naxals'. Now he calls them 'dimaagi naxals'. It is a sure sign of his desperation," Ramesh said in a post on X.
He further alleged that the prime minister ends up doing what those he labels "urban naxals" or "dimaagi naxals" demand or advocate."It is not for nothing that the PM has a MA being the 'Master Abuser' in Entire Political Science that he is," Ramesh added.
PM Modi warns against ‘intellectual Naxals’
PM Modi raised the issue during his 13th consecutive Independence Day address from the Red Fort, saying that while armed Naxalism had been eliminated from large parts of the country, its ideological influence remained a concern."We have succeeded in getting rid of armed Naxals in the jungles, but the 'dimaagi Naxals' are looking for opportunities to create violence, unrest.... They want to drag the society on the wrong path," the prime minister said.
"These intellectual Naxals have to be identified and isolated," he added.
PM Modi also said people with a Maoist mindset had for years established themselves in government institutions and influenced public policy.He said decades of Naxalism and Maoist violence had destroyed the lives and aspirations of millions of young people.The prime minister said more than 3,500 police and security personnel had been killed in the conflict and claimed that his government had made ending Naxalism a priority after taking office in 2014.
Congress attacks government on Independence Day
Ramesh's response came as Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also criticised the PM Modi government during Independence Day celebrations at the party headquarters in Delhi.Kharge accused the government of failing to deliver fundamental rights, avoiding parliamentary accountability and pursuing divisive politics. He also challenged PM Modi's claims of transformation, crediting previous Congress-led governments with initiatives including the Right to Food, Right to Education and the Right to Work through MGNREGA.
"From the Red Fort, the PM claims credit for everything; it is a mercy he doesn't claim that the world survives only because of him," Kharge said.He also accused the government of using "hate campaigns" against protesters and alleged that it was "crushing the poor".For Congress, Kharge said, freedom meant ensuring education, opportunities and dignity rather than merely holding political power.The BJP, meanwhile, attacked leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi for not attending the official Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that Gandhi's absence reflected the mindset of a "Dimagi Naxal" ecosystem.

articles.title: Dormition of the Mother of God – one of the major Christian feasts of the year
articles.body:
News
Dormition of the Mother of God – one of the major Christian feasts of the year
Saturday 15 August 2026 08:20
Saturday, 15 August 2026, 08:20
PHOTO BTA
Font size
The Bulgarian Orthodox Church marks the Dormition of the Most Holy Mother of God (The Assumption of Mary), one of the twelve major Christian feasts. According to Holy Scripture, this is the day when the Mother of God leaves her earthly life and joins her Son.
In Bulgarian folk tradition, the feast is known as Golyama Bogoroditsa (Great St. Mary’s Day). Malka Bogoroditsa is the day commemorating the birth of the Mother of Christ.
The Dormition of the Most Holy Mother of God at Bachkovo Monastery
PHOTO BTA
The Dormition of the Mother of God is marked by solemn services in Orthodox churches across the country. Traditionally, thousands of worshippers gather at the Bachkovo Monastery to pray before the miraculous icon of the Mother of God, which is believed to hear the prayers of the faithful, bring healing, and help women who come to pray for a child.
Believers seek the protection of the Holy Mother of God in times of hardship and life’s challenges. On this day, family gatherings are also traditionally held accompanied by a kurban- a ritual offering for life, health, a fruitful year, and protection from misfortune and illness.
Traditional dishes served on Golyama Bogoroditsa (Great St. Mary’s Day) include freshly baked, ornamented pita bread, chicken stew, boiled wheat, corn, and pumpkin. The feast day also marks the first tasting of the new grape harvest. Worshippers traditionally donate candles, handwoven cloth, towels and money to the church.
On August 15, people named Maria, Mariana, Mariela, Marieta, Marin, Mario, Panayot, Preslava, and others celebrate their name day.

articles.title: Estonia's traffic deaths up compared to the same period last year
articles.body:
Estonia's traffic deaths up compared to the same period last year
Although the total number of serious traffic accidents and injuries declined in the first seven months of this year, 30 people have lost their lives on Estonia's roads and streets, four more than during the same period last year.
Estonia's road safety picture has been mixed this year. According to preliminary police data, 55 fewer people have been injured in traffic accidents than last year, while the number of fatalities has moved in the opposite direction, with four more deaths than last year, Transport Administration traffic expert Villu Vane said.
Compared with the Nordic countries and other European countries, Estonia's rate of road deaths per million inhabitants remains too high. According to a 2024 Europe-wide study, most European countries, including Norway, Denmark and Germany, had fewer traffic fatalities per million inhabitants than Estonia. With 50 deaths per million inhabitants, Estonia was also well above the European average of 44. Estonia's improvement in road safety over a 10-year period was also modest, at just 12 percent.
Vane said the root causes of the high number of fatalities lie in road users' habits and attitudes.
"This probably reflects our behavior in traffic, which isn't always what it should be and perhaps also reflects our attitudes toward things like obeying speed limits. It illustrates how we behave on the road," Vane said.
According to Vane, the situation has improved compared with 10 or 20 years ago. Seat belt use, for example, has become the norm, but there has been no comparable progress when it comes to speeding.
"If we look back, it took a little while for people to get used to wearing seat belts, but we've accepted it now. The overall picture is relatively good, with 99 percent of drivers and passengers in the front seats wearing seat belts, or 98 percent in some years. Unfortunately, when we look at fatal accidents, every year several people die in crashes because they weren't wearing a seat belt," Vane said.
When it comes to speeding, Vane said there has been improvement over the longer term, but Estonia has made little progress in recent years.
"One year we take half a step forward and the next year we take a step back," he said, describing the situation on Estonia's roads.
Vane said it is still too early to say what effect recent legislative changes — which introduced warning signs ahead of mobile speed cameras and lowered the speeding threshold at which fines are issued — have had on road safety.
"First of all, it's still relatively early to say because the signs were only recently installed ahead of mobile cameras — signs have been in place for fixed cameras for a long time. I think the impact so far has been relatively negligible. But there's always the question of whether the sign really needs to be there," Vane said.
Vane cited the legacy of the past as one reason for poor behavior on the roads. Asked what shapes the attitudes of young people who have grown up in Estonia since the country regained independence, Vane pointed to the influence of role models and their surroundings.
"It's probably the traffic environment and what they see, as well as how people behave at home. There are quite a lot of factors at play here," he said.
Elderly the most at-risk group in traffic
Looking at the profile of those killed, Vane highlighted two main risk groups. "Quite often, the road user is elderly, while young men also continue to account for a high proportion of fatalities," Vane said.
Asked who the typical person responsible for a traffic accident is, Vane said he could not give a clear answer. "We haven't specifically profiled them and it varies widely," he added.
According to 2024 European Union statistics, the most vulnerable age groups are people ages 25 to 49 and those over 65, each accounting for 31 percent. Men predominate both among those responsible for traffic accidents and among victims. The difference between the number of male and female victims is smallest among pedestrians.
Although Tallinn's traffic strategy calls for reducing road deaths to zero, there have already been several traffic fatalities in the city this year. What is Tallinn doing wrong?
Vane said the city may not necessarily be doing anything wrong as such, but the traffic environment has not been made safe everywhere and there are still places where improvements could be made.
"In cities in particular, speeds could be reduced in areas where pedestrians are present. Unfortunately, there are also fatal accidents where it's difficult to do much to prevent them. One possible example — we don't know for sure yet — is the most recent fatality in Tallinn where a person was struck by a car while directing traffic. There is a possibility that the driver suffered a medical emergency at the wheel," Vane said.
"Accidents that occur while vehicles are reversing are also relatively difficult to prevent, although there are measures that can be taken in certain cases. When it comes to freight transport, traffic arrangements can be designed so that vehicles only have to reverse short distances and pedestrians don't inadvertently enter those areas," Vane said.
People who shouldn't be driving
Speaking about medical conditions and medical certificates, Vane pointed to gaps in the system and its oversight.
"A person's health changes over time. People can develop illnesses while their medical certificate is still valid, but as I understand it, if someone develops a condition that means they are no longer allowed to drive, their medical certificate is not currently revoked automatically. That means someone can become ill and be told they must not drive, but still get behind the wheel. That's clearly dangerous," Vane said.
Doctors' decisions are also influenced by the social realities of rural areas and the availability of public transportation.
"Whether a doctor renews a medical certificate also depends on where the person lives and how accessible basic services are — whether they can take a bus to the store and back in a reasonable amount of time or whether there is no bus service at all. In that case, how are they supposed to get to a store 10 kilometers or even farther away? Unfortunately, a rural doctor may sometimes turn a blind eye and issue the certificate so the person can at least manage their day-to-day life somehow," Vane said.
Solutions: Enforcement and safer living environment
Vane said reducing traffic fatalities and improving road safety culture requires more than isolated technological solutions, with consistent work needed in three main areas.
"We need to continue doing what we've been doing. That means making the traffic environment safer as much as possible, particularly for pedestrians, and we probably also need to continue with prevention campaigns to some extent. Their impact may not be very large, but over time they do have an effect and probably influence certain groups in society. Police enforcement is, of course, another essential element. If there is no enforcement, things aren't going to improve. If drivers sense that there are certain violations the police don't respond to or don't have the resources to respond to, some drivers will start taking advantage of that," Vane said.
Vane also noted that under the implementation plan for Estonia's national road safety program, one important measure is lowering speed limits in built-up areas, which directly improves pedestrians' chances of surviving a collision.
Vane said traffic conditions in municipalities are largely determined by political decisions made by local authorities, although the state can still set the overall direction.
"The state can do that through the road safety program's implementation plan, which includes lowering speed limits in built-up areas as one of its measures. The question is always whether it will actually be implemented — that's often a political decision that leads to endless wrangling, but the state has set out the direction and the idea," Vane said.
--
Editor: Marcus Turovski

articles.title: Gut viruses are evolving new tricks to beat bacteria — and could help fight superbugs
articles.body:
Scientists have found that some viruses can deliberately generate genetic diversity to evade bacterial defences, offering a potential new clue for developing treatments when antibiotics fail.
Viruses that selectively target and kill bacteria — also known as bacteriophages or simply phages — infect bacteria but leave human cells alone. Once they attach to a bacterial cell, they inject their genetic material, hijack the cell's machinery and force it to produce new phages until the bacterium bursts.
The problem is that bacteria can evolve defences against phages, just as they evolve resistance to antibiotics.
The new research suggests that phages have their own evolutionary countermeasure.
Some of the viruses living in the human gut can rapidly generate genetic variations among their offspring, increasing the chances that at least some will survive when bacteria fight back, according to the study, published Thursday in Nature Microbiology.
The finding could offer a new route in the search for alternatives to antibiotics, as drug-resistant infections become harder to treat.
Researchers at Michigan State University have identified previously underappreciated regions of bacteriophage genomes that act as genetic “hotspots”, allowing the viruses to repeatedly alter key genes as they replicate.
This suggests these regions help phages hedge their evolutionary bets against bacterial defences. Rather than producing a population of genetically identical viruses, they generate a diverse collection of offspring with different characteristics — increasing the odds that some can continue infecting and killing their bacterial hosts.
“This changes our understanding of how phages evolve,” said co-author Chris Waters, a faculty member in Michigan State University’s Ecology, Evolution, and Behavior program. “Instead of hijacking their hosts to mass produce exact copies of themselves, they are actually using these mutation hotspots to make a zoo,” he said, adding that phages are “essentially hedging their bets.”
A genetic escape route
The researchers studied bacteriophage T2, which infects E. coli, after examining a bacterial defence system that can recognise and destroy invading phage DNA.
The team transferred the defence system into E. coli in the laboratory and exposed the bacteria to phages.
The protection did not last.
Within hours, the phages began overcoming the bacterial defences.
“Within a few hours, the phages always started to win,” Waters said. “We couldn’t understand why,” he added.
When researchers sequenced the resistant viruses, they found repeated mutations in a gene called agt, particularly in a stretch of repetitive DNA. “When I saw the data, I thought, oh my gosh,” Waters said.
That sequence turned out to be what scientists call a contingency locus — a highly mutable region where the DNA-copying machinery can slip when replicating repeated sequences.
The result is a reversible frameshift mutation that can change how the gene's instructions are read.
Some phages gain an extra repeat; others lose one. The result is a population containing different versions of the virus, potentially with different abilities to evade bacterial defences.
The researchers found that these repetitive regions accumulated mutations thousands of times faster than the rest of the phage genome.
And the mechanism is not confined to a single virus.
Using experimental evolution and genome sequencing, the researchers found similar contingency loci in E. coli phage T4. They also found that simple sequence repeats were widespread across diverse E. coli phages, although their abundance varied between genes with different functions.
Could it help treat superbugs?
The research comes as scientists and policymakers look for alternatives to antibiotics.
Phage therapy is not new. Phages were used therapeutically as early as the 1920s to treat bacterial infections, but interest in the approach declined after antibiotics such as penicillin became widely available.
Now the rise of antimicrobial resistance has revived interest.
The appeal is partly down to specificity. Whereas many antibiotics can kill beneficial bacteria alongside the pathogen they target, individual phages can be highly selective for particular bacterial species or strains.
But that specificity is also a weakness: bacteria can evolve resistance to a phage, potentially rendering a treatment ineffective.
The Michigan State findings raise the possibility that scientists could eventually exploit the viruses' own evolutionary strategies to make phage treatments more resilient.
“If we can harness these kinds of evolutionary tricks, we might be able to make more effective phage therapies in response to the antibiotic resistance crisis,” Waters said.
“We’re never going to be able to completely get rid of resistance,” he added. “But if we can better understand how bacteria protect themselves from phage infection and how phages fight back, we might be able to minimize it.”

articles.title: 'Nehru did a lot, but did not possess arrogance': Kharge on Independence Day
articles.body:
'Nehru did a lot, but did not possess arrogance': Kharge on Independence Day
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 15, 2026, 12:46 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday invoked India's freedom struggle and the legacy of its first generation of leaders, remembering Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru while highlighting the Congress's contribution to the country's nation-building journey.Remembering Nehru's contribution to building modern India, Kharge on Independence Day said the former prime minister had laid the foundations of a democratic and secular nation and established institutions including IITs, IIMs and public sector undertakings."Nehru ji laid the foundation of a modern, democratic and secular India. He established IITs, IIMs, PSUs. Nehru ji did a lot for the country, but he did not possess arrogance," the Congress chief said.The Congress party head also recalled Mahtama Gandhi's "Do or Die" call during the Quit India Movement, highlighting the role played by young Indians when senior leaders were jailed by the British.He said, "When Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' and all the senior leaders were in jail, it was the youth of the country who carried forward the 'Quit India Movement'."Kharge said the freedom struggle had envisioned more than independence from colonial rule, arguing that India's freedom fighters had also dreamed of eliminating poverty, unemployment, untouchability, injustice and fear.
"Our freedom fighters had not only dreamed of liberation from British rule, but also from poverty, unemployment, untouchability, injustice, and fear. Independence was not just a change of power, but a resolve to make every Indian's life better. Every Prime Minister from the Congress has advanced this very vision," veteran Congress leader added.
‘Someone speaking from Red Fort claims they have done everything’
Kharge also invoked the contributions of former prime ministers Lal Bahadur Shastri and Indira Gandhi, crediting them with strengthening India's agricultural, military and strategic capabilities."Shastri ji strengthened the foundations of white and green revolution in the country. Indira ji strengthened India's military and strategic capabilities, and also played a major role in creation of Bangladesh. We also integrated Sikkim with India. All these were done by Congress party leaders, but someone speaking from Red Fort claims that they have done everything. It’s a mercy they don’t claim that whatever remains of the world has survived because of them," he said.Taking aim at what he described as the BJP-led government's tendency to claim credit for past achievements, Kharge asserted that Congress had played the dominant role in India's development."The development you see in the country today is because of Congress. Congress has 90% contribution in development you witnessed in the country today. We improved people's financial condition, not change names. But, these people just take credit. This will not go on for long," Congress president said.
Kharge backs protesting youth, attacks BJP-RSS
Kharge also trained his guns on the government's handling of youth grievances, saying young people were being denied opportunities and their protests were being met with hostility.
Rajya Sabha MP said, "Today, the dreams of the youth are being trampled. The country's youth are agitating, and we along with our leader of the opposition -- are supporting them. The Constitution grants everyone the right to protest for their cause; they are not anti-nationals. Hate campaigns are launched against those who protest."He added, "Our leader of the opposition declared years ago that we would not spread hate but instead spread a message of love. However, the BJP and RSS oppose this. They worked against the country even before independence and continue to do so today by dividing Hindus and Muslims. The current government is crushing the poor. We will continue to fight against the government."Kharge's remarks came on 80th Independence Day, which he celebrated alongside Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi.

articles.title: Israeli airstrike on southern Lebanon kills 7 people, Lebanese state media say
articles.body:
Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 9 people, Health Ministry says
BEIRUT (AP) — Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon killed at least nine people Saturday, in some of the deadliest attacks since a precarious truce between Israel and Hezbollah went into effect on June 20.
Lebanon’s Health Ministry and state news agency said one of the airstrikes that targeted a home on the edge of the village of Ansar killed seven people, including three children, and wounded two. The second, on the village of Deir al-Zahrani, killed two and wounded nine.
Israel and the Lebanese government announced a “framework agreement” on June 26, laying out a plan for Israeli forces to withdraw from southern Lebanon, in exchange for the disarmament of the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group. It also envisions steps toward an eventual peace agreement between the two countries — which technically remain in a state of war nearly 80 years after Israel’s establishment.
Hezbollah has refused direct talks and wasn’t party to the deal.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam criticized Israel’s airstrikes on southern Lebanon, saying they intimidate “residents in their homes” and undermine efforts to stabilize the situation in the south.
“The seven martyrs of the Israeli airstrike on the town of Ansar are not military infrastructure and the children and women killed were not military targets,” Salam said in comments posted on X. He added that it is the job of the Lebanese state to deal with any military infrastructure in the country.
“Israel must halt this escalation,” Salam said. He added that the security of the Lebanese people and their right to life on their land “are not subject to negotiation or bargaining.”
Intense Israeli airstrikes early Saturday also hit the strategic Ali Taher hill, which overlooks parts of the southern city of Nabatiyeh and main roads leading to it, NNA reported. Despite the truce, Israel’s military has continued its almost daily attacks on the area, which is north of the Litani River and has been a de facto boundary in Lebanon, with large areas to the south under Israeli military control.
The Israeli military said in a statement that it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in the areas of Ali Taher and Ansar in response to an action against Israeli soldiers in the area. The military added that it will not allow the Hezbollah to harm Israeli civilians or soldiers “and will continue to operate to remove threats.”
A Hezbollah official did not immediately respond when asked for comment on whether they carried out any attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon.
Earlier this month, two Israeli soldiers were killed in an explosion in southern Lebanon, the first Israeli deaths since the shaky truce. Hezbollah did not comment on the blast.
Lebanon and Israel have held seven rounds of talks; the most recent took place in Rome earlier this month.
The Iran-backed Hezbollah has refused to disarm and accuses the Lebanese government of making too many concessions without guaranteeing an Israeli withdrawal.
The latest Israel-Hezbollah war erupted on March 2, when Hezbollah fired rockets across the border two days after the U.S. and Israel launched their attacks on Iran. More than 4,000 people have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon since then, including hundreds of civilians. About 40 soldiers and three civilians — including a military contractor — have been killed on the Israeli side.
____
Associated Press writer Sam Mednick contributed to this report from Tel Aviv, Israel.

articles.title: War update: 233 clashes on front lines over past day, most in Kostiantynivka sector
articles.body:
War update: 233 clashes on front lines over past day, most in Kostiantynivka sector
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces reported this in an update on the battlefield situation as of 08:00 on Saturday, August 15.
Russian forces carried out 71 airstrikes, dropping 241 guided aerial bombs. They also deployed 10,626 kamikaze drones and carried out 3,042 shelling attacks, including 36 using multiple launch rocket systems.
Artillery fire hit Neskuchne, Bachivsk, Koreniok, Sopych, Tovstodubove, Yastrubshchyna, Volfyne, Hirky, Bezsalivka, Kozache, Seredyna-Buda and Rohizne in the Sumy region. Tovstodubove also came under an airstrike.
Ukrainian aviation, missile forces and artillery struck two command posts, five areas where Russian personnel were concentrated, three artillery systems and eight UAV command posts.
On the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk fronts, Ukrainian forces repelled six enemy assaults. Russian troops carried out four airstrikes, dropping eight bombs, and shelled Ukrainian positions 62 times.
On the Southern Slobozhanshchyna axis, Ukrainian forces repelled 12 attacks. Russian troops attempted to advance near Starytsia and Vovchansk and toward Izbytske, Vilcha, Lyman, Shyroke, Aniksine and Khatnie.
On the Kupiansk axis, Russian forces launched 14 offensive actions toward Petro-Ivanivka and near Holubivka.
On the Lyman axis, Russian troops launched five attacks toward Drobysheve and Lyman.
On the Sloviansk axis, the enemy launched 23 assaults near Riznykivka, Zakitne and Kryva Luka and toward Rai-Oleksandrivka, Ozerne and Mykolaivka.
On the Kramatorsk axis, Russian forces launched one assault toward Yurkivka.
The Kostiantynivka sector saw the heaviest fighting, with 34 attacks recorded. Russian forces launched assaults near Kostiantynivka, Ivanopillia, Illinivka, Toretske and Sofiivka and toward Stepanivka, Dolha Balka and Kucheriv Yar.
The enemy launched 29 attacks on the Pokrovsk axis, attempting to advance near Dorozhnie, Kotlyne and Udachne and toward Svitле, Novyi Donbas, Muravka, Bilytske, Shevchenko, Vasylivka and Serhiivka.
On the Oleksandrivka axis, Russian forces launched six attacks toward Piddubne, Myrne, Verbove and Kalynivske.
On the Huliaipole axis, the enemy attacked Ukrainian defenders seven times, attempting to advance toward Rivne, Verkhnia Tersa and Novoselivka.
On the Orikhiv axis, Ukrainian forces stopped one Russian attempt to advance toward Pavlivka.
No Russian assault operations were recorded on the Dnipro River axis.
No signs of Russian forces forming offensive groupings were detected on the Volyn and Polissia axes.

articles.title: From Gaza condoms to 'Your mom': Outgoing White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt's most divisive moments
articles.body:
Karoline Leavitt announced this week she was stepping down from her role as White House Press Secretary. From her combative relationship with the press to viral moments which have made her infamous, here is a lookback at her most divisive moments behind the podium.
The Trump administration unexpectedly lost its megaphone this week, with the news of White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt resigning from her post to spend more time with her family.
Some have joked that her departure came days after Donald Trump left her and several members of his cabinet on a decoy plane that was supposedly targeted by a terrorist threat, while he was smuggled onto a secret flight out of Turkey.
The official line is that Leavitt will leave for personal reasons, saying on social media that since the birth of her second child, she’d realized she "cannot be the best mom" while devoting the “constant time, energy, and attention,” her job requires.
Regardless, what is certain is that she has outlasted many of her predecessors like Sean Spicer and Kayleigh McEnany. Throughout her 18-month tenure, the 28-year-old - and youngest person to ever hold the job - has proven to be a valuable asset for Donald Trump, who described her as "one of my most trusted aides".
She's also been incredibly divisive. For some, she's a staunch and unwavering Trump loyalist; others describe her as a dishonest and verbally abusive MAGA zealot.
The news of her quitting has been met with both disappointment from Trump's base, who know he will have a hard time replacing someone so fiercely dedicated to defending him throughout his many controversies, and cheers from those who routinely refer to her as "KKKaroline Leavitt".
Her time behind the White House podium has not been without controversy.
Whether it's attacking journalists and wishing to control press access to the White House, affirming proven falsehoods or hyperbolically praising Trump's achievements when opening her briefings, here is a lookback at five of Leavitt's most contentious moments.
Condoms in Gaza
Even some of Karoline Leavitt's harshest critics have admitted that her vociferous defence of Trump has been impressive by the administration's standards. Some have also pointed out online that her deviations from facts and the truth have made then-Trump advisor Kellyanne Conway's "alternative facts" look innocent by comparison.
At her first-ever White House briefing, Leavitt announced that the Trump administration had foiled a plan to use taxpayer dollars to "fund condoms in Gaza.”
She stated that DOGE and the US Office of Management and Budget had “found that there was about to be 50 million taxpayer dollars that went out the door to fund condoms in Gaza.”
Trump repeated the claim, but added that the condoms were for Hamas.
Leavitt’s comments made headlines around the world - specifically because there was no evidence offered for this outlandish federal plan to spend millions on condoms in Gaza. Experts on US aid to Gaza and global health aid were baffled by the claim, with Steve Fake, a spokesperson for aid nonprofit Anera, telling CNN at the time that there was “definitely no purchase of condoms”.
“We have asked around, and no one is sure what this is referring to.”
The Associated Press beef
In March 2025, AP reporter Josh Boak challenged Leavitt over Trump’s tariff policy, arguing that tariffs function as taxes on importers.
“He’s actually not implementing tax hikes,” said Leavitt. “Tariffs are a tax hike on foreign countries that, again, have been ripping us off. Tariffs are a tax cut for the American people, and the President is a staunch advocate of tax cuts.”
Boak pushed back by saying: “I’m sorry, have you ever paid a tariff? Because I have. They don’t get charged on foreign companies; they get charged on the importers.”
Leavitt replied by calling the question “insulting” and added: “I now regret giving a question to The Associated Press.”
For context, the exchange occurred during a broader dispute between the Trump administration and AP over the press agency's terminology.
Indeed, the Trump administration blocked them from accessing press events due to AP continuing to refer to the Gulf of Mexico by its actual title, as opposed to Trump's desire to rename it the "Gulf of America".
“It is a fact that the body of water off the coast of Louisiana is called the Gulf of America," said Leavitt, who defended AP's restrictions by saying she was holding news outlets accountable for reporting "lies".
The sanctions on AP were later lifted, but the incidents proved how keen Leavitt was on taking control over the press pool system, wishing to arbitrate who got access and who didn't. She later added MAGA personalities to the permanent press corps – podcasters and allies who didn't fall under her description of media outlets: "The press does only want to make the president look bad. That's it. That’s a fact."
Critics described these attempts as the "introduction of propagandists" and a way of undermining the core functions of the "Fourth Estate".
Leavitt defended herself and the administration by saying it was part of an effort to broaden access beyond traditional news organizations.
The viral "Your mom" jab
Leavitt has constantly sparred with journalists she deemed to be "left-wing extremists" or "Trump haters", but one exchange went down like a lead balloon – leading many to label the president's inner circle as “moronic”, “childish” and “juvenile”.
Leavitt went viral last October when she shared an image of a text exchange with the HuffPost’s White House correspondent, S.V Dáte, on X.
At the time, Trump was planning to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Hungary.
"Is the president aware of the significance of Budapest?” asked Dáte in his message to Leavitt, adding: “In 1994, Russia promised, in Budapest, not to invade Ukraine if it gave up the nuclear weapons it inherited when the Soviet Union dissolved. Does he not see why Ukraine might object to that site?”
Dáte finished the message with the question “Who suggested Budapest?”, followed by a polite “Thanks.”
Leavitt replied: “Your mom did.”
She followed that up by labelling Dáte as a “far-left hack who nobody takes seriously" and added: “Stop texting me your disingenuous, biased, and bulls*** questions."
In one trending reply, Leavitt showed to what extent she was keen to dismiss the press' function of holding presidents to account, and how little she cared about being measured in her responses to journalists she saw as being "anti-Trump".
The response also saw countless commentators online highlighting the hypocrisy of accusing a journalist of lacking seriousness and professionalism for a newsworthy question and answering with a reply more commonly found in playgrounds.
The Epstein files: A "hoax"
Last November, Leavitt described the Epstein files as a “hoax that is being perpetuated by opportunistic Democrats”.
She went on to say that Trump knew Epstein because they both lived in Palm Beach and that Trump kicked him out of his Mar-a-Lago club because “Jeffrey Epstein was a paedophile and he was a creep.”
Earlier this year, in February, reporters pressed Leavitt about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s relationship with Epstein, as Lutnick had acknowledged visiting Epstein’s private island in 2012 - despite previously saying he had ended the relationship years earlier.
Leavitt immediately responded by defending the Commerce Secretary as "a very important member of President Trump’s team" before criticising reporters for their questions.
“I will just point out that there are a lot of wins in the news this week that people in this room have not asked about because you continue to ask questions about the same subject so let me point them out for you,” Leavitt said.
She then began to recite recent stock market results and abruptly ended the press briefing with: “The President is very busy today and you will see him all tomorrow at the event in the East Room touting his Administration’s energy policy.”
She walked off stage to the bafflement of the press pool.
The ICE question by a "left-wing hack"
In January 2026, The Hill columnist Niall Stanage questioned Leavitt about ICE, following the fatal shooting of Renee Nicole Good by an ICE agent.
Stanage listed statistics that 32 people died while in ICE custody in 2025 before referencing Good’s death.
Leavitt asked him: “Why was Renee Good unfortunately and tragically killed?”
Stanage replied: “Because an ICE agent acted recklessly and killed her unjustifiably.”
Leavitt's response was seen my many as deflection 101 and unacceptable.
“Okay, so you’re a biased reporter with a leftwing opinion,” she said. “Because you’re a leftwing hack. You’re not a reporter, you’re posing in this room as a journalist. And it’s so clear by the premise of your question. And you and the people of the media who have such biases but fake like you’re a journalist - you shouldn’t even be sitting in that seat.”
“You’re pretending like you’re a journalist, but you’re a leftwing activist,” she continued. “The question that you just raised and your answer proves you’re biased. You should be reporting on the facts.”
Leavitt will depart from the position as White House Press Secretary at the end of August. As of writing, there is no indication on who her replacement will be.

articles.title: IRGC chief praises armed forces after 6 months of war

Major General Ahmad Vahidi, commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said in a message Friday that Iranian forces had "brought the world's most heavily armed military to its knees" over six months of fighting, in remarks marking the start of the Islamic month of Rabi al-Awwal.
Addressing IRGC personnel, army troops, police, the Basij and border forces, Vahidi praised their endurance through harsh conditions, including intense heat and humidity on Iran's southern islands and coast and cold weather in the northern border highlands, along with successful offensive and defensive operations carried out under heavy fire.
Vahidi drew a comparison to Iran's eight-year war with Iraq in the 1980s and thanked the families of those who fought. He offered condolences and well wishes for the new Islamic month, and voiced hope that the war's toll on the region, particularly Gaza and Lebanon, would soon end.

articles.title: Trump was ‘joking’ about declaring Strait of Hormuz US territory: US media
articles.body:
Rabia Iclal Turan and Gizem Nisa Demir
15 August 2026•Update: 15 August 2026
US President Donald Trump was “joking” when he said he would declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory after the war with Iran, US media reported Friday.
Trump has not met with his advisers to discuss such a move, Wall Street Journal reporter Brian Schwartz said through US social media platform X, citing an unnamed senior White House official.
“President Trump has not met with his advisers about declaring the Strait of Hormuz a US territory post the war and was joking during his speech today in New York,” Schwartz wrote.
Trump made the remark during a political rally at the Nassau County Police Academy in Garden City, New York.
“After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States,” he said with a chuckle. “It’s true,” he added.
Schwartz, who attended the speech, said Trump chuckled after making the remark but then appeared to insist that it was true.
Trump also claimed that Washington controls maritime access through the strategically vital waterway.
“We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to,” he told supporters.
 
Iran disputes US control claims
Iranian military officials have disputed the claim, with Iran’s central military command on Thursday calling assertions of US control over the waterway “baseless lies and fabrications.”
As of Aug. 12, some 3,371 vessels had crossed the strait in the 166 days since the war began, representing around 20% of pre-war traffic volumes, according to data from commodities and shipping analytics firm Kpler cited by CNN.
The US and Iran had agreed to a Pakistan-brokered ceasefire in April and later signed a deal on June 17 to launch negotiations toward a final agreement. However, the talks subsequently stalled over disagreements including security guarantees and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
The two sides also exchanged military strikes from July 8 to 24, with Washington attacking targets inside Iran, and Tehran responding with strikes on what it described as US military facilities and equipment in several Arab countries, including Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait.
The Strait of Hormuz connects the Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and is one of the world’s most important energy shipping routes.

articles.title: UK hits back after Netanyahu labels it 'the Islamic republic of Britain'
articles.body:
Netanyahu made the comments during an army radio podcast interview, in which he also joked that the UK was the "first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons."
The British government has reportedly hit back at comments by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu describing the UK "the Islamic republic of Britain."
A government spokesperson has labelled the remarks as "completely unacceptable" and said that the issue had been raised with the Israeli government.
Netanyahu made the comments during an army radio podcast interview, in which he also joked that the UK was the "first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons."
During the interview, the Israeli leader praised Randolph Churchill, the son of former British PM Winston Churchill, for positive coverage of Israel during the Six-Day War of 1967.
"Try and find that now, in what is called the Islamic republic of Britain," he said.
The host encouraged the point, saying: "Isn't all of Europe like that now?"
To which Netanyahu agreed, adding: "Yes, but someone said, 'the first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons will be the Islamic republic of Great Britain.'"
"So, we'll make sure there isn't a second one here in Iran," he continued.
The Islamic Republic of Pakistan has been a nuclear power since 1998.
Netanyahu's comments echo similar claims made by politicians and activists on the British and international right, who claim that Britain is becoming increasingly influenced by Islam.
The UK and Israel's relationship has come under increasing strain in recent months, particularly since new British PM Andy Burnham's arrival in Downing Street.
A few weeks before taking over as prime minister, Burnham apologised for his Labour party's initial response to the war in Gaza and said that it needed to "do better."
While he condemned the Hamas militant group's "monstrous" October 7 attacks and "appalling" antisemitic incidents in the UK, he said it was vital to "be clear in our criticism of what has happened in Gaza."
"The unbearable suffering in Gaza is a scar on our collective conscience," Burnham said in early July.
"It's completely unacceptable that innocent Palestinians, including children, continue to be killed," he continued, adding that Westminster must put more pressure on the Israeli government.
