articles.title: Russian foreign minister, his Thai counterpart sign consultation plan for 2026-2028
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 14. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow signed a consultation plan between the two countries’ foreign ministries for 2026-2028.
The signing ceremony took place before the two sides’ talks.
"Certainly, the consultation plan we have just signed for the next three years will make our foreign ministries’ relations more systematic and dynamic," Lavrov said.

articles.title: Hong Kong strives to publish 1st five-year plan in September
articles.body:
HONG KONG, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Janice Tse Siu-wa, secretary for constitutional and mainland affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government, said on Friday that the HKSAR government will continue its efforts in collating and analyzing views, striving to publish Hong Kong's first five-year plan within September.
Tse said that the plan was not only an important matter for Hong Kong, but also an integral part of the national 15th Five-Year Plan, serving as a major initiative to integrate into and serve the overall development of the country and a milestone for public administration in Hong Kong.
The public consultation ran from June 15 to Aug. 14, with over 100 consultation sessions organized throughout the period, including about 30 sessions conducted by the HKSAR chief executive himself to listen to views and suggestions from various sectors, Tse noted.
As of Friday, the HKSAR government has received over 16,000 submissions from different sectors, the general public and stakeholders from different backgrounds, who generally agreed that the plan will help Hong Kong better seize opportunities and make deployments, Tse added.
Tse said that the general public and stakeholders have taken the formulation of the plan very seriously and have high confidence in Hong Kong's future, keen to contribute views to jointly outline the blueprint for the next five years and better integrate into and serve the overall national development. ■

articles.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages on Saturday
articles.body:
Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages on Saturday
Ukrinform
    No electricity consumption restrictions are planned in Ukraine on Saturday, August 15.
    According to Ukrinform, NPC Ukrenergo announced this on Telegram.
"Tomorrow, Saturday, no restriction measures are planned," the company said.
Ukrenergo urged consumers to use electricity sparingly and to shift the use of high-power appliances to the period from 10:00 to 17:00.
As previously reported, following new Russian strikes, as of the morning of August 14, consumers in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, and Sumy regions were without electricity.

articles.title: China Focus: Bank plays Cupid in China's public service makeover
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Who says banks are just for banking? At a downtown Tianjin branch in northern China, bubbles drift through the lobby as smiling couples arrive hand in hand and leave as newlyweds, turning a place once reserved for financial transactions into the starting point of a lifelong romantic commitment.
Couples are greeted by a lush purple iris floral wall and an oversized clock-shaped selfie spot that proudly declares, "We're Married!"
On its opening day, Aug. 6, newlyweds who received their marriage certificates on-site couldn't hide their delight: "It's romantic, cozy and truly ceremonial. Plus, it's right outside our office -- incredibly convenient."
Co-established by Tianjin's Hexi District Civil Affairs Bureau and the local Postal Savings Bank branch, it is the country's first marriage registry housed in a bank, redefining what customers expect when they walk through the doors.
On their big day, couples receive a free postcard to pen their hopes and promises to each other, before dropping it into the in-store time mailbox. The branch safeguards the postcard for seven years, mailing it back to the couple's address on their wedding anniversary -- a tender reminder that love, like savings, thrives on patience, commitment and daily deposits of care.
But the registry offers far more than certificates and special moments. Newlyweds can also access financial consultations, ranging from family financial planning to home loans for their first nest, while customizing their debit card with their favorite wedding-day photo.
"This new service model marks a fresh attempt by our bank to reach deeper into the community and get closer to the real-life needs of young people," a bank executive said, adding that the branch is striving to create a warm, memorable and supportive space for young couples.
Similar initiatives have been popping up across China since the marriage registration process was simplified in May 2025. The new policy allows residents to register at any qualified civil affairs office nationwide, without the need for a household registration booklet.
The policy shift has since inspired cities and tourist attractions across the country to roll out their own signature registration venues.
At Xingfuba -- a metro station in Feixi County, east China's Anhui Province, whose name sounds like "be happy" in Chinese -- getting married is as easy as getting off the train. The station has already witnessed over 5,700 couples embarking on a new chapter of their lives.
Some tourist spots have gone a step further, turning marriage registration into a travel experience. At Sayram Lake in northwest China's Xinjiang, a registry now sits by the water. And at a theme park in Dalian, northeastern Liaoning Province, couples can tie the knot in a Ferris wheel. Even music festivals have now jumped on the bandwagon as well.
As of May 8 this year, China had set up 525 park-style marriage registration venues and 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation nationwide.
These approaches, experts say, are helping to boost marriage registration numbers, which saw an uptick in 2025 compared to the previous year.
Playing Cupid may be fun, but it also highlights a hard truth for the banking industry, with much of its transactions happening online. With most banking services just a tap away on a phone, what can brick-and-mortar branches offer that a screen can't?
Some banks are already re-imagining their physical presence. In Nantong, east China's Jiangsu Province, one bank has opened its doors to soccer fans, inviting them to catch local matches, while handing out free city souvenirs and attraction tickets. Another branch in Pu'er, southwestern Yunnan Province, has teamed up with a coffee chain, serving up beverage vouchers alongside banking services.
Meanwhile, the partnership between banks and government affairs is opening up new possibilities. An increasing number of bank outlets are now offering services such as social security, healthcare insurance, tax processing and real-estate registration, turning lobbies into one-stop civic hubs.
The love-themed bank in Tianjin is just one example of this broader shift, and it has won widespread acclaim.
As one Weibo user who goes by the handle Nomihut wrote: "When a marriage registry moves into a bank, we see more than just an innovative way to get a certificate. We see a city that's willing to make room for ordinary people's romance, and to keep reinventing itself for their convenience." ■

articles.title: Consistent attacks, smears against China by Philippines' defense secretary harm interests of Philippines: spokesperson
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The consistent attacks and smears against China by the Philippines' Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. harm not only the bilateral relations, but also the interests of the Philippines and all its people that will bear the brunt, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Friday.
Spokesperson Guo Jiakun's remarks came after Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has accused China of using the action against Filipinos to pressure the Philippines over its law enforcement operations against Chinese nationals. Teodoro said the actions against 100 Filipinos are "simple extortion and blackmail."
Noting foreign nationals in China should abide by Chinese laws and regulations, Guo said China's immigration authorities perform their duty in accordance with the law and protect the lawful rights and interests of the personnel concerned. The actions do not target any specific country.
It's learned that it was exactly this defense secretary who personally led the armed forces to seize and detain Chinese nationals lawfully working in the Philippines, Guo said.
"This person's consistent attacks and smears against China harm not only the bilateral relations. It is the interests of the Philippines and all its people that will bear the brunt," Guo added. ■

articles.title: Malaysia records strong Q2 economic growth, says PM
articles.body:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The Malaysian economy continued to defy expectations for the third consecutive quarter, growing strongly by 6.0 percent in the second quarter of 2026 despite shocks that have disrupted the global economy, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the figure, higher than the 5.4 percent in the preceding quarter, marked Malaysia's strongest second quarter showing outside the pandemic period since 2014.
He attributed this to the government's proactive response to the Middle Eastern conflict through financial support for small- and medium-sized enterprises and targeted fuel subsidies, according to a statement from the Finance Ministry.
"These measures helped sustain household spending, business activity, and the economy's strong growth momentum into Q2 2026... While disruptions to global supply chains have exerted upward pressure on prices worldwide, Malaysia's inflation remained contained at 1.9 percent in Q2 2026," he said.
The ministry also said the quarter's performance brought growth in the first half of 2026 to 5.7 percent, placing the economy on a firm footing relative to the government's full-year growth forecast of 4.0 percent to 5.0 percent.
Private consumption remained a key driver of growth, expanding by 4.8 percent, buoyed by higher spending on restaurants and hotels, transport, and food and beverages amid festive celebrations, the mid-year school holidays, and sustained tourism-related activities, it said.
Private and public investments continued to grow, underpinned by ongoing investments in the technology sector and the nationwide deployment of critical infrastructure.
It added that the government remains mindful that the benefits of economic growth are not felt evenly across households and businesses: "Continued geopolitical uncertainty, disruptions to global supply chains, higher input and food prices, and employment pressures in certain sectors remain key risks to household well-being and business activity," it said. ■

articles.title: Central African Republic celebrates Independence Day with call for reforms
articles.body:
YAOUNDE, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The Central African Republic marked its 66th Independence Day on Thursday as President Faustin-Archange Touadera called for reforms to advance the country's modernization.
"This institutional change is not a mere formality. It commits us to a radical and comprehensive transformation of our country. We are not repairing the old system; we are building a new Central African Republic," Touadera said in a televised address.
"This metamorphosis must unfold on every front: political, security, economic, social, and environmental," he added.
Touadera also struck a firm tone on security, saying the reform agenda would not be stopped by outside pressure.
"No incursion, no security-related blackmail from enemies will make the country back down," he said. "Our response will be systematic, comprehensive, and relentless."
The anniversary was marked by military and civilian parades in cities across the country.
The Central African Republic gained its independence from France on Aug. 13, 1960. ■

articles.title: Ukraine strikes Novatek's gas condensate processing complex in Russia's Leningrad Region
articles.body:
KIEV, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Ukrainian forces struck Russian gas producer Novatek's gas condensate processing complex at the Baltic port of Ust-Luga in Russia's northwestern Leningrad Region, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said Friday.
The Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement that the complex was hit overnight from Thursday to Friday. A fire was reported at the site, and preliminary information indicated that two processing units had been hit.
The complex processes stable gas condensate into light and heavy naphtha, jet fuel, fuel oil and gas oil, and facilitates the transshipment of gas condensate and the export of petroleum products to international markets.
In 2025, the complex processed 7,986 metric tons of stable gas condensate, an increase of 8.5 percent from 2024, according to Novatek's website. ■

articles.title: Three injured in gas explosion near Brussels central station
articles.body:
BRUSSELS, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Three people were injured in a gas explosion at a building near Brussels Central Station on Friday, local media reported.
After a low-pressure gas pipe was damaged during construction work at a building near the railway station, firefighters and staff from Brussels energy distribution network operator Sibelga were subsequently dispatched to the scene.
Around 100 people inside the building were evacuated as a precaution, and the street was cordoned off.
At around 1:30 p.m. (1130 GMT), an explosion occurred inside the building while emergency crews were dealing with the gas leak, leading to the injury of three people, including two Sibelga employees.
The building houses the offices of the European Union's Single Resolution Board. The exact cause of the accident is currently being investigated. ■

articles.title: Azerbaijan hosts first BWF Junior International Series badminton tournament
articles.body:
BAKU, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The Azerbaijan Junior Open 2026 started here on Friday, marking Azerbaijan's debut as a host on the Badminton World Federation (BWF) Junior International Series circuit.
The three-day tournament features 64 Under-19 players from nine countries competing in five events: men's and women's singles and doubles, and mixed doubles.
Host Azerbaijan is represented by 22 players, while other competitors come from Türkiye, Uzbekistan, Georgia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, India and Tajikistan.
Finals in all five events are scheduled for Aug. 16. ■

articles.title: On the campaign trail for United Russia, Putin kicks a soccer ball, admires giant halibut, and dons a sailor’s uniform
articles.body:
On the campaign trail for United Russia, Putin kicks a soccer ball, admires giant halibut, and dons a sailor’s uniform
Russian President Vladimir Putin has been traveling actively around Russia in recent weeks — since the start of summer, he has visited seven regions outside Moscow and St. Petersburg. Before that, he had not left the two capitals and the Novgorod region (where his residence in Valdai is located) for a record seven months. In the regions, Putin is visits major industrial plants and mass events and interacts with the public; state propaganda is covers all of this in great detail. The trips themselves fit neatly into the election campaign of United Russia, which presents itself as the president’s party (and which is experiencing a ratings catastrophe). Here’s what happens in the regions when the president comes to visit.
August 3, Krasnoyarsk. The price of a liter of gasoline in the city falls by 24 rubles just before Putin’s arrival (then returns to its previous level the next day). The president attends the final of Bolshaya Peremena (“Big Change”), where the host introduces him to the stage: “The greatest dream of all the millions of kids — a man, our dear friend, the president of the Russian Federation.” Someone passes Putin a ball. He kicks it back. Applause follows. The ball is sent to a museum.
August 10, Ulan-Ude. Buses across the city are plastered with quotes from Putin, including: “I commend the energy and initiative of the people of Buryatia, and their sincere love for the Motherland.” The president meets with a boy who had “invited” him to Ulan-Ude a week earlier, in Krasnoyarsk: “I’m addressing you as supreme commander in chief: my dream is to become a pilot, please help me get into a Suvorov military school” — “We’ll sort it out.”
August 11, Novosibirsk. Electric scooters are banned from the new asphalt hastily laid in the city center ahead of Putin’s visit. He talks with young scientists: “What threats does artificial intelligence pose to us?” — “Vladimir Vladimirovich, you have nothing to fear!” — “I’ve never been afraid of anything.” On the way to the airport, Putin “spontaneously” stops his motorcade and takes photos with children who had waited there for several hours. Right nearby, a gas station’s price board has been turned off.
August 12, Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk. Putin takes part in Pacific Fleet exercises and weighs in on the day’s news, accusing the European Union of piracy over the seizure of Russian merchant ships and threatening “retaliatory measures.” The president appears in public for the first time in the new uniform of the Navy’s commander in chief. The date marks the 26th anniversary of the sinking of the submarine Kursk. Putin does not mention it.
August 13, Iturup Island. Putin visits the Kuril Islands for the first time. He had avoided the trip previously to keep from antagonizing Japan. At a fish processing plant, the president samples caviar and marvels at the enormous halibut and tuna. He talks with local residents: “What great weather you have here! A resort!” — “We thought you had arranged that, since it happens so rarely.” The governor tells Putin that residents of the region are determined to do everything for victory. “That’s the kind of people we have,” Putin says. “The genetic code of winners.”
At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication.
If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at [email protected].
To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter.

articles.title: Levee breach sealed in China's flood-hit Henan
articles.body:
ZHENGZHOU, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- A levee breach in central China's Henan Province was successfully sealed on Friday night after nearly two days of emergency repair work, local authorities said.
The breach, measuring more than 40 meters wide, occurred along the Beiru River in Jiaxian County, Pingdingshan City, on Wednesday night after heavy rainfall caused a section of the levee to give way, forcing the relocation of more than 2,000 people.
No casualties have been reported so far.
Due to the narrow road atop the levee, heavy construction vehicles were unable to reach the site. Rescue workers formed human chains to pass gravel-filled sandbags to the breach, while drones and rescue boats were deployed to transport materials.
The operation came amid widespread flooding triggered by heavy rainfall brought by the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin, the year's 13th typhoon, which has affected multiple parts of Henan Province in recent days.
In response, the National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief activated a Level-IV national disaster relief emergency response for Henan on Friday. The central government has allocated 30,000 items of relief supplies, including folding beds, summer quilts and family emergency kits, to support relief and resettlement efforts in Zhoukou, Xuchang and other affected areas. ■

articles.title: IN BRIEF: What is known about power outages in Central Asia
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 14. /TASS/. Power outages have been reported in various parts of Tajikistan’s capital city of Dushanbe.
Many people have also reported being left without power in Kazakhstan’s Almaty and the Almaty region, and in the Kyrgyz capital, Bishkek.
Later, power outages were reported from Uzbekistan’s southern Surkhandaryinskaya Region.
TASS has collected key facts about the situation.
Situation in Bishkek
Partial power outages have been reported in Bishkek, according to a TASS correspondent.
Power was reportedly lost several times in a couple of minutes.
According to the local media outlet 24.kg, several city districts are having electricity supply problems.
The press service of the Kyrgyz energy ministry says it has taken measures to correct the power issues.
Kyrgyzstan’s energy system has switched to the isolated operation mode after high voltage line shutdown in neighboring Kazakhstan, the ministry said later.
Power outages in Kazakhstan
An emergency power cut occurred in 14 districts of Almaty and the Almaty Region of Kazakhstan, the press service of the Alatau Zharyk power company said.
At 2:38 p.m. local time (9:38 a.m. GMT) on August 14, following an emergency shutdown of the 500 kV overhead power lines owned by KEGOC JSC, the emergency protection system (SAON - automatic load switch-off system, AFD - automatic frequency load shedding), went off in the Alatau Zharyk grid network, resulting in power cuts to customers in Almaty and the Almaty region.
The city’s residents have posted videos on social media showing traffic jams on the city’s roads caused by traffic lights that are not working.
Due to widespread power cuts in the city, which caused traffic lights to malfunction, police officers in Almaty have begun directing traffic manually.
Other media outlets have reported that there are problems with internet service.
Apart from that, Almaty residents write on social media that the city is having water supply problems.
According to the media, American rapper Kanye West is expected to give a concert at a stadium in the city’s Almalinsky district.
Kazakh media reported, citing users, that power outages occurred in Shymkent, the country’s third largest city, and in a number of the country’s southern regions.
The country’s energy ministry reported later that the power outage in Kazakhstan had been caused by an overcurrent in Central Asia’s power exchange system.
According to the ministry, the operator company, KEGOC, is carrying out repair works, with power supplies having been restored in several regions.
The situation is under contril, the ministry said.
The total power supply restrictions affecting consumers due to the blackout in Kazakhstan’s power system amounted to an estimated 2,810 MW, according to KEGOC’s press office.
On 14 August, a technical malfunction occurred in Kazakhstan’s Unified Energy System, resulting in the shutdown of the Agadyr-Ulken and Aktogay-Taldykorgan power lines, it said.
As a result, the southern zone of Kazakhstan’s Unified Energy System and the Central Asian Unified Energy System have been isolated from the main grid.
According to preliminary data, the technical malfunction was caused by a power surge from the Central Asian Unified Energy System
The grid operator began repair works immediately.
As a result, the 295 MW capacity limits in the Karaganda, Abai and Ulytau regions of Kazakhstan have been lifted.
Situation in Tajikistan
Power outages have been reported in various Dushanbe districts, local residents told TASS.
They occurred both in the center of the city and in its suburbs.
Repair works are underway, Tajikistan’s ministry of energy and water resources said.
The causes of the power outages have not yet been identified, the ministry said, adding that a special working group has been set up for that.
The ministry refuted social media reports about an alleged accident at the Nurek hydropower plant and called on people and media outlets to trust only official statements.
Power supplies have partially restored in Dushanbe, a TASS correspondent reported.
Power has been restored in the city center. Local residents also told TASS that power supply has been restored in some other areas of Dushanbe.
Outages in Uzbekistan
Power outages were reported from Uzbekistan’s southern Surkhandaryinskaya Region, the country’s energy ministry said.
According to the ministry, a power grid failure in a neighboring country affected the Central Asian power grid, resulting in power cuts in Surkhandarya and some other regions.
Repair works are underway, the ministry noted.
The ministry provided no further details about power cuts in other regions of the country.

articles.title: China to issue commemorative coins marking 100th birth anniversary of Jiang Zemin
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's central bank announced on Friday that it will issue four commemorative coins starting Aug. 17 to mark the 100th birth anniversary of late Chinese leader Jiang Zemin.
The coins comprise one ordinary commemorative coin, two gold coins and one silver coin, all of which are legal tender in China, according to the People's Bank of China.
The ordinary commemorative coin has a face value of 1 yuan (about 14.73 U.S. cents) and a diameter of 25 millimeters. Made of nickel-plated steel, it will have a mintage of 10 million pieces.
Its obverse features China's national emblem, along with the country name and year of issuance, while the reverse bears a portrait of Jiang, a Chinese inscription marking the 100th anniversary of his birth, "1926-2026," and the face value.
All three gold and silver coins feature China's national emblem, the country name and year of issuance on the obverse.
A 30-gram round gold coin, featuring a portrait of Jiang on the reverse, contains 30 grams of pure gold, measures 32 millimeters in diameter and has a face value of 500 yuan, with a maximum mintage of 1,000 pieces.
An 8-gram round gold coin features on its reverse a photograph of Jiang taken at his graduation from Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 1947. Containing 8 grams of pure gold, the coin measures 22 millimeters in diameter, has a face value of 100 yuan and a maximum mintage of 10,000 pieces.
A 30-gram round silver coin features a photograph of Jiang speaking at a meeting on the "Three Stresses" education campaign for leading officials in Gaozhou, south China's Guangdong Province, in 2000. Containing 30 grams of pure silver, the coin measures 40 millimeters in diameter, has a face value of 10 yuan and a maximum mintage of 20,000 pieces.
The gold and silver coins will be distributed by China Gold Coin Group Co., Ltd.
Jiang passed away in 2022 at the age of 96. ■

articles.title: Ecological assessment shows South China Sea islands, reefs in good condition
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The overall ecological conditions of nine islands and reefs surveyed in the South China Sea are generally good but displayed marked differences, according to a bulletin released by the South China Sea Bureau of the Ministry of Natural Resources Friday.
The document provides the first overall evaluation of the ecological conditions of the country's South China Sea islands and reefs, laying a foundation for their protection and management.
The ecological conditions of the Xisha Islands are showing positive signs of recovery, while Huangyan Dao in the Zhongsha Islands features a unique and diverse ecosystem, the bulletin said.
A total of 135 species of reef-building corals have been recorded at Huangyan Dao, with live coral coverage in its protected area reaching 38.8 percent.
The Nansha Islands and reefs are generally in good ecological condition, but some individual reefs have suffered severe ecosystem degradation, it noted.
At Tiexian Jiao, live coral coverage has fallen by nearly 70 percent from 2016 levels, amid outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish, tropical cyclones and human activities, particularly the Philippines' persistent and illegal construction on Zhongye Dao.
Meanwhile, persistent discharge from a foreign military vessel illegally grounded at Ren'ai Jiao, along with accumulated waste and fishing nets, has sharply reduced live coral coverage there and hindered coral growth and recovery.
A separate bulletin highlighted China's efforts to restore marine ecosystems in the South China Sea. From 2021 to 2025, 262 marine ecological restoration projects were carried out, with total investments exceeding 21.3 billion yuan (about 3.14 billion U.S. dollars).
By the end of 2025, about 2.66 million hectares in the South China Sea had been designated as marine ecological conservation redline areas, while marine nature reserves covered about 7 million hectares. ■

articles.title: Reckless ebike users put all of us at risk | Letter
articles.body:
There may be something in the argument identified by Andy Beckett that increased use of ebikes reflects broader changes in urban areas, including the cost of housing (Lime bikes hurtling around the city: is this the revenge of a priced-out generation?, 8 August). Yet none of that excuses the sheer impunity that radiates from ebike users, worsened by the design of city bikes which encourage the rider to sit back as if on a magic steed from which to survey their kingdom.
Their irresponsibility imposes externalities on other road users and pedestrians: riding through red lights and across junctions with no heed to other traffic, wearing headphones (but seemingly never helmets), being on the phone or apparently scrolling while riding, carelessly weaving just to maintain a conversation, riding far too fast on paths shared with pedestrians, dropping bikes like litter. As for riding home after drinking in the pub – seriously?
As a helmet-wearing cyclist, it is maddening to dodge people who seem barely familiar with a bike, let alone being in traffic. The behaviour needs to change. In the first instance, that must be through regulation and for riders and suppliers to be liable for the consequences of their actions, which sadly are sometimes serious.
Kevin Lloyd
Highbury, London

articles.title: Pakistan keeps up mediation efforts to resolve US-Iran conflict — ambassador
articles.body:
ASHGABAT, August 14. /TASS/. Pakistan continues to make mediation efforts to resolve the conflict between Iran and the United States, Pakistan's ambassador to Turkmenistan Faryal Leghari said.
"The civilian and military leadership of Pakistan, in particular Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal General Asim Munir, are working tirelessly to support mediation efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution of the conflict between the United States and Iran. Recognizing the enormous benefits of regional peace, we must continue to encourage dialogue, restore trust where relations have become strained, and hope that commendable mediation efforts will bring all parties involved closer to a just and lasting settlement," she said at a reception at the Pakistani embassy on the occasion of the country's Independence Day.
The diplomat also added that Pakistan highly appreciates Turkmenistan's policy of permanent neutrality and consistent support for peaceful dialogue. She said that it was in Islamabad where Turkmenistan's policy of neutrality was proclaimed, which was supported at the summit of the Organization for Economic Cooperation (ECO) in 1995.
"Pakistan also remains firmly committed to peace. We believe that differences should be resolved through diplomacy, dialogue, respect for international law and the sovereign equality of states," Leghari said.

articles.title: eccentrica removes the roof from the lamborghini diablo for its V12 roadster
articles.body:
ECCENTRICA BRINGS ITS OPEN-AIR DIABLO TO THE QUAIL
Eccentrica is unveiling its new V12 Roadster at The Quail by The Peninsula, A Motorsports Gathering, during Monterey Car Week, and designboom will be there to see it in person. Based on a first-series Lamborghini Diablo, the open-top restomod follows the company’s original Eccentrica V12 with an arguably straightforward proposition: take one of the least discreet supercars of the 1990s, remove the roof, and rebuild almost everything underneath. Created together with Milan-based studio Borromeo De Silva, the Roadster uses more than 3,500 bespoke components to reinterpret the Diablo without sanding away the qualities that made it quite so unreasonable in the first place.
Rather than simply cutting off the roof and hoping California weather does the rest, Eccentrica has reworked the structure around the new open cabin. The body combines steel and carbon fiber, while the track has been widened and the proportions adjusted to give the car a more planted stance without disguising its Diablo origins. A dedicated aerodynamic study addresses airflow around the exposed cockpit, and carbon fiber structural reinforcements compensate for the missing roof. Revised suspension geometry and a custom semi-active damper system further update a platform born well before software started asking drivers whether they would like to install something.
Behind the cabin sits a re-engineered 5.7-liter naturally aspirated V12, recalibrated for sharper throttle response and improved thermal and airflow management. It produces 550 hp at 7,000 rpm and 600 Nm of torque at 6,500 rpm, with a claimed top speed of 208 mph (335 km/h). Power is managed through a six-speed gated manual gearbox, while three driving modes adjust the car for different road conditions. Hydraulic steering remains part of the equation, paired with a modern Brembo braking system — contemporary assistance, in other words, without turning the experience into a touchscreen exercise.
The engineering program is led by Maurizio Reggiani, former Lamborghini chief technical officer whose résumé includes the Murciélago, Gallardo, Aventador and Huracán. For the Roadster, his team has focused as much on feedback as outright numbers, modifying the suspension, steering, braking and chassis to make the car more immediate from behind the wheel. The approach reflects Eccentrica’s broader obsession with what it calls analogue emotion: sounds, vibrations and mechanical inputs are treated less as imperfections to be filtered out than as part of the point. There are faster ways to travel in 2026, certainly, but few involve a metal gate between the gears.
Inside, the Roadster combines Connolly leather, Alcantara, anodized materials and exposed carbon fiber, balancing its motorsport references with a more tailored finish. Each example will be configured individually with its owner, extending to colors, trims, materials and detailing throughout the cabin and exterior. Eccentrica plans to build only 19 V12 Roadsters, giving every car its own specification rather than treating customization as a particularly long options menu.
The result sits somewhere between preservation and provocation. The familiar wedge remains unmistakably Diablo, but the widened stance, open cockpit and reworked surfaces shift it away from straightforward restoration. More importantly, the Roadster doubles down on a kind of driving increasingly defined by what it leaves out: no turbocharging, no automatic transmission and, now, no roof. Following its digital reveal earlier this month, the V12 Roadster made its first physical public appearance at The Quail on August 14th.
more than 3,500 bespoke components reshape the original diablo platform

articles.title: Zelensky having hard time choosing new Ukrainian ambassador to US — Politico
articles.body:
BRUSSELS, August 14. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky is having trouble finding someone to head the Ukrainian embassy in the United States, Politico quoted sources as saying.
"Of course, there are people who want the job, but there’s no one who really measures up to it. Zelensky is having a hard time filling the position," Politico quoted a Ukrainian diplomatic source as saying.
The sources said that Zelensky accelerated the government shakeup, hoping to appoint former Prime Minister Yulia Sviridenko to replace former envoy Olga Stefanishina, but he didn't count on Sviridenko rejecting his offer.
According to former Deputy Prime Minister for European Affairs Ivanna Klimpush-Tsintsadze, candidates who could potentially fill the role are wary of taking on the job.
Klimpush-Tsintsadze explained that the new ambassador should be part of Zelensky's inner circle, where there are no serious contenders.
On August 7, Verkhovna Rada deputy Dmitry Razumkov said that Washington had rejected Rustem Umerov's candidacy for the post of Ukrainian ambassador because of his ties to Timur Mindich, against whom a criminal case is currently being opened. Law enforcement agencies are also investigating the former ambassador of Ukraine to the United States, who is accused of illegal enrichment. According to the investigators, Stefanishina was negotiating the purchase of a $550,000 house near Kiev, while the official income would not have afforded her such an acquisition.

articles.title: Russia's inflation stabilizing, says economy minister
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 14. /TASS/. Inflation in Russia has stabilized. Economic Development Minister Maxim Reshetnikov said in an interview with the Vesti news program.
"The Bank of Russia is carefully but consistently lowering the key rate, and, of course, everyone recognizes the trend and sees inflation stabilizing," Reshetnikov said.
The minister noted that a certain level of uncertainty persists in the economy, driven in part by developments in the fuel market and recent terrorist attacks.
"At the same time, we see that our businesses and the broader economy are responding adequately, with companies promptly carrying out all necessary recovery work," he added.
As of August 10, 2026, year-on-year inflation in Russia stood at 6.06% (based on calculations using average daily data for this year and the previous year for corresponding dates), the Federal Statistics Service (Rosstat) reported earlier.
On July 24, 2026, the Bank of Russia decided to lower its key rate from 14.25% to 14% per annum, contrary to analysts’ forecasts that it would remain unchanged. That said, the Central Bank pointed to the need for a more gradual rate reduction, according to the regulator’s press release.

articles.title: Irregular border crossings into EU fall 37% in 1st 7 months of 2026
articles.body:
Aysu Bicer
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Irregular border crossings into the EU fell 37% in the first seven months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, with approximately 61,000 detections recorded at the bloc’s external borders, according to preliminary data released Friday by Frontex.
The figures do not include “the exceptional events at the external borders in Ceuta/Spain at the end of July,” the EU border agency said.
Between July 29 and 31, tens of thousands of Moroccans gathered near the border fence with Ceuta in what authorities described as the largest mass irregular migration attempt toward the enclave. Most later returned to Morocco.
Most major migratory routes recorded fewer crossings than in 2025, with the Eastern Mediterranean and Central Mediterranean routes accounting for around 60% of all detections.
The Eastern Mediterranean remained the busiest route, with 20,232 detections, down 28% year-on-year. The Central Mediterranean recorded 16,454 detections, a 55% decline, with Libya remaining the main country of departure.
The Western Mediterranean recorded around 11,500 detections and was the only major route to register an increase.
The Western African route saw the steepest decline, with detections falling 60% to 4,682, while the Western Balkans recorded 4,910 detections, down 26%. The Eastern Land Border registered 3,209 detections, a 44% decrease.
Frontex attributed the overall decline partly to continued cooperation with partner countries and preventive measures in key countries of departure that reduced crossings toward Europe.
Separately, attempted and successful Channel crossings toward the UK fell 46%, with 22,469 detections. These are counted as exits from the EU and are not included in the EU entry total.
Frontex said around 3,800 officers remain deployed at the EU’s external borders to support national authorities, including in implementing new rules under the Pact on Migration and Asylum.

articles.title: Over 650,000 refugees in South Sudan face aid crisis as funding dries up: UN
articles.body:
Benjamin Takpiny
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
More than 650,000 refugees and asylum seekers in South Sudan are at risk of losing access to vital food, nutrition, and other assistance due to critical funding shortfalls, leaving families who have fled war and hunger with nowhere else to turn, warned UNHCR, the UN refugee agency, and the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) on Friday.
The two UN agencies said in a joint statement that without immediate and urgent funding, the final food and nutrition assistance for the most vulnerable 240,000 refugees across the country will be provided in September.
"For hundreds of thousands of refugee families, the consequences of an interruption in critical aid would be immediate and long-lasting, including heightened risks of malnutrition, exploitation, and abuse of women and children. Of particular concern to UNHCR is the risk of yet more cross-border movement as people search for food and assistance," the statement said.
This warning comes as ongoing conflict across the region continues to force people to flee into neighboring countries in search of food, shelter, and safety. In South Sudan, up to 3,000 refugees and returnees continue to arrive from Sudan each week, further straining already overstretched humanitarian resources.
"We are seeing the devastating impact of conflicts that force people from their homes colliding with a severe shortage of resources that is now making the crisis worse," said Adham Effendi, deputy country director for WFP in South Sudan.
"Urgent support to save lives and livelihoods is vital," Effendi added.
According to the statement, WFP faces an immediate $37 million funding gap for its refugee response and an overall funding shortfall of $258 million for the remainder of 2026, threatening vital support for 4.2 million food-insecure people across the country. 
Meanwhile, UNHCR has secured only 28% of the $286 million needed this year to sustain core protection and assistance for nearly four million refugees, internally displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities.
"Every week, thousands more refugees and returnees continue to arrive from Sudan with almost nothing, many exhausted, hungry, and in urgent need of protection and assistance," said Mesfin Degefu, UNHCR deputy representative in South Sudan.
South Sudan has continued to uphold its open-door policy for refugees despite facing significant humanitarian and development challenges of its own. More than 1.4 million refugees and returnees have crossed into South Sudan since war erupted in Sudan in 2023.

articles.title: Bulgaria set to propose legislative changes to address youth violence
articles.body:
Burak Bir
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
The Bulgarian government will propose legislative changes to tackle youth violence by the end of September, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said Friday.
Speaking to journalists in the southern city of Plovdiv, Radev said his government will propose legislative changes to tackle youth violence by the end of September, Bulgarian news agency BTA reported.
"What is happening with some young people is extremely worrying," he noted.
The prime minister's remarks came after the killing of Georgi Kuzev, a 37-year-old man, at Youth Hill in Plovdiv.
A total of 10 teenagers aged between 14 and 17 were detained after Kuzev was killed in an assault in the area on Aug. 4. Five of them, three boys and two girls, were charged with murder and remanded in custody.
"The local municipal commissions are not working. Absolutely nothing is happening there. We must bring work in schools and with parents to the fore so that such things do not happen," he added.
Radev noted that restrictions on adolescents’ access to social media were also under consideration.

articles.title: Saudi royal court adviser thanks Turkish president for support for 2027 Spanish Super Cup in Istanbul
articles.body:
Emre Asikci and Seyit Kurt
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Saudi Royal Court adviser Turki Al-Sheikh on Friday thanked Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for his support for holding the 2027 Spanish Super Cup in Istanbul.
Al-Sheikh, who also chairs Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, said in a written statement that he was delighted the tournament would be held in Istanbul, describing the event as “only the beginning of a wonderful relationship.”
“I would also like to express my gratitude to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for all his support and for his instructions to hold this event in Istanbul and accomplish great things here,” he said.
Al-Sheikh also thanked Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for their support and approval of the event, as well as Bilal Erdogan, the son of President Erdogan, for his efforts throughout the process and for helping facilitate the organization in Istanbul.
He said he had met Bilal Erdogan in Istanbul about a month and a half ago, when they promised to bring “many surprises” with them.
“We promise that we will stage a tremendous event that will be a great success,” Al-Sheikh said, adding that a special night featuring artists and other surprises is planned for February.
“This is only the beginning of many surprises between two great countries with deeply rooted relations stretching back hundreds, even thousands of years,” he added.
The statement said Riyadh Season is sponsoring the Istanbul tournament under an agreement between the Spanish Football Federation and Saudi company Sela, in cooperation with the Turkish Football Federation.
It added that the event forms part of the continued presence of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority and Riyadh Season at international sporting events.
Atletico Madrid, Barcelona, Real Madrid and Real Sociedad will compete in the tournament, with matches scheduled for Feb. 2-7 at Istanbul’s Ataturk Olympic Stadium.

articles.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to let White House ballroom construction continue
articles.body:
Diyar Guldogan
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
The Trump administration on Friday asked the Supreme Court to clear the way for construction of the White House ballroom to continue, accusing lower courts of overstepping their authority and arguing that the project is necessary for national security.
In a filing signed by Solicitor General D. John Sauer, the administration sharply criticized the lower appellate panel's characterization of its position.
This project, like its predecessors, should be a matter for the president and the political process, not construction-by-injunction, Sauer said.
In the filing, the administration echoed Trump’s argument that the ballroom is essential to presidential security, citing multiple assassination attempts against the president.
"This case involves an extraordinary and unlawful injunction that will halt the ongoing construction of the integrated military complex, including a totally secure ballroom space, at the East Wing of the White House, which is vitally required by national security," the filing said.
The Trump administration's appeal to the Supreme Court follows a 2-1 ruling last Friday by the US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit that the ballroom project requires congressional approval, blocking above-ground construction while allowing underground work tied to new security features to continue.
Last year, President Donald Trump announced the construction of a 90,000-square-foot (8,361-square-meter) ballroom, which is estimated to cost $400 million.

articles.title: Serbia has no intention of joining NATO — Vucic
articles.body:
BELGRADE, August 14. /TASS/. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has reiterated that his country has no plans to join the North Atlantic Alliance.
"On the one hand, Montenegro, a NATO member, and on the other, Serbia, which is not and will not be a NATO member. Montenegro imposed sanctions against Russia, and Serbia did none of that," the Serbian president told journalists during a visit to the Expo 2027 construction sites.
On June 10, following a meeting with NATO Supreme Allied Commander-in-Chief Europe Alexus Grynkewich, Vucic stated that Belgrade will maintain military neutrality while simultaneously cooperating with the North Atlantic Alliance.

articles.title: French court rejects ex-RT bureau head’s appeal against her deportation
articles.body:
PARIS, August 14. /TASS/. Paris’ Administrative Court has once again turned down an appeal by former head of RT's bureau in France Ksenia Fyodorova challenging her deportation, AFP reported.
According to the court, "the condition of urgency required for the issuance of an interim ruling suspending enforcement has not been met." In early August, the court had also stated that there were insufficient grounds to suspend the decision in the interests of "the urgent protection of fundamental freedoms."
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told the BFMTV television channel earlier that the country’s authorities were working to expel Fyodorova. The economy and finance ministry blocked her French accounts. However, her residence permit had earlier been extended for ten more years. French President Emmanuel Macron refused to comment on why she had been granted a residence permit extension, saying that such issues are beyond his competences.
Fyodorova, the winner of the 2008 TEFI prize, or Russian national television award, in the category "Information Program," was put in charge of RT France in 2017. She reported the bureau’s closure in 2023 after its accounts were frozen. She currently takes part in programs on the French news channel CNews as an analyst.
Deputy director of the Russian foreign ministry’s information and press department, Alexey Fadeyev, slammed the French interior ministry’s decision as "an act of reprisal against a rebellious journalist." According to Fadeyev, this step was not a surprise for Russia as France tends to "see a Russian trail" behind all of the country’s problems.

articles.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to let White House ballroom construction continue
articles.body:
President Donald Trump on Friday asked the Supreme Court to allow construction of his White House ballroom to continue, one week after a federal appeals court ordered that the $400 million building project must come to a stop.
The Trump administration wants the Supreme Court to immediately block the lower court's preliminary injunction on further construction at the former site of the White House's East Wing, which the president had ripped down last year without notifying Congress.
The Aug. 7 ruling from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld an injunction issued by a federal district judge. The injunction is currently set to take effect next Friday, Aug. 21.
The National Trust for Historic Preservation, which brought the lawsuit, urged the Supreme Court not to let the ballroom construction go on while the Trump administration's appeal plays out.
"The Administration's transparent efforts to evade the rule of law, frustrate judicial review, and limit the availability of meaningful relief in the courts must stop here," the group said in a statement Friday afternoon.
Trump has increasingly argued that building the ballroom is a matter of national security and military readiness because it will include what he describes as a "drone port" on its roof.
In Friday's Supreme Court application, U.S. Solicitor General D. John Sauer highlighted the building's function as a military asset.
"This case involves an extraordinary and unlawful injunction that will halt the ongoing construction of the integrated military complex, including a totally secure ballroom space, at the East Wing of the White House, which is vitally required by national security," Sauer wrote.
If the appellate court's block is allowed to take effect, it "would wrongfully install a single district judge as sole arbiter of what further construction is 'strictly necessary' to protect the safety of the President, his family, staff members, and visitors to the White House, including foreign dignitaries, and presidents and prime ministers of other countries," Sauer wrote.

articles.title: Russia Rejects Black Sea Ceasefire, Says It Would Give Ukraine “Temporary Respite”
articles.body:
- Category
- World
Russia Rejects Black Sea Ceasefire, Says It Would Give Ukraine “Temporary Respite”
Russia has refused to accept a mutual ceasefire with Ukraine in the Black Sea, stating that it sees no grounds for such a measure and questioning whether Türkiye ever formally put the proposal to Moscow.
Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova set out the position on August 14, in comments published on the ministry's official channel, responding to a media question about a Turkish proposal for a moratorium on hostilities at sea.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Zakharova stated that Russia had not received a formalized Turkish appeal through official channels, one that would specify the conditions for the proposed moratorium.
That account is at odds with Ankara. On August 8, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan told Anadolu that Türkiye had relayed the initiative to both sides and urged them to build a mechanism for a Black Sea ceasefire.
Justifying the refusal, Zakharova pointed to what she described as repeated Ukrainian drone attacks on civilian vessels in the Black Sea, a framing that reflects Moscow's position rather than any independent confirmation.
She claimed Russia regularly faces "unbridled acts of terrorism" carried out by Ukrainian drones against merchant ships of coastal states.
"We do not see any prerequisites for improving the situation, and, consequently, grounds for half-measures that only give the Kyiv regime a temporary respite," Zakharova added.
She also ruled out reviving the 2022–2023 Black Sea Grain Initiative, under which Moscow briefly held off on strikes in exchange for its agricultural exports reaching world markets.
In Moscow's account, the deal collapsed because the West kept restrictions on Russian farm goods in place while the corridor was exploited for attacks on Russian targets, assertions advanced before without independent verification.
Moscow has tied any maritime arrangement to its broader demands over the war, including the removal of what it calls security threats stemming from NATO's eastward expansion and guarantees for Russian-speaking populations in Ukraine. On those terms, a narrow, sector-specific truce at sea appears unlikely in the near term, Armenian news outlet NEWS.am concluded.
The safety of civilian shipping in the Black Sea has been eroding from both directions for months. Over the summer, repeated Russian missile strikes on foreign-flagged merchant ships at Ukrainian ports killed crew members aboard cargo ships flying flags including those of Togo, Tanzania, and Liberia.
One July strike on the Odesa region alone left a sailor dead and three others wounded aboard an Antigua and Barbuda-flagged cargo ship.

articles.title: Ukraine’s Strikes Wipe Out Wildberries’ Major Warehouses as Losses Near $12 Billion
articles.body:
- Category
- World
Ukraine’s Strikes Wipe Out Wildberries’ Major Warehouses as Losses Near $12 Billion
Ukraine’s campaign targeting Wildberries has destroyed all of the Russian e-commerce giant’s major warehouses and roughly one-third of its total warehouse capacity, according to estimates cited by Forbes on August 13.
Direct losses suffered by Wildberries from the destruction of its logistics infrastructure had reached 147–223 billion rubles (around $1.75–$2.66 billion) by mid-August, Data Insight lead analyst Sergey Semko estimated for Forbes. Including the costs of dismantling damaged structures, removing debris, and restoring the affected sites, the losses could rise to 278 billion rubles (approximately $3.32 billion).
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Wildberries sellers have also suffered substantial losses. Semko estimated that merchandise destroyed in the attacks was worth between 445 billion (about $5.31 billion) and 507 billion rubles (nearly $6.1 billion), putting the combined losses for the company and its sellers at around 800 billion rubles (almost $10 billion).
Margaret Evstigneeva, head of the Association of Suppliers of Goods for E-Commerce Platforms, placed the losses incurred by sellers even higher, estimating them at 600–700 billion rubles ($7.16–$8.35 billion). Combined with Wildberries’ losses, the total damage could therefore approach 1 trillion rubles (around $11.9 billion).
“Many lost up to 95% of all their goods. At the same time, Wildberries considers itself the affected party and paid small sellers an average of 2,000–30,000 rubles, which covered less than 20% of their losses,” Evstigneeva said.
Just a week earlier, Ukrainian long-range Liutyi strike drones targeted a Wildberries logistics facility in Yekaterinburg, Russia’s Sverdlovsk region, traveling more than 1,700 kilometers before reaching the site.
Footage from the site showed multiple fires burning beneath the roof of the large warehouse complex. Wildberries later confirmed that its logistics facility had come under attack and that a fire had broken out.

articles.title: Trump adviser, Gaza envoy to visit Israel for talks on US plan
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner is due in Israel next week for discussions on Washington’s efforts to move forward with its Gaza initiative, according to an Axios report, with Board of Peace representative Nickolay Mladenov expected to join the visit.
The planned trip would be Kushner’s first visit to Israel since January, the news outlet said in a report citing five sources familiar with the plan.
Kushner and Mladenov intend to meet Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other Israeli officials in an effort to reach understandings on implementing the plan’s next stages over the coming months, it added.
Netanyahu on Sunday rejected a 15-point Gaza plan approved by the Board of Peace and accepted by Hamas, insisting that the Palestinian group must be disarmed before any further Israeli withdrawal from the enclave.
His remarks came despite a roadmap issued by the board on July 31 which calls for Hamas’ disarmament and a gradual Israeli withdrawal to proceed in parallel.
Axios quoted a US official as saying that "we see eye-to-eye on the strategic goal, but Israel has expressed some doubts about the plan and we want to talk to them in order to make sure we are coordinated.”
The White House does not want the Israeli elections to stall the implementation of the next phase of the plan, the report said.
Another US official said the Trump administration understands Netanyahu’s political needs.
"We have no problem with it as long as he continues to do what we ask - especially regarding restraining attacks in Gaza,” the official was quoted as saying.
Hamas official Ghazi Hamad previously told Anadolu that the agreement stipulated the "storage of heavy weapons” under the authority of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, in parallel with progress on the other components of the deal.
The roadmap also provides for transferring Gaza’s administration to a Palestinian technocratic committee, deploying an international stabilization force and placing weapons under the national committee’s authority with international oversight.
These measures would proceed alongside a phased Israeli withdrawal and reconstruction.
Since Oct. 2023, Israel’s war on Gaza, backed by the US, has killed around 73,000 Palestinians and injured more than 174,000, most of them women and children. The offensive has also damaged or destroyed nearly 90% of the enclave’s infrastructure.

articles.title: Thames Water plans to restart desalination plant – after drought has ended
articles.body:
Thames Water is preparing the UK’s only desalination plant to restart operations later this year – but it will not be ready until the winter, long after the current drought is likely to have passed.
The utility company said that it was hoping to start operating its plant in Beckton, east London, “by the end of the year”, in order to help build up reservoir supplies over the winter for next summer.
Water companies across the UK have imposed hosepipe bans as they try to conserve supplies, with much of the country enduring a fifth heatwave that is worsening drought conditions.
The Beckton plant has only ever run five times, providing just 7.2bn litres of drinking water or about seven days’ worth of the capital’s daily demand over 15 years.
Desalination plants are widely used in the Middle East to provide drinking water. Yet the desalination plant in Beckton has long been regarded as a white elephant.
Thames Water, which supplies 16 million customers in London and the Thames valley, fully opened the plant in 2011, spending an initial £270m to install it. It was designed to use seawater from the Thames estuary in times of drought. However, for the past 15 years it has barely operated. The total cost of the plant is now counted at £500m, providing a meagre return for customers who funded it through their bills.
Thames Water’s performance during the drought will be closely scrutinised, with the prime minister, Andy Burnham, due to decide the company’s future in the coming weeks.
A Thames Water spokesperson said: “Preparations are under way at the Thames Gateway water treatment works in Beckton, east London, so it can be brought online by the end of the year, if needed, to help support reservoir recovery over the winter.
“Any decision to use the desalination plant will depend on weather conditions, demand, and reservoir levels in the coming weeks.”
Burnham on Thursday said he was angry and that water customers were not a “bottomless source of funding” after 13 companies were allowed to increase bills to fund extra projects. Thames Water was one of five companies permitted to raise bills in the next four years.
However, operating the Beckton plant may not be financially attractive for Thames Water, given the high cost of electricity. Thames Water is already under severe financial pressure. Its creditors have effectively been in control of the business for two years, but they are seeking leeway from the government on fines for pollution before formally taking over.
Chris Weston, Thames Water’s chief executive, last year told MPs on the environment committee that the Beckton plant had serious problems. The company’s engineers were “working very hard to try to make it work”, he said.
The plant relies on treatment membranes to allow water but not salt to pass through. Weston said the membranes were last year at the end of their life, but the company was unable to replace them because there was no testing facility they could use on the new ones.
“The desalination plant is a big problem for us,” Weston said. “I wonder why it was built in the first place. It is not a good story, it was not a good investment, and there are no excuses about it.”
MPs have expressed frustration in recent years that the plant has not been available to provide drinking water during heatwaves.
Operating the plant in cooler temperatures could, however, prove more financially viable if wind power is in abundance and there is less strain on the grid, meaning electricity prices could be lower.

articles.title: West Bank settler attacks continue despite international uproar
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Israeli settler attacks in West Bank continue despite international outrage
Israeli forces and settlers continued their assault against Palestinian communities across the occupied West Bank on Friday despite mounting international condemnation over the siege of homes in Qusra and escalating attacks elsewhere.
In Qusra, south of Nablus, settlers remained near Palestinian homes for a sixth consecutive day, while Israeli forces prevented foreign and Israeli solidarity activists from reaching besieged families with water and other basic supplies.
The siege has drawn unusually sharp criticism from Washington, with White House officials pressing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settlers after learning that one of the affected homes belongs to a Palestinian American.
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee -- a supporter of the settler movement -- described those responsible as "Israeli terrorists" and their actions as "criminal", while France condemned what it called the "occupation" of Palestinian homes and called on Israeli authorities to arrest and prosecute those responsible.
Amid the criticism, Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz ordered the military to prepare a plan to transfer civilian law enforcement in the occupied West Bank to the police.
"The army's role is to combat Palestinian terrorism ... and not chase hilltop youth," Katz said, using a term commonly applied to hardline young settlers involved in establishing unauthorised outposts and attacks on Palestinians.
Under the proposal, Israel Police would establish a dedicated force to handle civilian matters in the occupied territory.
Settlers returned on Friday morning to an outpost near Palestinian homes in Qusra, erecting a canopy in the presence of soldiers. Border Police later dismantled it, but the settlers remained nearby.
The confrontation has centred on the Ras al-Ain area west of Qusra, where settlers established an outpost between three Palestinian homes belonging to the families of brothers Rizq and Youssef Hassan and Qusay Abu Rida.
Residents have been prevented from moving freely and accessing basic necessities, while settlers last month cut water and electricity supplies to three neighbouring homes, according to the UN Human Rights Office.
Mohammad Joudat, a media activist from Qusra, told The New Arab that foreign and Israeli solidarity activists attempted on Friday to bring water and other supplies to the besieged families.
"Israeli forces arrived at the scene, prevented them from reaching the homes and completely removed them from the area," Joudat said.
Israeli forces entered Qusra on Thursday and evacuated the three homes before gathering their residents in one of them.
Local reports said the army subsequently informed residents of 16 homes that they would have to evacuate so they could be used as military positions.
The UN Human Rights Office said settlers had consolidated control over the area west of Qusra since an outpost was established there in November 2025.
Residents have since faced home invasions, physical assaults, theft, vandalism and arson, including an attack on a mosque, it said.
The UN office said the latest actions, carried out with Israeli support or acquiescence, were making life "intolerable" for Palestinian families and were clearly aimed at forcing them from their homes and land.
Taybeh faces continued attacks
The events in Qusra come amid a wider escalation in settler attacks across the occupied West Bank, including in Taybeh, the territory's last entirely Christian Palestinian village.
Israel declared Taybeh a closed military zone earlier this month, saying the measure was intended to protect residents following repeated settler attacks.
But Ihab Hassan, a Palestinian Christian activist, told The New Arab that attacks had continued despite the closure, while journalists, foreign activists and other outside observers faced restrictions on entering the village.
"No, the Israeli army is not protecting the residents. I say this based on what is actually happening on the ground," Hassan said.
"Israeli settler attacks on the village have continued even after it was declared a closed military zone. The difference now is that journalists, foreign activists, and other outside observers face restrictions on entering."
Hassan said international and Israeli activists had previously provided a protective presence in Taybeh, sometimes placing themselves between settlers and Palestinian residents.
"Restricting their access while settlers continue to reach and attack the village has left the community even more isolated and vulnerable," he said.
Hassan said the situation reflected a broader pattern across the occupied territory.
"In some cases, the army says it will 'remove' the settlers, but the fact that an army claims it cannot remove settlers who are besieging Palestinian families speaks for itself," he said.
He argued that settlers were also seeking to exploit the current political environment to seize land and establish realities that would be difficult to reverse.
"Once families are driven from their homes, land and property are taken over, and new facts are established on the ground, reversing them becomes extraordinarily difficult, even under a future Israeli government that might take a different approach," Hassan said.
"For Taybeh, this is therefore not simply about individual attacks," he added.
"It is about whether the last entirely Christian Palestinian village in the West Bank can remain on its land."

articles.title: Croatia wildfire near Omiš injures residents and disrupts holiday travel
articles.body:
Fourteen people were taken to hospital, with seven reportedly in a life-threatening condition early on Friday. Parts of Omiš lost power as the fire approached the town centre, while homes, cars and boats were damaged or destroyed. Evacuees spent the night in a sports hall, sleeping on beds and floors.
Residents described chaotic scenes as they fled the advancing flames. Omiš fire brigade commander Slavko Tučaković said numerous homes and vehicles had been destroyed, causing extensive damage to property, the natural environment and wildlife.
Firefighters brought the blaze under control by Friday, while crews were also deployed to another wildfire on the Pelješac peninsula. Authorities said there were no fatalities.
The fires came at the height of Croatia’s summer tourist season, threatening to disrupt travel and put further pressure on the local economy. Sections of the main coastal road near Omiš were closed, affecting links between Split and Dubrovnik as well as day trips and coach tours. Damage to homes, cafés, restaurants, cars and boats could also reduce the area’s tourism capacity at a time when demand is at its peak.

articles.title: Putin wants to dismantle NATO and the EU from within; he has assigned Moldova a key role in this - NYT
articles.body:
Putin wants to dismantle NATO and the EU from within; he has assigned Moldova a key role in this - NYT
Kyiv • UNN
The Russian dictator set a task for 2026 at a secret briefing: the breakup of NATO and the EU from within. Moldova plays a key role in this, where Moscow is interfering in the elections.
At the end of last year, Putin gathered his inner circle for a secret briefing to convey the task for 2026: the "collapse of NATO and the EU from within." Moldova plays a key role in achieving this goal, UNN reports, citing The New York Times.
Details
According to the authors of the publication, in this tiny country, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, organized a voter-bribery scheme, and set up training camps for election interference - all with the aim of overthrowing the pro-Western government and President Maia Sandu.
The Kremlin’s campaign included methods familiar from other Western countries, such as hacking attacks and disinformation. However, in Moldova, this interference may have gone further than anywhere else outside Ukraine and is one of Putin’s largest and boldest efforts to destabilize the West
At the same time, Russian officials publicly deny interfering in Moldova’s affairs and reject accusations that Moscow is trying to undermine the authority of the West.
In December last year, Putin sharply criticized European leaders in an address to the Russian military command for "stoking hysteria" over the threat from Russia. However, shortly afterward, he gathered his inner circle for a secret briefing to deliver a directly opposite message, according to officials from two countries familiar with the event. "Your goal for 2026," Putin told them, "is the collapse of NATO and the EU from within"
Moldova plays a key role in these efforts. According to Western intelligence officials, the Kremlin’s top priority is the conquest of Ukraine, while second is establishing control over Moldova. Although Moldova is not a member of the European Union or NATO, it has a strategic location, situated between NATO member states and Ukraine.
Moldova would become an ideal staging ground for Russia’s further aggression against Ukraine or the West, officials said, adding that Putin still hopes to seize part of southern Ukraine to create a land corridor connecting Russia with Moldova.
A map of Russian troop movements published by Belarusian dictator Alexander Lukashenko at the beginning of the full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022, showed that one of the Kremlin’s objectives was to reach Transnistria via southern Ukraine - a separatist region of Moldova where an operational group of Russian troops is stationed, the successor to the 14th Soviet and Russian Army. However, the Kremlin did not achieve this goal.
Russia wants to use Moldova as a staging ground for hostile actions against Ukraine, as well as against its main defense and financial allies - the EU and NATO
Previously
The director of Moldova’s SIS, Alexandru Musteață, said that Russia had intensified disinformation campaigns and was preparing to interfere in the next elections.
