- list 2 of 3Israel’s ‘Green Rafah’ plan aims to fragment Gaza, experts say
- list 3 of 3What now as Israel rejects Trump’s 15-point plan for Gaza?
Netanyahu specifically opposed a provision of the plan that would see Hamas gradually disarm, transferring its weapons to a Palestinian third party, with Israel concurrently withdrawing its troops from Gaza. Hamas announced in it had agreed to a preliminary version of the deal and has said that it remains committed following Israel’s rejection.
An official with the Board of Peace, which was launched as part of a broader Gaza “ceasefire” agreement reached between Israel and Hamas in late 2025, said Kushner will be accompanied by the board’s director general, former Bulgarian government minister Nickolay Mladenov, and executive committee member, former British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
The official said the trio will “hear the concerns that have been raised and talk about next steps”.
“What is critical is that we both agree on the desired outcome and are finding ways to accelerate progress,” said the official, who maintained that both the Board of Peace and Israel “agree on the end state, which is a demilitarised Hamas”.
In Cairo, the official said Kushner, Mladenov, and Blair will meet Egyptian and other mediators, and will seek to solidify a roadmap.
Repeated ceasefire violations
Hamas’s approval of the preliminary disarmament agreement has been seen as a major breakthrough, even as details of implementation have remained undefined.
Under the 20-point ceasefire plan for Gaza signed last year, fighting was meant to be halted by both sides to pave the way for Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups to decommission their weapons and for Israel to withdraw from Gaza.
After that, the agreement calls for Hamas to transfer power to a technocratic Palestinian government, for an International Stabilisation Force to be deployed, and for a major reconstruction effort to begin.
However, there have been near-daily Israeli violations, with local authorities reporting that at least 1,260 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire went into effect.
All told, 73,389 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in the wake of the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on October 7, 2023.
Israel, meanwhile, has gradually expanded its area of control in Gaza, accounting for about 70 percent of the enclave.
Settler violence surges
Kushner’s visit also comes as settler violence, which rights groups have long maintained is enabled by Israel’s military forces, has surged in the occupied West Bank.
That has included a settler siege on the village of Qusra in the Nablus government, where residents say they have been cut off from water and electricity as part of an attempted land seizure.
The violence has prompted a rare rebuke from US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, who pointed to a specific case of settlers targeting the home of a dual US citizen in Qusra.
“Actions by those who carried out this horrific act of terror meant to intimidate and harass this family are disgusting,” Huckabee wrote in a post on X. “No excuse for such thuggish behaviour.”
He added that the US embassy has been “VERY involved & the [Israeli military] & Israel Police have gone at our request to remove the Israeli terrorists doing this”.
Huckabee has remained a staunch supporter of Israel and a vocal supporter of Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which are illegal under international law.
The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has documented 3,033 settler attacks in the West Bank between January 2025 and June 2026, averaging about six a day.
Israeli forces and settlers have killed 76 Palestinians, including 18 children, in the occupied territory so far in 2026, according to the UN.

articles.title: Brussels central square transformed into giant Japan-inspired flower carpet
articles.body:
Inspired by Hokusai’s 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa,' the carpet features more than 700,000 flowers and measures approximately 70 metres long and 24 metres wide.
The cobblestones of Brussels’ Grand-Place have been transformed into a vibrant floral display as the Belgian capital celebrates the 24th edition of its Flower Carpet, this year inspired by Japan.
Japanese artist Hiro Sugiyama designed this year’s composition, a reinterpretation of Katsushika Hokusai's iconic woodblock print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa".
Using over 700,000 flowers, mostly dahlias—a Belgian floral classic—the design pays tribute to Hokusai's 200-year-old masterpiece. Sugiyama said the carpet brings a piece of contemporary Japanese culture to Belgium.
The Japanese artist spent eight months developing the design, and had initially planned to make the composition even more colourful, but explained he was limited to a palette of 16 colours due to time constraints.
"To be honest, at the beginning, I was pretty nervous about [the limited colours palette], but once I came here and saw the design and the flowers laid out, I was very excited and realised that I didn't need to worry about it at all, because it looks beautiful already," Sugiyama said.
Belgium-Japan 160th anniversary
The Belgian-Japanese collaboration marks the 160th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two nations, and comes a decade after the first Flower Carpet collaboration in 2016.
Brussels Flower Carpet Organisation member, Richard Poncint, said the carpet is more than just an artwork, but is also a symbol of bringing people and cultures together.
"Culture events show people that we can work together, we can do interesting things together and that's one of the things we do here also with our Japanese friends," Poncin said.
Once a theme has been chosen, the number of flowers are calculated and colour palette is chosen, the organisers explain. Several days before the carpet is assembled, a full-size design is drawn on a large cotton canvas laid out on the city square.
On Thursday, more than a hundred volunteers worked for approximately six hours to arrange the flowers into the artwork the artist had intended.
Japanese Ambassador to Belgium, Takeshi Osuga, was also present, helping to lay the flowers.
"A lot of Japanese sponsors contributed to this event and I wanted to contribute by laying out the flowers," Osuga said.
The Flower Carpet returns back to the historic central square in the Belgian capital every two years, with the first display dating back to 1971.
The carpet is 70 metres long and 24 metres wide, and consists of dahlias, begonias, grass and bark. Visitors can walk around the carpet or view it from the balcony of the Town Hall.
The 2026 Flower Carpet is on display from August 13 to 16. While all sold out online, tickets can be bought at the venue itself during opening hours at the entrance of the Town Hall.

articles.title: Ukrainians invest over US$11m in Vyriy drone production in just one day
articles.body:
Ukrainians invest over US$11m in Vyriy drone production in just one day
The Inzhur MilTech fund, through which Ukrainian citizens can invest in drone production by Vyriy Industries, has raised over UAH 500 million (around US$11 million) on its first day.
Source: Vyriy Industries
Details: Vyriy Industries reported: "12,239 investors took part, and the average investment was UAH 40,819 [US$912]."
The company said the funds raised will be used to expand production and purchase components. It says its products are used by over 200 units in Ukraine's defence forces.
Launched on 13 August, the Inzhur MilTech fund allows private investors to finance the scaling up of unmanned systems production by Vyriy Industries. The investment programme is open until 31 December 2026.
Background:
- Investors purchase Inzhur MilTech fund certificates, and the funds raised are invested in Vyriy Industries corporate bonds. The minimum investment is UAH 1,000 (US$22).
- Inzhur is a Ukrainian investment company through which private investors can invest in funds and bonds.
- Vyriy Industries is a well-known Ukrainian drone manufacturer. Recently, together with Noctis, the company presented the Zirka, an interceptor drone designed to counter Shahed-type UAVs. The drone has a declared speed of up to 340 km/h.

articles.title: Farewell ceremony for Ukrainian leader Colonel Konovalets held in Kyiv – photos
articles.body:
Farewell ceremony held in Kyiv for 20th-century Ukrainian military leader Yevhen Konovalets – photos, video
The 3rd Army Corps has held a farewell ceremony for Colonel Yevhen Konovalets, a founder of the Ukrainian Military Organisation (UVO) and the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) and commander of the Sich Riflemen Corps.
Source: Ukrainska Pravda journalists at the scene; 3rd Army Corps
Details: The ceremony took place at the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Patriarchal Cathedral of the Resurrection of Christ on the first night after Colonel Konovalets' remains were returned to Ukraine.
Quote from Andrii Biletskyi, Commander of the 3rd Army Corps: "Two generations meet here today. Colonel Konovalets represents the generation of the Sich Riflemen, the Black Zaporozhians An elite cavalry formation of the Ukrainian People's Republic Army , and the fighters of the UVO, OUN and Ukrainian Insurgent Army A Ukrainian nationalist resistance force active during and after World War II . We are the generation of the Maidans, the Anti-Terrorist Operation The ATO or Anti-Terrorist Operation is a term used from 2014 to 2018 by the media and the government to identify combat actions in parts of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts against Russian military forces and pro-Russian separatists and the full-scale Russia-Ukraine war. Each of these generations inherited the Ukrainian cause unfinished.
We are the first generation with a real chance to break this heavy chain and complete the work of the colonel and all our great predecessors – the struggle for a great, powerful and united Ukraine – so that we no longer have to pass this heavy duty on to our children and future generations."
Details: Konovalets' coffin was brought to the cathedral by an original Austin armoured car dating back to the time of the Ukrainian Revolution, which had been restored by service members of the 3rd Army Corps' repair and recovery battalion.
Outside the cathedral, Konovalets' coffin was met by a guard of honour carrying torches, composed of members of the 3rd Army Corps and the Yevhen Konovalets Military School.
A gun carriage was attached to the Austin armoured car, a gesture traditionally used in Ukraine and Europe as a sign of the highest military honours.
A three-inch gun was also attached to the armoured vehicle – an original 1917 model that had been in service with the army of the Ukrainian People's Republic, specifically the Sich Riflemen Division commanded by Colonel Konovalets.
Background:
- Yevhen Konovalets was a key figure in the Ukrainian liberation movement of the first half of the 20th century. He commanded the Sich Riflemen Corps, one of the most combat-effective units of the Ukrainian People's Republic Army, and was a founder of the Ukrainian Military Organisation and the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists.
- In 1938, Konovalets was assassinated in Rotterdam by Soviet intelligence agent Pavel Sudoplatov. The colonel was buried at Crooswijk Cemetery in Rotterdam, with the intention that he would eventually be reburied in his homeland after Ukraine regained its independence.
- On 13 August, the remains of Yevhen Konovalets were brought to Ukraine.
- On 25 May, the remains of former OUN leader Andrii Melnyk and his wife Sofiia Fedak-Melnyk were reburied at the National Military Memorial Cemetery.
- On Constitution Day 2026, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy submitted a bill to the Verkhovna Rada (Parliament) on establishing a Ukrainian National Pantheon to honour prominent Ukrainians.
- The government approved the establishment of the Ukrainian National Pantheon in the grounds of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra. The Ukrainian Institute of National Memory will be responsible for developing the project.

articles.title: Russia to create ‘Rapist-Pedophile’ database
articles.body:
Russia plans to build a unified electronic database of people who have committed sexual violence against minors, Anastasia Udaltsova, a deputy in the State Duma, the lower house of Russia’s parliament, told Ksenia Sobchak’s Telegram channel Krovavaya Barynya (“Bloody Lady”).
The channel’s editors published screenshots of a response from Russian Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov to a June request Udaltsova had sent him. The document says the Interior Ministry is already conducting “research and development work” on the registry and plans to launch it in 2027. Udaltsova did not post the letter to her own Telegram channel, but she reposted coverage of it from Sobchak’s channel and two others.
The Telegram channel Baza, which has ties to Russian security services, had already reported on the registry’s creation, citing its own sources. The Russian news outlet Expert published a similar report after speaking with Udaltsova, and its journalists say they, too, have obtained the document Sobchak’s channel cited.
All three sources say the new registry will be called “Rapist-Pedophile,” though Manturov’s letter does not mention that name. Expert reported that the database will be closed, accessible only to Interior Ministry employees. Udaltsova opposes this limitation, saying the registry should be made public.
It remains unclear what criteria will determine who is included in the database: in particular, whether it will cover people whose criminal records have already been expunged.
The idea of creating such a database in Russia has been discussed for at least the past decade. In 2025, Sergei Mironov, chairman of the A Just Russia party, sent the proposal to Alexander Bastrykin, head of the Investigative Committee, Russia’s federal investigating authority. Mironov argued that creating “open databases of pedophiles is consistent with international practice.”
In July, the Digital Development Ministry published a draft doctrine outlining goals for developing a system to combat internet-based crime. The document said the possibility of creating such a registry should be considered, but it set no earlier than 2029 for implementing any of the proposed mechanisms.

articles.title: Bomb-disposal team, light public housing unit win chief executive’s award
articles.body:
Bomb-disposal team, light public housing unit win chief executive’s award
Hong Kong leader John Lee praises teams for embodying professional spirit of civil servants in ‘rising to challenges and pursuing excellence’
A bomb-disposal team and a unit behind Hong Kong’s light public housing scheme have won this year’s chief executive’s award, praised for embodying civil servants’ professional spirit in “rising to challenges and pursuing excellence”.
City leader John Lee Ka-chiu presented the Chief Executive’s Award for Exemplary Performance to the two interdepartmental teams at a ceremony on Friday.
Lee praised them for fulfilling their duties with a steadfast sense of mission and exceptional competence, winning public trust through tangible results.
“From the professionalism and solidarity demonstrated in handling a wartime bomb to the efficiency and innovation in building light public housing, civil servants have displayed a service spirit of utmost dedication, willingness to take on challenges and readiness to shoulder responsibilities,” he said.
The award recognises meritorious and exemplary teams or individuals in the civil service.
Last September, a 1,000-pound (454kg) wartime bomb, containing 500 pounds of high explosives and having enormous destructive potential, was discovered at a construction site in Quarry Bay. About 2,900 residents from 18 buildings were evacuated. Officers successfully defused the bomb after a nine-hour operation.

articles.title: Multi-property owner loses HK$10 million after fraudster poses as possible tenant
articles.body:
Multi-property owner loses HK$10 million after fraudster poses as possible tenant
Woman duped into bogus friendship by scammer, who promised tips on how to make money fast with cryptocurrencies
Police said that while no tenancy agreement was signed, the con artist struck up a friendship with the woman and claimed they could teach her how to invest in cryptocurrency, framing it as “the next opportunity to get rich”.
The scammer gave the victim step-by-step instructions on how to set up a cryptocurrency wallet, but tricked her into revealing her wallet details and password, before persuading her to invest large sums of money.
The woman then spent about HK$10 million on cryptocurrencies, which the scammer then transferred out of her digital wallet.
She only realised the deception when she discovered her cryptocurrency wallet was empty.

articles.title: La Liga returns: What to expect from 2026-27 season
articles.body:
Efe Ozkan
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Less than a month after Spain lifted the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the country's top-tier La Liga league returns with Barcelona chasing a third straight title and Jose Mourinho beginning his second spell at Real Madrid.
The 2026-27 campaign officially gets underway on Aug. 15, although several opening-round fixtures involving World Cup semifinalists have been postponed to allow players their mandatory rest period following the expanded 48-team tournament.
Barcelona remain team to beat
Hansi Flick's Barcelona enter the season as favorites after winning back-to-back La Liga titles and adding the 2026 World Cup to a remarkable summer dominated by Spanish internationals.
The Catalan club's core remains intact, with Lamine Yamal, Pedri, Dani Olmo, Pau Cubarsi and Mikel Oyarzabal expected to spearhead another title challenge.
Barcelona's success has been built on the same possession-heavy identity that conquered Europe in 2024, but Flick's side has evolved into a more vertical and aggressive attacking team.
Mourinho reshapes Real Madrid
The biggest storyline of the summer is Jose Mourinho's return to the Santiago Bernabeu.
After two trophyless seasons, Real Madrid have embarked on a major sporting reset under the Portuguese coach, with president Florentino Perez backing an ambitious restructuring of the squad.Kylian Mbappe remains the centerpiece of Madrid's attack, while Bernardo Silva and Ibrahima Konate headline a wave of elite arrivals designed to restore balance throughout the team.
Vinicius Junior has also committed his long-term future to the club, while Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to become a key figure under Mourinho following Dani Carvajal's departure.
Mourinho inherits enormous expectations, but questions remain over whether Madrid's midfield can fully replace the influence once provided by Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.
Atletico seek to end title drought
Diego Simeone begins another campaign knowing Atletico Madrid cannot afford to fall further behind Spain's top two.
Despite remaining one of La Liga's strongest defensive sides, Atletico have endured another frustrating trophyless spell.
Julian Alvarez continues to lead the attack, while Simeone will hope another summer of squad reinforcement finally produces a genuine championship challenge.
European hopefuls, survival battle
Beyond the traditional giants, Villarreal, Athletic Club, Real Betis and Real Sociedad are all expected to compete for Champions League qualification.
Sevilla aim to re-establish themselves in the European places after several inconsistent seasons.
Newly promoted Racing Santander, Deportivo La Coruna and Malaga return to Spain's top flight hoping to avoid an immediate return to the Segunda Division.
Levante and Elche also enter the campaign among the clubs tipped to be involved in a tightly contested relegation battle.
With Mourinho back in Madrid, Barcelona pursuing a third straight title and a new generation of Spanish stars entering their prime, the 2026-27 season promises a closely watched title race.

articles.title: Morocco tightens security ahead of calls for mass crossing into Spain’s Ceuta
articles.body:
Khalid Mejdoub and Sahin Demir
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Morocco stepped up security measures Friday in the northern city of Fnideq and other areas ahead of social media calls for a mass attempt to cross into the Spanish-administered enclave of Ceuta.
An Anadolu correspondent said authorities reinforced checkpoints leading to Fnideq, as well as the northern cities of Tetouan, Tangier, and Nador.
Authorities also installed barbed wire along the border crossing between Fnideq and Ceuta while deploying large numbers of security personnel and auxiliary forces across the city.
The measures came ahead of Aug. 15 after Morocco’s Interior Ministry said it had detected anonymous social media calls urging a mass illegal crossing into the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla.
On Wednesday, Interior Ministry spokesperson Rachid El Khalfi said authorities had monitored anonymous posts and messages circulating on social media in recent days encouraging attempts to organize an illegal mass crossing into the two enclaves.
He described the calls as posing serious risks to people’s safety and said they sought to exploit migration issues through acts of incitement punishable under Moroccan law.
El Khalfi said authorities were closely monitoring the situation and taking necessary measures to prevent illegal crossing attempts and intercept those involved.
The Ceuta border witnessed its largest irregular crossing wave in recent years between July 29 and 31, when tens of thousands of Moroccans headed toward the enclave before most returned to Fnideq.
Last Friday, Morocco’s National Human Rights Council said the death toll from the Ceuta crossing wave had risen to 14, while Spanish figures put the number of fatalities at 80.
Moroccan authorities estimated that around 40,000 people attempted the crossing, while Spanish authorities said the number exceeded 70,000.
Ceuta and Melilla are located on Morocco’s northern coast but remain under Spanish administration. Morocco claims sovereignty over both enclaves.

articles.title: Türkiye’s Sonmez advances to Cincinnati Open tennis 2nd round
articles.body:
Halis Sunnetci
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Turkish tennis player Zeynep Sonmez rallied to beat Australia’s Daria Kasatkina 2-6, 7-6(4), 6-3 on Thursday and advance to the second round of the Cincinnati Open.
The 24-year-old recovered after losing the opening set, winning the second-set tiebreak 7-4 before taking the decider 6-3.
Sonmez converted six of seven break points, compared with six of 12 for Kasatkina, who committed 11 double faults.
The players finished level with 95 points each, highlighting the closely contested nature of the match.
Sonmez will face world No. 10 Amanda Anisimova from the US in the second round on Saturday.
The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) 1000 tournament is played on outdoor hard courts in the US state of Ohio.

articles.title: France's top court strikes down under-15 social media ban
articles.body:
France's top court has blocked a bill banning social media access for under-15s, saying it infringed upon freedom of expression, a setback for President Emmanuel Macron, who asked his government to rewrite the legislation.
"By prohibiting minors under the age of fifteen from accessing certain online services, the law inherently requires every person, even an adult, to prove their age before accessing them," the Constitutional Council said in its decision on Friday.
"However, by failing to specify the conditions and limits under which such proof must be provided, the legislature has not established the legal safeguards necessary to ensure compliance with these requirements," it added.
French lawmakers had approved a ban on social media access for children under age 15, becoming the first in Europe to follow Australia, whose world-first ban barred access to platforms including Facebook, TikTok and YouTube for under-16s in December.
Macron has ordered Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to rework the draft legislation to take the Constitutional Council's concerns into account, the Elysee said in a statement.
The Elysee said Macron was determined the reform would take effect before spring 2027, when France holds a presidential election.
Macron cannot run for a third term.

articles.title: Wildberries and other marketplaces ask Russian government for hundreds of billions of roubles in aid
articles.body:
Wildberries and other marketplaces ask Russian government for hundreds of billions of roubles in aid
The Association of Digital Platforms (ADP), which brings together Wildberries, Ozon, Yandex, Avito and Kuper, has proposed that the Russian government introduce a package of support measures for businesses affected by drone attacks.
Source: ADP's letter to Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin on 12 August, as reported by Russian media outlet Vedomosti
Details: One of the measures proposed by the ADP is direct one-off payments from the federal budget. The companies say this would allow businesses to resume operations at their usual capacity, as well as preserve businesses and jobs.
According to the association, the amount of such support should be calculated based on the actual damage suffered and the scale of operations of each individual organisation.
In addition, affected businesses are proposing that they be granted a six-month deferral or instalment plan for paying taxes and mandatory contributions, while penalties and fines should be temporarily suspended during periods when they were objectively unable to operate normally.
Another Russian media outlet, The Moscow Times, reports that the amount requested by the ADP is estimated at hundreds of billions of roubles. In particular, goods worth between 445 billion roubles and 507 billion roubles (US$5.2-6 billion) were destroyed in fires at Wildberries warehouses following a series of attacks.
The Association of Suppliers of Goods for Trade on Electronic Platforms (APTEP) estimates sellers' losses even higher, at 600-700 billion roubles (US$7.1-8.3 billion)
Meanwhile, Wildberries itself, which lost around a third of its warehouse capacity, suffered direct losses estimated at 147-223 billion roubles (US$1.7-2.6 billion), according to DataInsight.
This figure rises to 278 billion roubles (US$3.3 billion) when the costs of dismantling structures, removing waste and restoring the affected sites are taken into account.
Background:
- Following attacks on Wildberries, some Russian marketplaces began changing their terms for sellers and removing their liability for goods lost during UAV attacks.
- Wildberries, Ozon, Yandex Market, Megamarket and Magnit Market have changed their terms and conditions.

articles.title: Venus at greatest eastern elongation: when to look for the "Evening Star"
articles.body:
Venus at greatest eastern elongation: when to look for the "Evening Star"
Kyiv • UNN
On August 15, Venus will reach its greatest eastern elongation, moving 46 degrees away from the Sun, and will be visible in the evening sky. There will also be a visual conjunction of Mercury and Jupiter.
On August 15, Venus will reach its greatest eastern elongation and appear in the evening sky, while Mercury and Jupiter will also be in visual conjunction, UNN reports.
Greatest eastern elongation: what it means
A planet’s elongation is an astronomical term denoting its apparent distance from the Sun in Earth’s sky. More precisely, it is the angle between the directions to the center of our star and to a particular celestial body. That is why it is measured in degrees.
Elongation can be determined for any celestial body. In practice, however, astronomers regularly monitor its value for two planets—Mercury and Venus. The reason is that they are inner planets relative to Earth. Although tens of millions of kilometers may separate them from the Sun, in our sky they never move far away from it.
As a result, these planets can be seen only before sunrise or immediately after sunset, but never in the middle of the night. In addition, much of the time they are hidden behind our star or pass between it and us, or their angular distance from it in the sky is so small that they cannot be observed properly.
When Venus will be most visible in August
On August 15, Venus will reach its greatest eastern elongation and appear in the evening sky, while Mercury and Jupiter will also be in visual conjunction.
August 14–15 will be the best time for observation (the point of greatest eastern elongation)—on these days, Venus will appear at its maximum angular distance from the Sun, 46 degrees.
Why Venus is called the "Evening Star"
Venus is called the "Evening Star" because of the characteristics of its orbit and its extraordinary brightness. The name originated in ancient times, when people did not know the astronomical nature of celestial bodies but noticed remarkable patterns in the sky.
How to observe the planet without special equipment
The planet can be observed immediately after sunset during evening twilight—ideally 30–60 minutes after sunset. Look for it in the west/western part of the sky—in the direction where the Sun sets.
Venus is so bright that it can be clearly seen without a telescope or binoculars—its light is steady and, unlike starlight, does not twinkle.

articles.title: The End of Oak Street Is the Best Dinosaur Movie Since Jurassic Park
articles.body:
It's been 33 years since the enduring cinematic masterpiece that is Jurassic Park first hit theaters in June 1993. Since that fateful summer, Steven Spielberg's sci-fi survival thriller has reigned supreme as the undisputed king of dinosaur films. Now, The End of Oak Street is proving a dino blockbuster that serves up prehistoric horror with a side of genuine pathos is still a worthy endeavor.
Based on Michael Crichton's 1990 novel, Jurassic Park not only delivered some of the most memorable creature-feature scares in movie history, it was also a sharp cautionary tale about scientific hubris and the illusion of man's control over nature that was anchored by stellar performances from its core cast. But over the course of numerous sequels and reboots, the franchise largely shifted away from resonant character drama in favor of high-octane action sequences and increasingly monstrous beasts. Outside the Jurassic universe, there haven't been many successful attempts to reinvent the dinosaur wheel, so to speak.
Cue the release of The End of Oak Street, now in theaters. Written and directed by David Robert Mitchell (It Follows, Under the Silver Lake) and produced by J.J. Abrams (Cloverfield, Super 8), Oak Street follows the Platt family—husband and wife Greg (Ewan McGregor) and Denise (Anne Hathaway), their two children Audrey (Maisy Stella) and Brian (Christian Convery), and their rambunctious dog Starbuck (played by two different pups named Brisket and Buzz)—after a mysterious cosmic event transports their 1980s suburban Michigan neighborhood back to a primitive era. What follows is a brutal fight for survival against aggressive, hungry, and carnivorous dinosaurs who quickly turn the community's previously idyllic streets into their own personal feeding ground. There's an absurd scientific explanation for these events, but the movie doesn't spend too much time on it, which is mostly for the best within the bounds of its sub-100-minute run. Instead, The End of Oak Street is a thriller about suburban unease and domestic tension, with a primeval twist.
"I’m just calling back that feeling I had as a kid, where I could be in the yard looking over to the dead-end street nearby, looking down into the woods," Mitchell told the AU Review of what inspired Oak Street's vintage vibe. "There was this old brick or rock wall, and it was just imagining what’s in the shadows, you know? What’s beyond the chain-link fence? As a kid, just thinking about the films that I had seen, the stories I’d read, and imagining those things in my own suburban world, and then as an adult trying to remember that feeling. I do think it’s a little bit burned into my brain, that feeling."
The Platts and their neighbors must contend with a relentless pack of Velociraptors, a roving Allosaurus, and a behemoth of a snake that gets its jollies from sneaking up on its prey, among other predators. But Oak Street doesn't just spotlight the perils of man-eating dinosaurs. It also delves in the simmering marital friction that's threatening to tear the Platts apart from the inside.
While Greg is struggling to hold down a consistent job and drinking to cope with the anxiety surrounding that strain, Denise is channeling her domestic frustration into writing a secret novel about a housewife who leaves her family behind for a new life in New York City. "She’s the kind of woman who grew up in a time when many women went from their father’s home to their husband’s," Hathaway told Time Out of her character's mindset. "I wanted Denise to seem like the last person in the world you’d expect to be able to take on a Titanoboa with a knife."
After being catapulted hundreds of millions of years into the past, Greg and Denise are forced to simultaneously reckon with both the dangerous realities of being dropped in the center of a primordial jungle and the hidden truths fracturing their relationship. Of course, the rampaging dinosaurs are a bit more of an immediate issue. And Mitchell doesn't waste any time making the life-or-death stakes of the Platts' predicament abundantly clear. Those going into Oak Street blind should be prepared for a few gasp-inducing surprises.
Once the carnage gets going, Mitchell never really take his foot off the gas. And while the film's ending ultimately requires some logic-bending buy-in, the journey to get there is equal parts thrilling, fun, emotional, and ferocious. Harking back to its Jurassic forbear, The End of Oak Street channels everyone's favorite '80s Amblin classics, but with a far more vicious bite.

articles.title: Land sale refusal forces Brienz relocation rethink
articles.body:
Land sale refusal forces Brienz relocation rethink
Plans to relocate residents from the landslide-threatened Swiss village of Brienz to nearby Vazerol have been halted by a reluctance of locals to sell their land.
The authorities had asked the landowners in Vazerol to sell some land to resettle the newcomers. However, not everybody prepared to do so.
There will now be a vote on August 25 to establish resettlement zones in Alvaneu Dorf and Tiefencastel.
The municipality has received 42 relocation applications from owners of primary and secondary homes in Brienz, in the southeast canton of Graubünden.
In July, the municipal assembly approved a gross loan of CHF82.5 million for the relocation. The people of Brienz were urged to move away due to the imminent risk of a rockslide.
On several occasions over a period of months, residents had to temporarily leave their homes. They have since returned but the risk of future landslides remains high.

articles.title: Drones target Erbil as attacks fuel fears of regional spillover
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Five drones target Erbil as attacks fuel fears of regional spillover
Five drones targeted the Iraqi Kurdish capital of Erbil at dawn on Friday, with US-led coalition air defences shooting down three of them, Kurdish security authorities said, in the latest in a series of attacks to hit the autonomous Kurdistan Region in recent weeks.
One of the drones fell near the Rotana Hotel in central Erbil after the interceptions, prompting panic among residents and scattering shrapnel across the populated area.
The Kurdistan Region’s Counter-Terrorism Service said there were no casualties in the attack.
The incident came a day after another drone struck a house in a residential neighbourhood of Erbil, underscoring mounting fears among civilians over the repeated attacks and the risks posed by falling debris after aerial interceptions.
Authorities have not publicly identified who launched Friday’s drones. However, a senior official in Erbil told The New Arab that the attacks appear to involve multiple actors operating from both inside Iraq and across the border in Iran.
The official said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was targeting positions held by Iranian Kurdish opposition forces in the outskirts of Erbil, while Iraqi armed factions loyal to Tehran were launching attacks on sites in the region from the Nineveh Plain.
"The danger is not only related to the fall and explosion of the drones, but also to the fragments that are scattered with each attack over long distances, especially after the drones are intercepted by air defences," the official said.
"Residents live under constant security pressure. The sounds of planes and explosions, and their interceptions, have become part of the daily scene in the city."
Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdistan Region has experienced a growing number of drone, rocket and other attacks over recent weeks, affecting both Erbil and Sulaimaniyah provinces. The escalation has coincided with the US-Israel war with Iran and has continued despite no recent direct strikes between the three countries.
On 17 July, a deadly barrage of drones and rockets killed nine members of an Iranian Kurdish armed opposition group. The group blamed Tehran for the strikes, while Iran has long accused Iranian Kurdish opposition groups of acting in the interests of Western states and Israel.
The Kurdistan Region has repeatedly been exposed to attacks due to its sensitive geopolitical position. It hosts US troops, foreign oil companies and several Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, making it a focal point in the wider confrontation between Iran, its allied Iraqi factions, Washington and Israel.
Kurdish officials have previously said that some attacks were launched from Iranian territory, while others originated from within Iraqi soil.
Majid Balak, a member of the ruling Kurdistan Democratic Party, blamed the federal government in Baghdad for failing to halt the attacks.
"Protecting the airspace from internal and external attacks, and preventing the use of Iraqi territory to carry out attacks on security and facilities inside and outside the country, is the responsibility of the Iraqi government," Balak told The New Arab.
The continued strikes have raised concern that Erbil’s civilian areas could face greater danger even when air defences prevent drones from reaching their intended targets, as wreckage and explosive fragments fall into densely inhabited parts of the city.
Iran-backed militia warns Baghdad
Meanwhile, the head of the Iran-backed Badr group warned Baghdad against using force to disarm armed factions, arguing that a coercive campaign could "ignite civil war" as the government moves towards a looming 30 September deadline to bring all militias’ weapons under state control.
Mohammad Naji, head of the organisation’s political office, said in a statement posted on X that the use of force against armed groups in the country would deepen internal divisions and serve the interests of foreign powers, including the United States and Israel.
He conditioned a disarmament of weapons to three conditions: a complete withdrawal of US forces from Iraq, the removal of “strategic threats” and the full rebuilding of Iraq’s armed forces.
Naji also criticised Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, accusing him of succumbing to pressure from Washington. Al-Zaidi had ordered officials to prepare a draft mechanism for the disarmament of Iraqi armed factions, arguing it undermines the authority of security institutions.

articles.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Latvia near Russia
articles.body:
An Italian Eurofighter shot down a drone over north-eastern Latvia in the early hours of Friday, in an incident the Latvian armed forces attribute to Russian electromagnetic warfare pushing the aircraft off course and into NATO airspace.
The drone came down near the village of Rugāji in the Balvi region, close to the Russian border. Latvia’s National Armed Forces said NATO fighter jets had successfully shot down a foreign unmanned aerial vehicle that entered the country “as a result of Russian electromagnetic warfare”.
A NATO spokesperson said two Italian Eurofighters based in Lithuania were scrambled and one of them destroyed the drone, with two Turkish F-16s based in Estonia also launched. “All aircraft were operating under NATO command,” the spokesperson said, adding that an investigation is ongoing.
Airspace alerts were issued across several eastern and southern regions of Latvia and lifted at 4.50am local time. Finland separately restricted airspace and a sea area in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution, with the Finnish Defence Forces saying no drones entered the country and the restrictions lifted shortly after 7am.
Latvia’s defence ministry confirmed this was the second time a drone had been shot down in Latvian airspace, following a first incursion in June that was also handled by NATO fighters.
Baiba Braze, the Latvian foreign minister, thanked Italy for “maintaining (the) integrity of NATO airspace”.
The origin of the drone was not immediately established, and the Latvian statement did not identify it. Earlier on Friday more than 50 Ukrainian drones attacked targets in Russia’s western regions including Leningrad and Tver, striking the port of Ust-Luga and a warehouse belonging to the e-commerce company Wildberries.
The electromagnetic warfare claim is a recurring problem along the alliance’s eastern flank, and is more likely rather than a deliberate incursion. Jamming and spoofing of satellite navigation signals has been widespread across the Baltic region since 2022, affecting civil aviation and shipping as well as military traffic, and a drone relying on GPS to hold its track can be pushed across a border by interference intended for something else.
Whether the aircraft was Russian or Ukrainian in origin therefore remains open, and neither Latvia nor NATO has said. Drones from both sides have come down in NATO territory during the war, with Romania recovering fragments on multiple occasions and Poland scrambling aircraft repeatedly during Russian strike waves against western Ukraine.
Baltic Air Policing has run continuously since 2004, when the three Baltic states joined NATO without fighter forces of their own. Allied detachments rotate through Šiauliai in Lithuania and Ämari in Estonia on four-month tours, and the mission has shifted from routine interception of Russian aircraft transiting to Kaliningrad towards the more demanding business of intercepting small, slow targets that radar systems designed for fast jets do not handle easily.

articles.title: Leicester City put up for sale for more than $270 million
articles.body:
Efe Ozkan
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Leicester City has reportedly been put up for sale for more than $270 million, with Thai owners King Power seeking to end their 16-year ownership of the English club.
The sales process is being led by Citigroup, which has prepared an eight-page investment prospectus marketing the Foxes as well as several of the club's key assets, according to BBC Sport.
The package includes Leicester's men's and women's teams, the 32,000-seat King Power Stadium, the Seagrave training complex, opened in 2020 and valued at £121 million ($164 million), and Belgian club OH Leuven, Leicester's sister club.
The prospectus reportedly describes the sale as "a rare opportunity to acquire a club with an excellent track record of winning promotions to higher divisions."
Leicester's historic achievements, including its remarkable 2015-16 Premier League title won at 5,000-1 odds and the 2021 FA Cup, feature prominently in the sales pitch. However, the brochure makes no reference to the club's current status in League One following successive relegations from the Premier League and the Championship.
Citigroup forecasts Leicester's turnover to exceed $131 million for the 2026 financial year, but the prospectus reportedly omits the club's recent financial struggles, including more than $244 million in losses accumulated during its recent promotion and relegation cycle.
The club's latest published accounts also show $140 million in outstanding bank loans, highlighting the financial challenges facing any prospective buyer.
King Power acquired Leicester City in 2010 for $47 million and oversaw the most successful period in the club's history, transforming the East Midlands side from Championship contenders into Premier League champions and FA Cup winners.

articles.title: German rivers drying up as government quarrels over solutions
articles.body:
Persistent drought and historically low water levels – particularly on the Rhine, as well as on the Danube, Elbe and other waterways – are posing a massive threat to inland waterway shipping and putting pressure on key supply chains.
Because ships can now operate only with reduced cargo due to the shallow water, transportation costs are rising sharply, leading to bottlenecks in industrial supply chains.
In terms of economic consequences, less cargo can be transported as inland waterway vessels cannot fully utilize their capacity, resulting in a significant increase in the number of trips required to transport the same volume of goods.
Furthermore, shipping companies face rising costs: Higher transportation rates place a burden on energy-intensive sectors, the chemical industry and the steel and petroleum industries.
In addition, the country’s industries have to cut back on production as raw materials such as coal, steel, gravel or petroleum products arrive late at factories or not at all.
Low water levels in the rivers mean shifting to road transport: Freight must be rerouted to trucks and trains. Several federal states have eased the Sunday driving ban for trucks to alleviate the transportation crisis.
The crisis has also sparked an infrastructure debate as the federal government and the states are discussing immediate measures, the expansion of shipping channels and long-term investments in ports and waterways.
To avert impending supply shortages and maintain production in the economy and agriculture, the Federal Ministry of Transportation and the federal states have agreed on a comprehensive package of short-term crisis measures. The goal is to stabilize supply chains through close cooperation across road, rail and alternative waterways.
The economic damage from the river crisis is immense. According to surveys by the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, which shipping companies cite, similar periods of low water levels in the past have led to a noticeable decline in gross domestic product.
In addition, prices for consumer goods such as fuel are already rising in some regions, as the transport of petroleum products increasingly has to rely on more expensive truck fleets.
Since the waterways are blocked, the shipping industry must switch to road and rail transport in the short term. According to a statement released by Federal Minister of Transportation Steffen Bilger, the coming weeks will remain challenging and will require pragmatic action in close cooperation.
“The coming weeks will be challenging. Water levels on the Rhine and Danube will remain very low for the time being. That is why we must act pragmatically now. We have already implemented a number of concrete measures – ranging from exemptions to the truck ban to additional rail capacity and more flexible transshipment options. At the same time, we are working with the states to prevent further bottlenecks,” Bilger said.
However, in a recent statement, the Association of German Transport Companies criticized short-term, and superficial solutions.
Association Vice President Joachim Berends emphasized that the ongoing low water levels clearly demonstrate how vulnerable Germany’s logistics chains are. To ensure that transportation routes are built to be resilient in the long term, the association has clearly rejected calls for increased use of long trucks.
The association Chief Executive Oliver Wolff explained that such measures in no way solve the structural problems in freight transport. The roads are already overloaded, and more heavy trucks would massively exacerbate the problem of bridges and roads that are already in need of repair.
Instead, the focus must be placed entirely on intermodal transport, in which rail can efficiently handle large volumes of bulk goods.
For its part, the center-right government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz remains divided over how to fight low water levels.
Federal Minister of Transport Steffen Bilger is calling for the expansion of the river network.
“Fundamentally, we should all recognize that waterways deserve support because they are the most environmentally friendly mode of transportation,” he told the editorial network RND.
Bilger said that confidence in inland waterway transport can only exist if low-water problems do not occur on a regular basis.
Meanwhile, Federal Environment Minister Carsten Schneider spoke out against deepening rivers.
That cannot be the answer to the current situation, Schneider said. Rather, he added, what is needed is a “restoration” of the rivers, “moving away from canals toward natural rivers with meandering branches and floodplain landscapes that retain water across a wide area.”
Environmentalists, too, view river widening with skepticism and advocate instead for living rivers.
Meanwhile, a leading German economic expert warned of fuel price hikes as a result of the low river water levels.
“Disruptions in transportation can lead to physical bottlenecks. These usually don’t occur immediately. However, if low water levels persist, fuel is likely to become scarcer in some regions. Prices will then rise as well. In addition to the war in Iran, there would be another factor adding to the pressure,” Thilo Schaefer told the weekly news magazine Der Spiegel.
The head of the Digitalization and Climate Change division at the German Economic Institute in Cologne also pointed out that disruptions in waterway cargo traffic could severely impact the country’s economic growth.
“Following the 2018 drought, researchers at the Kiel Institute for the World Economy calculated the impact of the low water levels on the overall economy. They concluded that industrial production fell by 1% and total economic output by 0.4%. These exact figures should be viewed with some caution. However, the low water levels could stifle Germany’s already fragile economic growth,” Schaefer said.
“The frequency of low-water periods is increasing, and this is clearly due to climate change. We must remain committed to combating it. At the same time, we must adapt. For a transportation corridor as crucial as the Rhine, this means we must invest money so that it can continue to fulfill its function. Even if we cannot prevent drought, we can limit its effects,” he added.

articles.title: Japan considering response to Putin's visit to disputed island: Report
articles.body:
Saadet Gokce and Islamuddin Sajid
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Japan is considering "some measure" against Russia after President Vladimir Putin's visit to the disputed Iturup Island, a senior Foreign Ministry official said Friday, according to Kyodo News.
On Thursday, Putin visited the island, which Japan calls Etorofu, marking his first trip to the Russian-controlled but Japanese-claimed island chain off Hokkaido. Russia calls the islands the Southern Kuril Islands.
"We are considering what step to take going forward," the official told reporters. An additional sanction is believed to be under consideration, according to Kyodo.
Tokyo maintains that the Northern Territories, consisting of Iturup, Kunashiri, Shikotan and the Habomai islet group, were "illegally" seized by the now-defunct Soviet Union soon after Japan's surrender in World War II on Aug. 15, 1945.
Russia argues the seizure was legitimate.
The dispute has prevented the two countries from signing a peace treaty since World War II, while tensions have deepened in recent years amid Japan's sanctions against Moscow over the Russia-Ukraine war.
The Japanese government summoned Nikolay Nozdrev, Russia's ambassador in Tokyo, to lodge a "strong protest" over Putin's visit, while Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the islands are an inherent part of Japanese territory "both historically and under international law."
China's reaction
China on Friday said the outcomes of the victory in the World Anti-Fascist War must be “earnestly respected and upheld” when asked about Russian President Vladimir Putin’s visit to Iturup Island, one of the four islands Japan calls the Northern Territories.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun urged Japan to abide by the postwar international order established under the Cairo Declaration, Potsdam Proclamation and other relevant international legal instruments.

articles.title: Politico: Zelensky can’t find a Ukrainian ambassador to the US — every candidate says no
articles.body:
Politico: Zelensky can’t find a Ukrainian ambassador to the US — every candidate says no
Zelensky is struggling to find a new ambassador to the United States after several candidates turned down the post, senior Ukrainian officials and lawmakers told Politico.
Lawmaker Ivanna Klympush-Tsintsadze, who served as deputy prime minister from 2016 to 2019, said candidates with the standing and experience for the job fear they “would not enjoy the conditions they would need to do the job properly.” She said the nominee should come from Zelensky’s inner circle of trusted advisers, but that no one there meets the requirements.
A former Ukrainian diplomat said, “Framing it as if nobody wants the job would be a kind of oversimplification. Of course, there are people who want the job, but there’s no one who really measures up to it.” He said Zelensky will have “a hard time filling the position.”
Zelensky had offered the ambassador post to Yulia Svyrydenko as early as July, shortly after she resigned as prime minister, but she categorically refused, sources told the Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda. Politico’s own sources confirmed the same. Other candidates have since been “equally reluctant,” according to the outlet, which said the appointment will be no easy task given the need to work with the “Trump’s unpredictable White House.”
Oksana Markarova had served as Ukraine’s ambassador to the United States since before Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, remaining in the post through nearly all of Joe Biden’s presidency. Volodymyr Zelensky appointed Olha Stefanishyna, who had previously served as deputy prime minister, to replace her in August 2025.
Stefanishyna was relieved of her post in early August 2026. She said she had resigned of her own accord, “prompted by personal circumstances.” Two days later, Ukraine’s anticorruption agencies notified her that she was suspected of involvement in illegal enrichment and submitting false information in her asset declaration. Her case is now before the courts.

articles.title: Burnham brings in military and bans disposable barbecues in ‘tinderbox’ Britain
articles.body:
Downing Street has issued a temporary GB-wide ban on the sale of disposable barbecues and brought in the military to help deal with wildfires as Andy Burnham urged people not to risk lives in “tinderbox” Britain this weekend.
The prime minister spoke from Stourbridge in the West Midlands, where at least 19 people have been taken to hospital during eight fires that have ripped through several homes.
He said it was necessary to bring in a temporary ban on disposable barbecues from today, asking retailers to withdraw them from sale, as he spoke of the “absolutely devastating” wildfires.
“Please think about the situation we are in,” he said. “Britain is a tinderbox right now. Setting a fire in any outdoor setting is a risk to people’s homes and other people’s lives.”
He said not all of the 37 fires across Britain had been caused by barbecues but it was “probable” that some of them had been.
Advice published online by the government said that single-use grills had “been the cause of a number of serious wildfires across the country over the summer months.
“Disposable barbecues cannot be considered a safe product in the context of the ongoing weather and environmental conditions and must not be made available for sale either in store or online at the current time.”
The prime minister also revealed he planned to commission firefighting planes, as used to douse flames in Europe and the US, to combat the spread of wildfires, as he said the country had to “face up” to the “changing climate”.
Burnham said plans were being drawn up for emergency financial support for fire services battling the spread of wildfires. He warned that the weekend ahead would be difficult in terms of fires, and that hotter and drier than normal conditions could last through September and into October. He said late autumn could then bring the prospect of floods as the ground would be drier than usual.
The prime minister has faced criticism for not having addressed the issue of the climate emergency after his first Cobra meeting on the heatwave this week. At the same time, his government is mulling whether to allow more North Sea drilling at two fields, Jackdaw and Rosebank, which green groups warn is the wrong thing to do at a time of climate crisis.
Pressed on his views, he said the priority was to build resilience and make adjustments in the face of threatened fires and flooding, as well as more broadly making the shift to clean energy.
And asked about North Sea drilling, he said he would take a “pragmatic” approach, and argued: “We won’t be able to stop using oil and gas for some time, that’s just a fact.”

articles.title: Ukraine will transfer Russian T-72 tanks to foreign museums: what is known about the vehicles and how many of these tanks the Russian Federation has lost
articles.body:
Ukraine will transfer Russian T-72 tanks to foreign museums: what is known about the vehicles and how many of these tanks the Russian Federation has lost
Kyiv • UNN
The Cabinet of Ministers has allowed destroyed enemy equipment to be transferred to foreign museums free of charge. Museums in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Denmark, and the Netherlands will each receive one T-72 tank of different modifications.
On Thursday, August 13, at the initiative of the Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Culture of Ukraine, the Cabinet of Ministers allowed destroyed enemy equipment to be transferred free of charge to foreign museums. This concerns five Russian T-72 tanks in various modifications, which will be transferred to museums in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Denmark, and the Netherlands. UNN explains what is known about this tank and how many such vehicles the russian federation has lost in the war against Ukraine.
Thus, pursuant to government order No. 773-р:
-  The Netherlands will receive a T-72B tank; 
-  Estonia will receive a 2011-model T-72B3 tank; 
-  Latvia will receive a T-72B tank; 
-  Lithuania will receive a T-72BA tank; 
-  Denmark will receive a T-72B3 tank.  
As stated by the Ministry of Defense, the enemy equipment has lost its combat capabilities, contains no explosive elements, and may be displayed to visitors abroad. The ministry also emphasized that transferring destroyed examples of captured equipment to foreign museums would contribute to the international documentation of the consequences of Russian aggression against Ukraine.
How many tanks Russia has lost in the war against Ukraine
According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, as of August 13, Russia had lost 12,264 [units] in the war against Ukraine. According to Osint analysts, Russia had lost 4,437 tanks, of which 3,343 were destroyed, 165 were damaged, and 538 were captured.
Based on Osint data, it has been established that Russia lost 1,851 tanks of various modifications.
What is known about the T-72 tank
The T-72 "Ural" is a second-generation main battle tank developed in the USSR. It was adopted by the Soviet Army in 1973. The T-72 tank family was developed by the Ural Tank Plant (the F. Dzerzhinsky "Uralvagonzavod," code name "Plant No. 183").
T-72 tank
The T-72 is in service with CIS countries and was exported to socialist-bloc countries and the Middle East. T-72 modifications were produced under license in Yugoslavia (M-84), Poland (PT-91), Czechoslovakia, and India, which in turn also exported them.
Destroyed Russian T-72 "Ural"
The designers continued improving the T-64, which had a number of shortcomings, the main ones being its high production cost and lengthy manufacturing process. Therefore, a decision was made to prepare an additional version of a prospective tank whose production would be cheaper and whose manufacturing process would be faster.
There was also a proposal to install the four-stroke V-shaped V-45 diesel engine, whose production had been well mastered by industry; at that time, the engine was also significantly simpler and cheaper to manufacture.
The new tank was supposed to be another branch of the T-64 tank family. Thus, in the early 1970s, the Ural Tank Plant, jointly with the Kharkiv Tank Plant, began work on improving the design of the T-64 tank to install the V-45 engine.
However, the new vehicle differed from its predecessor in many respects; the differences were so significant that even the main components of these tanks could not be interchanged. Thus, after the relevant modifications and tests, on August 7, 1973, the "Object 172M" tank was adopted for service, and its production began at Uralvagonzavod under the designation "T-72 Main Battle Tank" (code name "Ural").
The vehicle retained from the T-64 the modified compact onboard gearboxes and the armament system. The T-72 tracks were standardized with those of the T-55 and T-62 tanks. In 1973, the first batch of 30 vehicles was produced. Serial production of the tank began in 1974.
Over more than 30 years, more than 20 modifications of the tank were developed. Thus, modernization of the T-72 began as early as the second half of the 1970s, and the tank received the designation T-72A.
T-72A
The vehicle was equipped with a TPDK-1 laser sight-rangefinder, a TPN-3-49 gunner's night sight with an L-4 illuminator, solid side anti-cumulative screens, a 2A46 gun (instead of the 2A26M2 gun), a 902B smoke-grenade launching system, a protection system against napalm, a road-signaling system, a TVNE-4B night-vision device for the driver-mechanic, increased dynamic roller travel, and a V-46-6 engine.
Russian serviceman surrendered to the AFU along with a T-72A tank
At the beginning of the 1980s, the Soviet Army began modernizing tanks of all types by installing explosive reactive armor systems on them. In 1985, Kontakt explosive reactive armor elements were installed on the T-72A tank, which was then accepted into service under the designation T-72AV.
T-72AV tank of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
At the same time, work was underway to install a guided-missile weapons system on T-72 tanks. Thus, the Object 184 vehicle was equipped with the 9K120 Svir guided weapons system.
T-72B
The installation of the guided weapons system required replacing the gun with the 2A46M gun-launcher. A new V-84 engine and the 1A40 fire-control system were also installed. The armor of the tank's frontal section was significantly reinforced, and a new turret with a new type of filler was used. The tank was accepted into service under the designation T-72B.
A destroyed T-72B at the beginning of the war
In 1989, the T-72B underwent an extensive modernization and received the designation T-72B model 1989 (the unofficial designation T-72BM).
A captured T-72B model 1989, seized by Ukrainian troops in the Kharkiv region in 2022
The tank received built-in Kontakt-5 explosive reactive armor, similar to that installed on the T-80U tank, as well as a modified composition of the upper glacis plate.
A Russian T-72B model 1989 "got tired" in the fields of Ukraine
After the collapse of the Soviet Union, production of the tank continued in Russia at Uralvagonzavod in Nizhny Tagil, where its modernization also continued. Probably one of the tank's most extensive modifications was carried out in 2011, when it was released under the designation T-72B3.
T-72B3 of the Russian Armed Forces
The tank is equipped with the Kontakt-5 protection system, a V-84-1 engine rated at 840 hp, and the Sosna-U gunner's multichannel sight, which includes visual, thermal-imaging, and rangefinder channels, as well as a missile-guidance channel, a wind sensor, the R-168-25U-2 Akveduk radio station, and a protection system against weapons of mass destruction.
The gun's autoloader was modified for new ammunition, and the running gear was improved with track links featuring a parallel hinge. There are no GLONASS receivers for the crew to determine the tank's location.
A T-72B3 of the Russian Armed Forces captured by Ukrainian troops
However, Ukrainian engineers were not idle either and continuously improved the tank, of which, according to open-source data, Ukraine had approximately 230 units as of the end of 2017, with another 140 in storage.
Thus, in 2018, trials were conducted of the T-72AMT, a Ukrainian deep modernization of the T-72 by the Kyiv Armored Plant. The vehicle received a package of upgrades dictated by combat experience in Donbas. The modernized tank received the new Nozh explosive reactive armor, already used on the Bulat and Oplot tanks; anti shaped-charge screens; the Kombat missile, capable of penetrating up to 750 mm of armor; a night-vision device with third-generation image intensifiers and a 1K13 night sight; as well as a kit consisting of an Aselsan digital radio station and an SN-3003 Bazalt satellite navigation system, along with a new engine.
T-72AMT at an exhibition in Kyiv
One of the latest modifications was carried out during Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The tank received the designation T-72B3 model 2022. The main battle tank received reinforced protection for the front fender sections, analogous to that of the T-90M.
An echelon of T-72B3 model 2022 tanks
Kontakt-1 explosive reactive armor modules were installed on the gun mantlet. Explosive reactive armor was also added to the turret. The Sosna-U multichannel system with a thermal imager received a mechanism for opening armored shutters, replacing manual opening by unscrewing four bolts. New sensors also appeared on the tank. During 2022–2023, some tanks received the simpler 1PN96MT-02 thermal sight instead of the Sosna-U; the same also occurred with the T-80BVM.
Starting in 2023, anti shaped-charge nets were also added to the turret, along with explosive reactive armor on the rear and a standard "barbecue" anti-drone cope cage. Starting in 2024, rubber-fabric screens have also been installed on the turret roof.
For the first time, a Russian T-72B3 of the 2022 model was destroyed in March 2023 in the area of Marinka in Donetsk region.

articles.title: How Türkiye transformed its defence industry over 25 years
articles.body:
Türkiye’s defence industry has undergone a dramatic transformation over nearly 25 years, evolving from a sector reliant on licensed production and foreign technology into a broad-based industry developing indigenous platforms, critical technologies and high-value products for international markets.
The scale of that shift is reflected in the numbers. Türkiye had just 56 defence companies and about 62 projects in 2002. By 2024-26, the number of companies had climbed above 4,500, while active projects surpassed 1,400 and their combined value exceeded $100 billion.
Defence and aerospace exports rose from $248 million in 2002 to $10.05 billion in 2025.
Exports reached $5.79 billion in the first six months of 2026 and $11.2 billion over the 12 months through July.
From foreign procurement to indigenous design
A fundamental shift in procurement policy drove the transformation.
In the early 2000s, Türkiye largely relied on off-the-shelf purchases, licensed production and technology transfers.
Over time, the emphasis moved toward domestic design, locally produced subsystems and greater control over critical technologies.
Research and development spending rose from $49 million in 2002 to more than $3.5 billion, while the domestic content ratio increased from about 20 percent to above 85 percent.
The industry now employs more than 100,000 people, with an average workforce age of 34. Annual sector revenue, meanwhile, climbed from roughly $1.1 billion in 2002 to more than $20 billion in 2026.
Drones put Türkiye on the global map
Unmanned systems have become one of the clearest symbols of the industry's rise.
Baykar's Bayraktar TB2 helped establish Türkiye as a major exporter of combat drones, while the Akinci expanded capabilities in payload, range, sensors and weapons integration.
The jet-powered Kizilelma is taking that development further, combining high speed with air-to-air and air-to-ground capabilities and the ability to operate from short-runway ships.
Turkish Aerospace Industries' Anka and Aksungur platforms have also expanded domestic capabilities in long-endurance surveillance, satellite communications, electro-optical systems, weapons and engines.
Fighter jets and helicopters broaden the aerospace push
Türkiye’s defence strategy now extends beyond unmanned aviation.
The Kaan twin-engine fighter program represents one of Türkiye's most technologically ambitious aviation projects, incorporating low-observable design, advanced avionics, radar and mission systems.
The Hurjet trainer is another step towards developing domestic manned military aircraft, while experience gained through the T129 Atak helicopter program contributed to the development of the indigenous T625 Gokbey.
A growing presence at sea
Türkiye's naval industry has followed a similar trajectory.
The MILGEM national ship program established a domestic foundation for designing and building naval platforms, from corvettes to frigates, while advancing locally developed combat-management systems, sensors and weapons integration.
The planned TF-2000 air-defence destroyer is designed to expand the Turkish Navy's long-range air-defence capabilities, while the MILDEN project is taking domestic shipbuilding expertise into submarine development.
The TCG Anadolu and Bayraktar TB3 have also introduced a new sea-air operating concept, combining amphibious capabilities with a drone designed to operate from a short runway at sea.
Layered air defence and precision strike
Türkiye has simultaneously expanded its domestic air-defence architecture through systems such as Hisar and Siper.
The Steel Dome concept brings together radars, electro-optical sensors, electronic warfare, command-and-control systems and air-defence weapons into a networked architecture designed to counter threats at different ranges and altitudes.
Missile programs including Som, Atmaca, Kara Atmaca and Tayfun have added precision-strike capabilities across air, sea and land domains.
Other systems, including the Altay main battle tank and Aselsan's Koral electronic warfare platform, have helped broaden the domestic industrial base while reducing reliance on foreign suppliers.
Engines emerge as the next frontier
Indigenous propulsion has become a central part of Türkiye's drive for technological independence.
Projects including the PD170, TF6000 and KTJ cover engines for unmanned aircraft, turbofan applications and cruise missiles, addressing one of the industry's longstanding strategic challenges: developing critical power systems domestically.
The push increasingly extends beyond individual platforms, with the industry seeking control over the technologies that underpin them.
From product sales to global partnerships
Türkiye's defence export model has also evolved.
Rather than focusing solely on selling finished equipment, companies increasingly offer training, maintenance, sustainment, system integration, co-production and technology partnerships.
Turkish defence products are now exported to around 185 countries, with roughly 230 different product types in active use worldwide.
The next phase focuses on further reducing foreign dependence on critical technologies, building high-volume production capacity, and expanding Türkiye's position in the global defence market.
The transformation, in other words, is no longer simply about producing more equipment at home. It is about building an end-to-end defence ecosystem capable of designing, powering, integrating, exporting and sustaining increasingly sophisticated systems.

articles.title: Chinese pioneer space scientist Wang Xiji dies at 105
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Wang Xiji, a Chinese space scientist who made pioneering contributions to China's rocket and satellite programs, died of illness in Beijing at the age of 105 on Wednesday, the China Academy of Space Technology announced.
His career spanned several fields of the country's early space development, including sounding rockets, carrier rockets, recoverable satellites and modern small satellites.
He championed and participated in establishing the disciplines of unguided rocket technology and space recovery technology. He led the development of China's first sounding rocket, proposed the technical plan for the first carrier rocket, and supervised the development of multiple recoverable satellites, making China the third country in the world to master satellite recovery tech capabilities, the academy said.
In 1999, Wang was awarded the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" Meritorious Service Medal, a national honor that recognizes extraordinary contributions to the country's early nuclear, missile and satellite programs. ■

articles.title: Experts gather in Kenya to explore biodiversity conservation, sustainable utilization
articles.body:
Erustus Kanga, director general of the Kenya Wildlife Service, speaks during a symposium on biodiversity conservation and sustainable utilization, alongside the inaugural Kenya grape industry exchange conference, in Kiambu County, Kenya, Aug. 13, 2026.(Xinhua/Xie Jianfei)
NAIROBI, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- A symposium on biodiversity conservation and sustainable utilization, alongside the inaugural Kenya grape industry exchange conference, was held on Thursday at Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology in Kenya.
The event was jointly organized by Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology, the National Museums of Kenya, the Wuhan Botanical Garden of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), and the Institute of Botany of CAS, and hosted by the Sino-Africa Joint Research Center of CAS.
Addressing the conference, Chinese Ambassador to Kenya Guo Haiyan noted tremendous scope to deepen China-Kenya cooperation in agricultural science and technology and to expand collaboration on biodiversity conservation.
"We stand ready to work with all of you to help Kenya accelerate agricultural modernization and advance biodiversity conservation, so that the benefits of scientific and technological innovation may reach more Kenyan farmers, and Kenya's rich biodiversity may continue to bring lasting benefits to its people," Guo said.
Wang Qingfeng, director of the Sino-Africa Joint Research Center, said the conference brought together scientists and scholars from China and African countries, providing an opportunity to discuss biodiversity conservation and agricultural development across the African continent.
He also expressed the hope that China and African countries would further strengthen cooperation in areas such as capacity building and scientific research.
Erustus Kanga, director general of the Kenya Wildlife Service, said the conference "brings science into conversation with agricultural innovation", and also creates space for Kenyan and Chinese institutions, researchers, government, communities and industry to "turn knowledge into practical results."
During the event, representatives from biodiversity research institutions in China, Kenya, Egypt, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, Madagascar and Zimbabwe also signed a declaration to support the establishment of the Alliance for Biodiversity Science in Africa.
According to organizers, the alliance, jointly initiated by the Sino-Africa Joint Research Center and the National Museums of Kenya, aims to promote long-term practical cooperation in joint scientific research, local talent cultivation, and the sharing of scientific achievements and research data. ■
