articles.title: Putin Ordered Kremlin to ‘Destroy NATO and EU From Within’ – NYT
articles.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has reportedly ordered his intelligence services and military to work toward “destroying NATO and the EU from within” in 2026, with Moldova emerging as a key target in the Kremlin’s strategy, The New York Times reported.
Friday’s report, based on officials from two countries familiar with a secret December 2025 meeting, says Moscow is pursuing the strategy on at least two fronts: testing NATO’s willingness to defend its members and destabilizing Moldova.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
US intelligence has assessed that Russia could seek to test NATO’s resolve as early as this fall through a limited attack on an alliance member.
Possible scenarios range from cyberattacks and sabotage to operations involving unidentified armed groups or a limited incursion into a NATO country on the alliance’s eastern flank.
But Moldova could offer Moscow a different route to destabilizing Europe.
Why Moldova matters
Western intelligence officials told the NYT that conquering Ukraine remains Putin’s top priority, while establishing control over Moldova is reportedly second.
Moscow’s strategic goal, according to the officials, goes beyond political influence in Chisinau. Putin is still believed to want to seize southern Ukraine and create a land corridor connecting Russia to Moldova.
That would put Moldova – a small country of about 2.4 million people wedged between Ukraine and NATO and EU territory – in an extremely vulnerable position.
Poland Uncovers Russian Plot to Kill US-Ukrainian Citizen in Warsaw
Moldova also has the Russian-backed separatist region of Transnistria on its territory, where Russian troops have been stationed for decades. That gives Moscow an existing military foothold just across the border from Ukraine and within striking distance of Moldova’s capital, Chisinau.
Control over Moldova could therefore give Russia another platform for pressure on Ukraine while placing the EU and NATO’s eastern flank under additional strain.
Moscow already has pressure points
Russia does not need an open invasion to destabilize Moldova.
In March, a Russian strike on a Ukrainian hydroelectric plant triggered an oil spill that polluted the Dniester River and disrupted water supplies in Moldova, including the country’s third-largest city.
Russian drones later struck a high-voltage line in western Ukraine that supplies Moldova with a large share of its electricity, exposing how closely the country’s infrastructure is tied to the war next door.
The pressure is also political. Moldova has been moving decisively toward the EU, while Moscow has repeatedly sought to exploit political divisions, disinformation and economic vulnerabilities to weaken that shift.
“Hybrid attacks every day”
German Chief of Defense Gen. Carsten Breuer has warned that Russia is already conducting hybrid operations across NATO, particularly on the eastern flank.
Poland and the Baltic states are now increasing security around dams, power plants, gas facilities and other critical infrastructure amid fears Russia could stage a false-flag attack using Ukrainian-made drones.
A Baltic intelligence official told Reuters that such an operation could be designed less to cause physical damage than to create political chaos inside NATO – forcing Washington and European capitals to debate whether Russia was responsible and whether the alliance should respond.

articles.title: Brazil police target former Rio governor Castro in new investigation, say sources
articles.body:
Brazil police target former Rio governor Castro in new investigation, say sources
RIO DE JANEIRO, Aug 14 - Brazil's federal police on Friday carried out search warrants targeting former Rio de Janeiro Governor Claudio Castro, two sources familiar with the investigation told Reuters.
Castro's lawyer said in a statement to Reuters that authorities had not searched his residence.
In a statement that did not name suspects, Brazil's federal police said it was investigating alleged fraudulent and reckless management, money laundering, tax evasion, capital flight, market manipulation and crimes against the economic order involving fuel marketing.
The probe is examining the alleged irregular issuance of environmental licenses for the refinery, in disregard of guidance from the relevant technical bodies, as well as money laundering tied to the scheme, it added.
The former governor was targeted in another investigation into suspected tax evasion in May, when police ordered privately owned refinery Refit to halt operations.
Castro resigned from office in March. An electoral court barred him from holding office for eight years for abuse of political and economic power, illicit fundraising and other issues in the 2022 general election. REUTERS

articles.title: Europe leads on Ukraine aid, US weapons remain key: Report
articles.body:
Burak Bir
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Europe significantly increased its military support for Ukraine, but US weapons still play a key role in continued aid to Kyiv, a study revealed.
In its Ukraine Support Tracker report released Thursday, the Kiel Institute for the World Economy said Europe significantly increased its aid allocations to Ukraine in May and June 2026.
The increase was mainly driven by the newly introduced Ukraine Support Loan, through which European institutions allocated nearly €11 billion ($12.7 billion) over the two months, the institute said.
Beyond the Ukraine Support Loan, European donors also accounted for the majority of newly allocated aid.
However, the research suggested that financial and humanitarian aid remained well below last year's level, while Europe still relies heavily on US weapons for its military aid to Kyiv.
From January to June 2026, European donors procured military aid worth at least €3 billion ($3.4 billion) from US defense companies, the institute said.
That corresponded to around 30% of Europe’s military aid provided through defense industry procurement, according to the report.
"Europe continues to depend on access to US weapons systems to sustain its military support for Ukraine," said Federico Mellace, lead analyst of the Ukraine Support Tracker.
Mellace added that the US remains a key supplier of systems such as Patriot, for which Europe currently has only limited alternatives.

articles.title: A drone crashed in Romania near the border with Ukraine
articles.body:
A drone crashed in Romania near the border with Ukraine
Kyiv • UNN
In Tulcea County, 5 km from Ukraine, a drone flying at low altitude crashed. There were no casualties or damage, and Romania's Ministry of Defence is investigating the incident.
In Romania's Tulcea County, approximately five kilometers from the border with Ukraine, a drone crashed after radar surveillance systems failed to detect it due to its low flight altitude. This was reported by Romania's Ministry of National Defence, according to UNN.
Details
According to Romania's defense ministry, the drone was not detected by radar surveillance systems. Preliminary information indicates that the aerial target was flying at a very low altitude, which prevented it from being detected.
The aircraft crashed in a wooded area. According to preliminary information, no one was injured as a result of the crash, and no material damage was recorded.
Romania's Ministry of National Defence sent a special team with a helicopter to the site. The military is to examine the area and establish the circumstances surrounding the drone's crash.
The ministry noted that it would provide additional information depending on how the situation develops.

articles.title: Pakistan marks Independence Day with calls for unity, peace, prosperity
articles.body:
Islamuddin Sajid
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Pakistan on Friday marked its 79th anniversary of independence with nationwide celebrations and special prayers as its leaders renewed calls for national unity, economic development and peace.
The day began with a 31-gun salute in the federal capital, Islamabad, and 21-gun salutes at provincial headquarters, according to state-run Radio Pakistan.
Mosques held prayers for the country’s peace, prosperity and solidarity, while public buildings, streets and markets were decorated with national flags, buntings and lights.
Flag-hoisting ceremonies and cultural events were held across the country, while a change-of-guard ceremony took place at the mausoleum of Pakistan’s founder, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, in Karachi.
In his Independence Day message, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to Jinnah, national poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal, and leaders and workers of the Pakistan Movement.
Sharif said the country’s independence came through immense sacrifices.
"On 14 August 1947, we were blessed with a homeland where we could live as a free nation with dignity and honour and shape our lives in accordance with our religious and cultural values," he said.
Sharif said Pakistan has made progress despite major challenges, highlighting economic stability, rising remittances, technological development and investment in education, agriculture and industry.
He also praised the armed forces and security personnel, and said Pakistan remained committed to defending its sovereignty and national interests, including its water resources.
Sharif described Pakistan as committed to peace and regional stability and highlighted the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement with Türkiye and Saudi Arabia.
President Asif Ali Zardari, in a separate message, urged Pakistanis to view independence as a continuing responsibility and called for stronger institutions, governance reforms, economic growth and greater opportunities for young people.
Both leaders called for national unity and renewed efforts to build a peaceful, prosperous and stable Pakistan.
Pakistan, along with neighboring India, attained independence following the end of British colonial rule in the subcontinent in 1947.

articles.title: UK Charity Commission acts over Great Israeli Real Estate event
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
UK Charity Commission takes action after complaints over Great Israeli Real Estate event
The UK Charity Commission confirmed on Thursday that it formally engaged with the trustees of the Edgware United Synagogue after a barrage of complaints was received regarding the Great Israeli Real Estate event that took place in London on 14 June.
The event promoted the sale of properties in illegal Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territories, triggering protests at the time.
The Charity Commission said it exercised its statutory powers under section 15(2) of the Charities Act 2011 to issue regulatory advice and guidance concerning the charity's decision to host the event.
It added that the trustees of the Edgware United Synagogue must now take account of and act upon the guidance moving forward.
The development comes after the Commission said its statutory regulatory powers reflect its assessment that the issues raised by the complaints, such as that from the International Centre of Justice of Palestinians (ICJP), warranted formal regulatory engagement.
The complaint from the ICJP argued that the synagogue had allowed its charitable resources and premises to host a commercial event, where attendees were persuaded to buy properties in illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The group also said that the event had gone ahead despite the trustees receiving detailed legal warnings before it took place, raising concerns over trustee governance, the discharge of trustees' legal duties, due diligence, the use of charitable assets, and reputational risk.
Another key concern about the event was the obligation of trustees to act exclusively in the best interests of their charity, while maintaining public trust and confidence.
The ICJP argued that by allowing the event to proceed, the trustees failed to consider the legal warnings and obligations, despite being made aware of the issues.
A statement from the ICJP, however, said that the Commission’s response was not sufficient, noting the serious nature of the matter.
The group said that they had submitted thorough evidence which showed the event raised serious concerns under both international law and UK laws.
“Where a charity permits its premises and resources to be used in connection with conduct that raises such serious legal concerns, the Charity Commission should take robust regulatory action to uphold charity law and protect public trust and confidence in the charitable sector,” a statement from the ICJP said.
The organisation called for a more adequate response and called for the Charity Commission to show that it is ready to use all of its powers in cases where charities risk being connected to serious breaches of law.
“Failing to do so risks undermining public confidence in charity regulation and sending the wrong message to trustees about the standards expected of them under charity law,” the ICJP said.

articles.title: Pilot killed in helicopter crash in eastern Germany
articles.body:
Oliver Towfigh Nia
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
A pilot died when his helicopter crashed in a forest near the eastern German town of Sehmatal in the Ore Mountains (Erzgebirge), public broadcaster MDR reported Friday.
The helicopter was reportedly en route to carry out liming operations in the forest area. District Fire Chief Falko Auerswald confirmed that the pilot was killed in the crash.
Police said they had no immediate information about the pilot’s identity or the cause of the accident. A spokesperson said authorities were notified of the crash at around 9.55 am local time (0755GMT).
Eyewitnesses reportedly described seeing a column of smoke visible from a great distance.
The Neudorf Forest District, which has jurisdiction over the area, and police confirmed an emergency involving a helicopter.
Helicopters are used to apply lime to forest soils. Aerial liming is carried out to counter soil acidification caused by environmental factors such as acid rain and nitrogen.

articles.title: Russia builds another tanker to circumvent sanctions via northern seas
articles.body:
Russia builds another tanker to circumvent sanctions via northern seas
Konstantin Posiet, Russia's second newly built ice-class tanker for transporting liquefied natural gas, has left Bolshoy Kamen Bay in Primorsky Krai and set course for the Northern Sea Route.
Source: Reuters
Details: For Russia, this tanker represents another step in circumventing Western sanctions.
The vessel was built at the Zvezda shipyard, one of Russia's most advanced shipbuilding facilities, to serve the sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 plant, which is under US sanctions.
According to LSEG data, the Konstantin Posiet is due to arrive at its destination on 30 August. The destination of the gas carrier has not been disclosed.
The Zvezda shipyard specialises in building large Arc7 ice-class tankers, capable of breaking through ice up to two metres thick.
The shipyard was due to build 15 tankers for Russia's Arctic LNG 2 project, but sanctions have delayed the programme.
The first domestically built ice-class LNG tanker from the Zvezda shipyard, the Alexey Kosygin, entered service in December last year.
With this new vessel, the company now has three ice-class tankers in total, allowing gas to be transported via a significantly shorter route.
Background: Russia relied on a single icebreaker to continue exporting liquefied natural gas from a US-sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 project throughout the winter.

articles.title: Zelensky Struggles to Find Ukraine’s Next Envoy to Trump
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is struggling to find a senior enough candidate to represent Kyiv in Washington as relations with the Trump administration enter a critical stage, Politico reported Friday, Aug. 14.
The vacancy follows the dismissal of Ukraine’s previous envoy to the United States, Olga Stefanishyna, and has complicated Zelensky’s broader government reshuffle. According to two former senior Ukrainian officials and four lawmakers cited by Politico, several potential candidates have been reluctant to take on the demanding position.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The ambassador will face the difficult task of dealing with US President Donald Trump’s unpredictable approach to military support for Ukraine, possible peace negotiations and Washington’s decisions on air defense and other critical military assistance.
Zelensky’s first choice rejected the post
The need to appoint a new ambassador reportedly influenced Zelensky’s plans for the government reshuffle.
According to a former Ukrainian senior official and a Republican foreign policy expert, Zelensky had hoped to offer the Washington post to Yulia Svyrydenko, who was then leaving the position of prime minister.
Zelensky later confirmed that he had offered Svyrydenko the ambassadorship.
“It is no secret that I counted on and offered Yulia Svyrydenko the post of ambassador to the United States,” he said at a press conference in late July.
Putin Has an Unexpected Ally in Ukraine’s War
The president said he wanted someone with the highest possible qualifications, ideally “a person at the level of a deputy prime minister, minister, or prime minister.”
Svyrydenko declined, however, disrupting Zelensky’s plans.
Other potential candidates have reportedly also been hesitant to take the position.
Ivanna Klympush-Tsintsadze, a Ukrainian opposition lawmaker and former deputy prime minister, said candidates with enough political influence and experience may be concerned that they would not have the conditions needed to work effectively in Washington.
“Certainly that would be the case without having the ear of the president or his trust,” she said.
A former Ukrainian diplomat, speaking anonymously, said it would be an oversimplification to say that nobody wants the job.
“There are people who want the job, but there’s no one who really measures up to it,” the diplomat said. “Zelensky is having a hard time filling the position.”
A difficult moment for Kyiv
The ambassadorial vacancy comes as Ukraine faces increasingly important decisions in its relationship with Washington.
The Trump administration has repeatedly changed its position on military assistance and the future of the war. Kyiv is also trying to persuade Washington to allow Ukraine to manufacture Patriot air defense missiles under license.
Trump initially indicated that Ukraine would receive permission to produce the interceptors, but later backed away from the idea.
The issue has become particularly urgent as Ukraine prepares for another winter of Russian attacks and faces a growing shortage of air defense missiles.
Zelensky has said deliveries of air defense missiles from Ukraine’s allies have fallen by two-thirds compared with 2025.
At the same time, Washington may seek to revive stalled peace negotiations with Russia. That would make the role of Ukraine’s ambassador particularly important, as Kyiv would need a senior representative capable of communicating directly with the White House and Congress.
The envoy would also have to lobby US lawmakers on weapons, air defense, intelligence sharing and other forms of support.
Government reshuffle adds to political pressure
The difficulty of filling the Washington post is part of a broader political challenge for Zelensky following his government reshuffle.
According to a Socis Center for Social Research survey cited by Politico, more than 55% of Ukrainians believe the country is moving in the wrong direction.
The president’s decision to dismiss Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov in July sparked positionsprotests and political criticism, while several in the government remain unresolved.
Opposition lawmaker Mykola Knyazhitskiy questioned why the reshuffle was necessary in the first place.
“No one has explained to Ukrainians why exactly the government had to be changed,” he said.
He also questioned Svyrydenko’s dismissal, noting that she had received a standing ovation from lawmakers during her farewell address.
The uncertainty surrounding the government reshuffle has raised broader questions about whether Zelensky is willing to look beyond his closest circle when selecting senior officials.
Washington post could remain vacant
The ambassadorial position could remain unfilled for some time.
Opposition lawmaker Yaroslav Yurchyshyn said it was possible Zelensky would not appoint a new envoy before the US midterm elections.
“It will be hard to judge who would fit the political landscape best until those elections have been held,” he said.
For Kyiv, however, leaving the position vacant carries significant risks.
Washington remains central to Ukraine’s ability to sustain its defense against Russia, while decisions on Patriot missiles, other weapons, intelligence cooperation and a possible new peace initiative could come in the months ahead.
The next ambassador will therefore need not only diplomatic experience but also direct access to Zelensky and enough political weight to navigate an administration where US policy toward Ukraine can change rapidly.

articles.title: Thailand attack suspect released on bail after brutal assault on Israeli mother and daughter
articles.body:
Paul William Bercu Gaubert, a French national who brutally attacked a 62-year-old Israeli woman and her 23-year-old daughter last week on Koh Phangan, Thailand, has been released from custody after bail of about 12,000 shekels ($3,200) was paid, and is now roaming free. The two Israelis, who were seriously injured in the attack and hospitalized, were informed Friday of his release. The mother remains hospitalized after undergoing two surgeries, while her daughter has been released from the hospital after also undergoing two surgeries.
“I’m feeling better, but I’m still hospitalized,” M. told ynet from her hospital bed. “My daughter received a message from the hotel in Koh Phangan saying they had learned that the attacker had been released. We began checking with the police and tried to understand whether it was true. Today we learned unequivocally that he paid 12,000 shekels in bail and was released from custody, and that he is roaming free on Koh Phangan or Ko Samui.”
M. said she and her daughter are fearful and anxious about their safety after learning of Gaubert’s release. He was also violent toward police officers when he was arrested and was hospitalized after force was used against him.
“From the moment we learned about it, we started having anxiety attacks,” she said. “My daughter, who was released from the hospital, wanted to travel to Koh Phangan but was afraid. There’s a sense of injustice because a man beats two women and nearly kills them — and now he’s walking around free.”
According to the mother, “We don’t know who paid his bail. I asked the policewoman and she said she didn’t know. We decided that if he is going to be released, it’s important to warn people because he is a danger to the public — especially Israelis and Jews. I would have expected other authorities to intervene because it’s frightening and dangerous to let him roam free. It’s important to publish the identity of this scumbag and monster.”
“My daughter underwent two nose surgeries and has now been released from the hospital,” the mother said. “I underwent two ear surgeries because he bit me and caused extensive damage there. I had reconstructive ear surgery under general anesthesia and I’m still hospitalized. I had bleeding in my head, and according to what they told me, the blood was absorbed, but fluid accumulated in my head and I had to undergo a procedure to drain it through my spine. Right now we’re doing better. It took me several days to open my eyes, and I started eating and drinking.”
The attack in Thailand
The mother had flown to Thailand to visit her daughter, who was on a long trip around the country, for two weeks. On Tuesday, they visited a waterfall on Koh Phangan, where they encountered Gaubert, who asked where they were from.
“We went to the waterfall on a motorcycle, parked on the road and then there’s about 100 meters that you have to walk,” the mother recalled. “Suddenly, a man who was also on a motorcycle stopped behind us and started asking how we were. We were busy buying coconuts. He asked my daughter where we were from and she said Israel.”
At that point, Gower began provoking the Israeli women.
“He said, ‘I don’t like what Israel is doing there [in Gaza],’ and I told him we were on vacation and didn’t want to talk about that issue or about what they had done to us,” the mother said. “He said, ‘I’m against violence,’ and the conversation ended. Suddenly, he called us from above, came down toward us and then started beating me brutally. My daughter tried to protect me and was beaten as well. We both fought him. I was hit in the head and at some point I apparently lost consciousness.”
The attacker continued beating the mother, while her daughter ran toward the road to seek help.
“He chased after her, and she managed to call out to two French women who were there,” the mother recalled. “When he saw that there were other people on the road, he took his motorcycle and fled. I remember lying on the road and people telling me that the police and an ambulance would arrive soon. They bandaged my head and took me and my daughter to a hospital on Koh Phangan.”
From her hospital bed, the mother added: “I never thought that something like this would happen to me here in Thailand, where people are so friendly toward Israelis. I’m always careful and don’t say that I’m from Israel. But here in Thailand, I thought it was safe. He had a French accent, but he didn’t look French. We could never have imagined he would do something like this. It’s truly horrifying, and we never thought our trip would end this way. All we wanted was to see a waterfall, and then a man comes and attacks two women in the most brutal way possible. We tried to fight back, but he was extremely violent.”

articles.title: Swiatek beats Rybakina in Canadian Open for 1st title of season
articles.body:
Efe Ozkan
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Polish tennis player Iga Swiatek secured her first WTA title of the season on Thursday with a straight-set victory over Kazakhstan’s Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final.
The six-time Grand Slam winner was cheered on by the crowd in Toronto as she beat world No. 2 Rybakina 6-2, 6-3.
As Australian Open champion Rybakina struggled in the opening set, 25-year-old Swiatek broke her serve twice while saving two break points of her own.
In the second set, Rybakina was unable to break world No. 8 Swiatek, who clinched her 26th career title in one hour and 15 minutes.
“It means so, so much to me because the past months were not easy,” said Swiatek, who will return to the top five in the rankings following her first Canadian Open title.
Swiatek said it can be challenging to contend with external criticism while searching for her best form.
“I’m really happy that I kept focusing on growing, changing my game a little bit, improving despite all the opinions that many people have about me every day on the internet,” she said.

articles.title: Baby's birth brings Helsinki's population to 700k
articles.body:
Helsinki gained its 700,000th resident early on Friday, the city has announced.
The city is celebrating the milestone today based on the latest population data and city information service calculations.
The City will honour the new resident with a €700 grant. The baby was born at the Women's Hospital at three minutes past midnight on Friday 14 August to the Lehtola family.
The newborn weighed in at 4.084kg and measured 54.5cm, the family's first child.
Helsinki Mayor Daniel Sazonov (NCP) visited the Women's Hospital on Friday morning to congratulate the family.
"I warmly congratulate the 700,000th Helsinki resident and the entire family at this important, happy and unique moment," Sazonov said in a city announcement.
'Record-breaking' growth
A city press release noted that the capital has experienced "record-breaking population growth" over the past few years.
"Helsinki's growth into a city of 700,000 residents is a testament to our city's appeal, its opportunities and its vibrant urban life," Helsinki Mayor Daniel Sazonov (NCP) commented. "The most important thing is that every Helsinki resident can feel that they are part of our city and live a good and meaningful life in Helsinki on their own terms."
The previous population milestone, 600,000, was reached in August 2012, according to calculations by the city's Urban Research and Statistics Unit.
People moving to the capital from abroad, as well as from elsewhere in Finland, account for approximately 80 percent of the city's annual population increase, according to the city's figures.
"The number of Helsinki residents born abroad has more than tripled this century. The share of Helsinki residents who were born abroad is 19 percent, while the share of foreign nationals is 13 percent," the press release noted.
The largest incoming population group is people of working age, whose numbers are expected to continue to grow strongly in the coming years.
Based on the city's population projections, Helsinki could hit one million residents by the 2060s.
The city will mark reaching the 700,000 milestone with an ad campaign, launching next week, which "tells the stories of Helsinki residents, the city's diversity and the life stages behind the population growth", the statement said.
The multi-channel campaign will be rolled out in eight languages, reflecting the fact that Helsinki's residents speak over 150 languages.

articles.title: Concerns raised over 'bumpier' tracks week before UK train derailment: Lawmaker
articles.body:
Burak Bir
14 August 2026•Update: 14 August 2026
Concerns were raised about deteriorating track conditions just a week before a train derailed in southeastern England, injuring 20 people, a UK lawmaker said Friday.
Speaking to Times Radio, Lewes lawmaker James MacCleary said extremely dry conditions may have affected embankments and railway tracks in East Sussex, where the train derailed Thursday.
MacCleary said he had met representatives of Govia Thameslink Railway, which operates Southern services, just last week and discussed the condition of the tracks.
"We did discuss the track and the fact that it has been a bit bumpier in recent months, which is possibly a result of the incredibly hot weather we've had recently," he said.
A spokesperson for Eastbourne lawmaker Josh Babarinde said he had spoken by phone with Rail Minister Peter Hendy after the derailment, in which two people were seriously injured.
The spokesperson said Babarinde told the minister that people had contacted him after the incident to report that the track had "felt turbulent" in the days and weeks beforehand, according to regional newspaper Sussex Express.
According to the Chime Whistle Publishing account on US social media platform X, rail staff were barred from discussing the Lewes crash with colleagues.
Another X account, "ASLEF shrugged," whose user describes himself as a train driver, criticized the suspension of train services following the accident, arguing that an emergency timetable should have been introduced.
Meanwhile, National Rail warned that disruption was expected to continue Friday.
Photos purportedly showing damage to the railway track after the derailment were also widely shared on social media, with users describing the scene as a “terrifying image.”
Another social media user blamed Network Rail for a lack of necessary improvements, saying the publicly owned company was “hugely in debt.”
Others questioned the government's nationalization policy, arguing that Network Rail is already a publicly funded entity.
An investigation is underway to establish the "root cause" of the derailment, which saw three carriages leave the tracks between Lewes and Haywards Heath.
The incident left two people seriously injured, while another 18 were taken to hospital.

Police registered an FIR after a woman sub-inspector alleged that the BJP MLA's daughter tried to bypass the queue and assaulted her. (Photo: Instagram)
NEW DELHI: The daughter of Karnataka BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda was booked for allegedly abusing and assaulting a woman police sub-inspector following an argument at a temple in Mandya district in Karnataka, police said on Friday.The incident took place on August 12 at the Maramma Temple in Ukkada village during Bhima Amavasya celebrations, news agency PTI reported.According to the complaint filed by the woman police officer, she was deployed at the temple for security duty when Aishwarya, the MLA's daughter, allegedly sought permission to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue.The police officer alleged that she asked Aishwarya to wait to avoid inconvenience to other devotees. According to the complaint, Aishwarya then identified herself as the daughter of an MLA and questioned why she was being stopped.The argument allegedly escalated, with Aishwarya abusing the officer and hitting her on the head. The complainant also alleged that she was threatened and prevented from performing her official duties.Based on the complaint, the Kyathanahalli police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assaulting a public servant, causing simple hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation, a senior police officer said.
However, the case has taken another turn, with Aishwarya filing a counter-complaint against the police officer.Police said an inquiry into her allegations has been initiated, but no FIR has been registered on the basis of her complaint so far. Further action will depend on the findings of the inquiry.Speaking to reporters, Tumakuru Rural MLA B Suresh Gowda apologised for his daughter's conduct and said that anyone found guilty should face legal consequences."If she has committed a mistake, it is wrong. Whoever has done the mistake should face the consequences under the law," he said.The BJP legislator said his daughter had visited the temple with her two young children and had requested permission to enter briefly because waiting in the queue could have caused inconvenience.
He also claimed that another person had been allowed to enter ahead of her, prompting his daughter to question the decision.While acknowledging that the argument had escalated, Gowda said his daughter should have shown greater restraint, particularly because she comes from a political family."I apologise on behalf of my daughter if she has made a mistake," he said.The MLA also called for a departmental inquiry into the incident and urged authorities to take action against anyone found responsible.

articles.title: Ukraine's National Bank expects slight rise in forex demand following Aug easing
articles.body:
The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) expects the August package of foreign exchange liberalization measures to generate only moderate additional demand for foreign currency, which will be insignificant compared with the size of the foreign exchange market, the regulator said in response to a request from Interfax-Ukraine.
The National Bank explained that most of the transactions covered by the package do not involve the purchase of foreign currency. These primarily concern transactions with foreign currency accounts, including cash withdrawals and payments for goods, works and services, including housing rentals abroad.
An assessment of the impact of each individual measure shows that the liberalization will not have a decisive effect on the foreign exchange market and will not create risks to its stability.
Regarding the change effective September 1 in the procedure banks use to calculate their foreign exchange position, the NBU expects minimal additional demand for foreign currency.
"This is because the inclusion by banks of that portion of provisions formed against active operations that is currently not included in the calculation will take place very gradually, in accordance with the schedule approved by the National Bank," the regulator said.
As reported, on August 11 the National Bank introduced a new package of foreign exchange liberalization measures for individuals and legal entities and the financial sector. In particular, the regulator raised the monthly limit on individuals’ purchases of foreign currency in non-cash form from UAH 50,000 to UAH 200,000, increased limits on cash foreign currency withdrawals and payments abroad, and expanded a number of opportunities for businesses.
Starting September 1, banks will also be able to gradually include in their calculation of the foreign exchange position a portion of provisions formed against active operations that is currently not included in the calculation.

articles.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Remarks on August 14, 2026
articles.body:
China Daily: The U.S. State Department spokesperson issued a press statement on August 8 local time, saying that the United States rejects China’s attempts to set up the national nature reserve at Huangyan Dao and deny Filipino fishermen access to their “traditional fishing ground” as reflected in the 2016 Arbitral Award. What is China’s response?
Guo Jiakun: Huangyan Dao has always been China’s territory. It is within China’s sovereign rights to establish and administer the Huangyan Dao national nature reserve. The U.S. is in no position to point fingers, and the “South China Sea arbitral award,” which is illegal, null and void, provides no solid ground for the U.S. to speak for the Philippines. China urges the U.S. to stop playing up tensions and instigating confrontation in the South China Sea, stop citing the illegal and invalid “award,” and stop using maritime issues as a pretext to smear China.
CCTV: The third APEC Senior Officials’ Meeting (SOM) will be held in Dalian from August 17 to 28. With the meeting approaching, could you brief us on the preparations for the meeting? What does China hope to achieve through the meeting?
Guo Jiakun: As the host of APEC in 2026, China will hold the third APEC Senior Officials’ Meeting and related meetings in Dalian, Liaoning Province, from August 17 to 28. This meeting will be the largest as to the number of participants and events. It will strive to achieve more outcomes across various fields and mechanisms under the APEC framework, laying the groundwork for the leaders’ meeting in November.
There will be close to 130 meetings and events, including the third Senior Officials’ Plenary Meeting as well as SOM’s committee meetings, working group meetings, workshops and other related meetings, covering various fields such as trade, transportation, food, customs, technology, energy, health, disaster reduction and anti-corruption. It is expected to have the participation of more than 2,300 representatives from member economies of APEC, the APEC Secretariat, the APEC Business Advisory Council and the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council.
The host city Dalian serves as a window to learn about China’s opening up in Northeast China. It boasts a robust industrial foundation, sound business environment, geographical advantages, beautiful scenery and liveable environment. We welcome friends from the media to actively report on the third Senior Officials’ Meeting and related meetings, and continue following and supporting the APEC “China Year.”
Yomiuri Shimbun: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday visited Etorofu Island (known as Iturup in Russia), one of four islands known as the Northern Territories in Japan (the southern Kuril Islands in Russia). Japan claims the Northern Territories as its own. What’s China’s comment on the visit?
Guo Jiakun: China maintains that the outcomes of the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War should be earnestly respected and upheld. China urges the Japanese side to abide by the postwar international order enshrined in the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation and other international legal instruments.
Bloomberg: The Philippines’ Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has accused China of using the action against Filipinos to pressure the Philippines over its law enforcement operations against Chinese nationals. Teodoro said the actions against 100 Filipinos are “simple extortion and blackmail.” Does Foreign Ministry have a comment on this?
Guo Jiakun: Foreign nationals in China should abide by Chinese laws and regulations. China’s immigration authorities perform their duty in accordance with the law and protect the lawful rights and interests of the personnel concerned. The actions do not target any specific country.
It’s learned that it was exactly this defense secretary who personally led the armed forces to seize and detain Chinese nationals lawfully working in the Philippines. This person’s consistent attacks and smears against China harm not only the bilateral relations. It is the interests of the Philippines and all its people that will bear the brunt.

articles.title: Arms manufacturers call on MoD to ensure continuity of defense procurement
articles.body:
Arms manufacturers call on MoD to ensure continuity of defense procurement
The “Ukrainian Council of Arms Manufacturers,” an industry association of Ukrainian manufacturers, addressed the Ministry of Defense with a corresponding appeal, the text of which is available to Ukrinform.
The arms manufacturers note that as of mid-August, one of the key problems for the Ukrainian defense industry remains the insufficient level of contracting. According to market participants’ estimates, up to 25% of existing production capacity is currently under contract. Manufacturers of various types of weapons and military equipment are left without a sufficient volume of orders.
For the industry, a prolonged period without sufficient domestic orders poses the risk of losing engineers and production teams, scaling back production lines, reducing working capital, and limiting opportunities to invest in improving and scaling up Ukrainian developments.
“In recent years, the Ukrainian defense industry has significantly expanded its capabilities in response to government requests and the needs of the military. It is important to prevent the loss of these capabilities due to interruptions in contracting,” the association emphasizes.
At the same time, disruptions in contracting are not just a problem for companies. Due to the long production cycle for weapons, delays in signing contracts in August pose a risk to supply volumes in the fall and winter.
Funding remains another challenge. Assistance from international partners is critically important for Ukraine; however, certain financial instruments have their own conditions and limitations and cannot fully replace domestic resources for procuring the full range of equipment required by the Defense Forces.
In this regard, the Ukrainian Arms Manufacturers Council calls on the Ministry of Defense to:
- ensure the continuity of contracting with Ukrainian manufacturers, regardless of personnel, structural, or procedural changes in the defense procurement system;
- prevent any gaps between current and future orders, taking into account the length of the production cycle and the need for advance procurement of components;
- ensure sufficient and predictable financial resources for the procurement of weapons and military equipment needed by the Defense Forces, particularly those items that cannot be fully funded through available partnership programs.
The industry association also calls for providing manufacturers with a clear order outlook that will allow them to plan production, retain their teams, procure components, and continue developing Ukrainian technologies.
It is also proposed to maintain an ongoing dialogue with the industry regarding the current level of contracting, production capabilities, and risks to future deliveries.
“What matters to the market is the result: the military must receive the necessary weapons and military equipment without interruption and on time, and Ukrainian manufacturers must receive a sufficient volume of orders to meet these needs today and maintain their production capacity for tomorrow,” the association emphasized.
As reported by Ukrinform, the Defense Procurement Agency has denied reports of a “halt in contracting.”
Photo: Defense Procurement Agency

articles.title: ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan PM Takaichi condemns Putin’s visit to disputed Kuril Islands
articles.body:
Japan Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has criticized Russian President Vladimir Putin's first-ever visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, saying they were "inherently Japanese territory."
In a post on X, Takaichi said Thursday that Tokyo had "repeatedly requested the Russian side to ensure that the president does not visit the Northern Territories." The Northern Territories refers to the Kuril Islands.
She added that Putin's visit was "absolutely unacceptable."
The Kuril Islands sit between the southern tip of Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula and the northeastern corner of Japan's Hokkaido. The sparsely populated and volcanic archipelago separates the Sea of Okhotsk from the Pacific Ocean. The four southernmost islands of the chain were annexed by the Soviet Union when it launched an invasion of Japanese territory toward the end of World War II.
During his trip, Putin visited the island of Iturup, where Russia operates a strategically important military base. Russia's president toured a fish processing complex, a hospital and a school, before holding a meeting with Valery Limarenko, the regional governor of Sakhalin.
The visit was also criticized by Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, who posted on Facebook that "Japan strongly protests this visit."
Japan renounced "all right, title and claim to the Kuril Islands" in the 1951 Treaty of San Francisco but did not recognize Soviet sovereignty over the territory.
The dispute over the islands has prevented Tokyo and Moscow from signing a peace treaty since the end of the war, although a 1956 joint declaration ended the state of war between the two nations.
Japan's defense white paper
Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, said that Putin's visit was likely part of the Kremlin's response to Japan's latest defense white paper and aims to undermine Takaichi's efforts to improve Japan's defense capabilities.
Japan published its defense white paper earlier in the month, prompting outcry from Putin, as well as Russia's ally, North Korea. Russia's president criticized the white paper for identifying Moscow as one of Tokyo's critical threats.
"Russia is continuing active military activities in the Northern Territories, which are inherent territories of Japan, under illegal occupation," the white paper said.

articles.title: Can a massive Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
articles.body:
Can a giant Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
August 14, 2026
With its grain fields, meadows and lake, the countryside around the tiny village of Konotopie in central Poland is idyllic. Now there is a monumental statue of the Virgin Mary towering above all this.
Home to just 120 residents and situated about 160 kilometers (99 miles) northwest of the capital, Warsaw, the previously little-known village of Konotopie has been in the headlines for weeks now as a result of the massive statue.
The snow-white structure, which is visible for miles around, is more than 55 meters (180 feet) tall. The statue itself is 40.6 meters high and stands on a 15-meter-high pedestal shaped like a crown that is intended to serve as a viewing platform.
The figure dwarfs Rio de Janeiro's famous statue of Christ the Redeemer, which reaches a total height of 38 meters including its base.
'Pile of concrete' or 'fantastic achievement?'
The statue will be officially inaugurated on Saturday, August 15, the feast of the Assumption of Mary, a major holy day in the Catholic calendar.
Although final construction work is still underway and the site remains fenced off and guarded, thousands of people — both pilgrims and sightseers — have been flocking to see it for months.
Opinion about the project is divided.
"It's a nightmare," one critic of the statue told the weekly magazine Newsweek, "a complete waste. Instead of investing that money in useful projects, they financed a giant pile of concrete."
"This Mary is absolutely beautiful. My utmost respect. A fantastic achievement," said one devout woman visiting the site, according to the right-wing conservative weekly Sieci.
Madonna statue financed by Poland's Warren Buffett
The benefactor behind the statue, 75-year-old Roman Karkosik, hails from a nearby village and is one of Poland's wealthiest individuals.
Nearly 40 years ago, when the shortage economy of socialism gave way to free-market capitalism after the collapse of communism in eastern Europe, Karkosik was a young graduate from technical high school.
He started out as a bartender, but moved on to buying and selling scrap metal, producing soft drinks and later became the first entrepreneur in Poland to manufacture plastic bottles.
Karkosik made a name for himself on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. Some journalists have compared his role in Poland to Warren Buffett's influence on Wall Street.
His fortune is estimated at roughly €442 million ($511 million), and he ranks 44th on Wprost magazine's list of Poland's richest people. He lives in an 18th-century manor in the town of Kikol, just two kilometers from Konotopie.
A 'gesture of gratitude'
Karkosik and his wife, Grazyna, avoid both public appearances and contact with the media.
The cost of the statue remains a closely guarded secret. Media reports speculate that the project may have cost as much as €23 million.
The Karkosiks have described the Marian statue as a "gesture of gratitude."
According to media reports, the devout businessman wanted to thank the Virgin Mary for his recovery from a serious illness. His two brothers, who were also successful businessmen, both died prematurely after illnesses.
This is not the first time Karkosik has provided money for a religious structure. Back in 2011, he funded the construction of a church at a nearby pilgrimage site.
Artist feared seeing the finished statue
"I was afraid to come to Konotopie to see what had become of my design in reality," sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski told Polish media. Worried that the hands and face of the Virgin Mary might appear distorted, Matejkowski only visited the site in July.
"I opened my eyes and was stunned. The Mother of God is opening her arms to embrace us," he said with satisfaction. "That was exactly my intention: for the figure to have a human character, to come toward us."
Matejkowski says the statue has the facial expression of his 11-year-old daughter and the delicate facial features of his wife.
Polish region hopes for economic boost
Konotopie is situated in one of Poland's economically weak regions. There are no major industrial employers here, and jobs are scarce.
Local leaders hope the Marian statue will stimulate economic growth.
"The monument is not only a spiritual landmark but also a strategic asset for the region. We expect it to attract more investors and tourists, which will benefit the local economy," Krzysztof Kowalewski of the authorities in the nearby town of Kikol told Polish media.
Mayor Renata Golebiewska has said that revenues at local restaurants and bars have already broken local records.
Not the first statue of its kind in Poland
Poland is well known for its monumental Christian structures.
Following Poland's transition to democracy in 1989, a massive basilica was built in the village of Lichen in central Poland, overshadowing even the cathedrals of Paris and Cologne in scale.
The basilica is 138 meters (453 feet) long, 77 meters wide, and features a dome with a diameter of 35 meters. It can accommodate 20,000 worshippers.
Since 2010, Poland has also been home to the world's tallest statue of Jesus. Located in Swiebodzin near the German border, the 36-meter-high statue stands on a 17-meter-high mound.
Rising secularization
Whether all these gigantic monuments can stop the ongoing secularization of Polish society, however, remains highly questionable.
Although Poland is still one of the most Catholic countries in Europe, public trust in the Church continues to decline.
For centuries, the Catholic faith was a key part of Polish identity.
In the 19th century, when the territory that now makes up Poland was not an independent state and was divided up among foreign powers, Catholicism played a major role in the resistance to Protestant Prussia and Orthodox Russia.
After World War II, despite ideological differences, the anti-communist opposition and the Catholic Church in Poland worked together against the communist dictatorship.
During this period, churches became refuges for persecuted dissidents, and several priests were murdered by the secret police.
Pope John Paul II, himself Polish, also played a significant role in the struggle against the regime.
Catholicism in modern-day Poland
Since Poland's transition to democracy in 1989, however, the Catholic Church has experienced a crisis similar to that seen across Europe.
According to a September 2025 survey conducted by the Polish polling institute IBRIS, only 35% of Poles still trust the Church, down from 58% in 2016. Distrust rose from 24% to 47% over the same period.
In 2026, the annual number of priests ordained in Poland fell below 200 for the first time since 2000. Church attendance has also been steadily declining, especially among young people.
Even a gigantic Madonna is unlikely to reverse that trend.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: How to grow long hair: hairstylist names the main care rules
articles.body:
How to grow long hair: hairstylist names the main care rules
Kyiv • UNN
Hair grows about 1 cm per month, but breakage can hinder length retention. The expert recommends proper care, nutrition, and timely trimming of the ends.
Growing long hair is not always hindered by slow growth; instead, the length often fails to increase for other reasons. Hairdresser and colorist Oleksandra Sorokina told UNN journalist in more detail about which habits and care rules help preserve hair length.
According to the expert, hair grows by approximately one centimeter per month on average. However, it is important to work not only on growth but also on preserving the length that has already been grown.
The most common problem is not slow growth itself but hair breakage. On average, hair grows 1 cm per month, but damaged ends can break off, making it visually seem as though the length is not increasing
In particular, daily habits and at-home care affect the condition of the hair. In addition, Oleksandra Sorokina emphasizes that nutrition plays a separate role, since the body needs nutrients to maintain healthy hair.
First of all, it is properly selected at-home care. This means avoiding high temperatures, combing carefully, and avoiding constantly tight hairstyles. A complete diet is essential. Hair needs vitamin D, protein, iron, zinc, and other elements
Regarding regular haircuts, the hairdresser emphasizes that a haircut itself will not make hair grow faster. At the same time, timely removal of split ends helps preserve the length itself and can make the hair look thicker.
A haircut itself does not speed up hair growth because the hair shaft grows from the root. And timely trimming of split ends can visually increase density and preserve the length that has already been grown
The specialist also advises consulting an appropriate professional in order to have a basic set of hair products individually selected for daily care, which will make your particular hair shiny and healthy.
The essential at-home care products that everyone should have are shampoo, conditioner, a mask, and heat protection. At-home care should also be properly selected specifically for your scalp and hair type, and it is important to use it regularly
One of the common mistakes when trying to grow long hair, Oleksandra Sorokina says, is trying to focus solely on accelerating hair growth, while people may not pay enough attention to the condition of the length and ends.
The same common mistake is trying to accelerate hair growth specifically while ignoring the length and failing to care for it. To see hair growth, first of all, we need to properly select at-home care, preferably with a specialist. Balance your diet, address all vitamin deficiencies, and regularly assess the condition of your hair and trim the ends in a timely manner
In addition, the expert warns that one should not expect a significant increase in length over several months. According to Oleksandra Sorokina, during this time hair may grow by only a few centimeters.
It is also necessary to have realistic expectations, because over several months hair may grow by two, or at most 4 cm - under favorable circumstances. It is also better to focus specifically on preserving the hair ends and their quality
