articles.title: Meth trafficking across Middle East becoming more advanced, UNODC warns
articles.body:
Meth trafficking across Middle East becoming more advanced, UNODC warns
Authorities in Iran intercepted 3,663 kilogrammes of methamphetamines headed for Europe and the Persian Gulf in the first quarter of 2026, according to the UN’s drugs and crime fighting agency (UNODC).
While international attention has primarily focused on the vast region’s declining opium production, advanced criminal drug trafficking networks have successfully shifted toward manufacturing and exporting synthetic drugs such as methamphetamine, commonly known as meth.
The evidence
Iranian seizures of meth increased from 30,393 kilos in 2022 to 40,453 kilos in 2025.
Seizing the often-fatal drugs wasn’t easy. Authorities conducted five intelligence-led operations targeting massive meth shipments from Afghanistan, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime reported from Tehran on Thursday.
The shipments were headed by land across the Afghanistan-West Asia corridor, where the illicit drugs typically travel through Türkiye en route to Europe.
“The clear signal from Tehran is that these substantial shipments are being intercepted before they can reach international markets,” UNODC’s Iran office wrote. “Yet, sustained success will require enhanced international cooperation and support.”
Dangers of meth
Meth is an extremely dangerous, highly addictive stimulant typically manufactured in covert laboratories. Overdosing on it can lead to seizures and death, while long-term use can lead to malnutrition and psychological dependence on the drug, UNODC says.
In the US, for example, about 96,000 overdose deaths between January 2021 and June 2024 involved meth, according to data from the country’s Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Consequently, UNODC said that disrupting shipments of meth represents lives saved across Europe and the Middle East and cuts off the illicit financial flows that fund organised crime.
Meanwhile, nearby countries such as Syria continue to seize thousands of tablets of Captagon, an illicit synthetic drug that is taken as a pill and is most prevalent in the Middle East.
The drug was a key source of currency for the toppled Assad regime but large-scale production has been disrupted under the new Government in Damascus.
UN aiding interceptions
Criminal networks are quickly adapting, using sophisticated concealment methods to move multi-tonne meth shipments, UNODC said.
But the UN’s crime fighting agency has moved quickly, too.
UNODC has helped Iran procure advanced detection scanners to stop meth at the border. It has also worked to strengthen the country’s forensic capabilities in identifying new, potentially dangerous synthetic compounds.
Sustained donor investment is critical to prevent the corridor from becoming a major drug smuggling route, but the effort also requires “a collective and sustainable approach by the international community,” according to the drugs and crime agency, which is headquartered in Vienna.
“By supporting UNODC’s work in Iran, donor nations are investing in regional stability and international security, while also protecting their own borders from the flow of illicit substances,” the agency said.

articles.title: An attack on healthcare every six hours, and no one held to account
articles.body:
An attack on healthcare every six hours, and no one held to account
Across the world, healthcare has suffered more than 10,000 attacks in the past eight years, including during the brutal conflict in Ukraine and efforts to contain the current Ebola outbreak spreading rapidly in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
That information comes from the World Health Organization (WHO) which on Friday reiterated that the critical sector must not be targeted.
The UN agency maintains a surveillance system for attacks on healthcare, which includes hospitals and other facilities, personnel and patients, ambulances and other transport, as well as warehouses and supplies.
Since 2018, more than 10,400 attacks have been reported across 29 countries and territories, resulting in approximately 5,700 deaths and over 8,000 injuries. To date, no one has been held accountable.
Death, destruction and psychological violence
Between January and August of this year alone, WHO recorded more than 900 attacks resulting in at least 900 deaths and more than 1,400 injuries – a rate of more than four attacks a day.
Most incidents occurred in Ukraine, Lebanon and the occupied Palestinian territory, but other locations include Myanmar, Iran, Sudan, the DRC, South Sudan, Russia, Syria and Nigeria.
“What we are witnessing are multiple forms of violence,” said Altaf Musani, WHO Director for Humanitarian and Disaster Management, briefing journalists in Geneva.
Heavy weapons were the most frequently reported means of attack in 2026, he said, followed by destruction of healthcare “and then, of course, the psychosocial violence”.
Lingering impacts
Additionally, 44 reported incidents involving the abduction, arrest or detainment of healthcare workers and patients were recorded during this period. Detention of healthcare workers accounted for most cases, with 94 people affected.
Mr. Musani stressed that while these numbers matter, they do not tell the whole story.
“When a hospital is attacked, the impact is not only on the people inside the hospital that day,” he explained.
“It is the patient who cannot receive healthcare tomorrow. It is the ambulance that cannot make the next referral. It is the healthcare worker who cannot return to work, or medicine supply that can no longer reach facilities.”
Hospitals damaged, care reduced
The fact that attacks have wide-reaching and long-ranging consequences is supported by hard evidence.
Mr. Musani cited a study of 69 attacks in northwest Syria which found that outpatient consultations fell by 51 per cent the following day, with the reduction continuing for up to 37 days.
In Sudan, 37 percent of facilities were reported non-functional in 2026, while only three per cent of assessed facilities had inpatient care, he said.
Meanwhile, all 36 hospitals in Gaza have been damaged, with only half remaining partially functional, and primary healthcare similarly impacted.
Since the start of the conflict in Ukraine, WHO has verified more than 3,000 attacks affecting health facilities, ambulances, warehouses and supply chains.
Furthermore, 12 attacks on healthcare have been verified since the DRC declared the current Ebola outbreak in May, disrupting the response.
More than statistics
“These are not simply statistics,” said Mr. Musani. “Behind every percentage is a patient. Behind every damaged facility is a service lost. Behind every interrupted service is someone who will be left without healthcare.”
Moreover, attacks can also sow fear, preventing people from seeking care and health professionals from coming to work, while diluting community trust.
He called for making the human consequences visible, using evidence to protect healthcare and the people who depend on it, and holding parties to conflict accountable.
Following the briefing, a journalist asked if anyone had ever been brought to account for attacks. Mr. Musani said that of the more than 10,000 verified incidents mentioned, “not a single one has entered the accountability system.”
He said that WHO has neither the mandate nor the expertise to hold parties to a conflict to account, but its Director-General has repeatedly called for warring parties to be held accountable.

articles.title: ‘Warned but not protected’: Four in ten adults in England ignore heat alerts
articles.body:
‘Warned but not protected’: Four in ten adults in England ignore heat alerts
As amber heat-health alerts spread across England this summer, a new study has found that the warnings are being received – but not changing behaviour.
Research published by the United Nations University’s Institute for Water, Environment and Health found that seven in ten adults in England had seen a formal heat alert, yet 41 percent of them took no action to protect themselves.
The most common reason was not confusion, but disbelief: many simply did not see themselves as being at risk.
Only 18 percent of people in England report a high perception of heat risk, the study found, and roughly 30 percent say they know little or nothing about how to protect themselves.
Older, not wiser
Social media, the system’s main means of getting the word out, was the least trusted source of heat information, particularly among older adults – the group most vulnerable to extreme heat.
The national survey published by UNU drew on the views of 1,097 adults along with 29 heat risk communicators.
England’s warning system has been severely tested this summer – a season that is normally fast drawing to a close once it is mid-August.
England's warning system was tested severely this summer. On 26 June, temperatures at Lingwood, Strumpshaw Hill, reached a provisional 37.7°C, breaking a June record that had stood since 1976, while the country was placed under only its second-ever Red Heat Health Alert.
That was surpassed on 13 August, when Kew Gardens in southwest London recorded a provisional 38.1°C – the year's hottest day so far, and the fifth-hottest on record, though still short of the UK's August record of 38.5°C set in 2003. Further amber alerts followed through the month.
Never too hot?
For Dr. Mehri Khosravi, the study’s lead author, the findings point to a deeper cultural problem. “Heat still gets treated as good weather,” she said, “or as something that only happens to the very old and the very ill.”
The research also found that weather information from authorities in England is built mainly to coordinate institutions rather than to prompt households to act: informing the public, rather than motivating protective behaviour, was the dominant goal for three quarters of those interviewed.
Professor Kaveh Madani, Director of the UNU institute and a co-author of the report, said the country had only gone halfway. “England has built one half of a heat plan, and built it well,” he said. “The other half is where people actually live.”
The report calls for heat resilience to be built into housing and planning policy, with stronger enforcement of building regulations, and for greater use of trusted local intermediaries such as libraries, faith groups and social care providers to reach the people digital alerts miss.

articles.title: ‘Ebola is winning’: Epidemic now killing one person every 30 minutes
articles.body:
‘Ebola is winning’: Epidemic now killing one person every 30 minutes
The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) – the fastest-growing on record and on track to become the deadliest – is killing one person every 30 minutes.
“Ebola is winning in the Democratic Republic of the Congo,” UN humanitarian affairs chief Tom Fletcher said. “We cannot let the virus outrun our response.”
Alongside the startling current fatality rate, Mr. Fletcher announced on Friday that he has allocated an additional $30.5 million from the UN’s Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) – building on the $24 million previously allocated to the DRC and its neighbors to tackle the outbreak.
The UN’s humanitarian office (OCHA) recently deployed a further 20 staff to the epicentre of the outbreak, but Mr. Fletcher said more may be needed to slow the spread.
Declared on 15 May by national authorities in the DRC, the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak has now killed 2,184 people – nearly 47 per cent of those who have been infected.
Six of the DRC’s 26 provinces have recorded Ebola cases, and Uganda has reported 20 cases.
“This is a wake-up call,” Mr. Fletcher said.” We need speed, scale and solidarity before this virus gets even further ahead of us.”
WFP expands food assistance
Starting tomorrow, the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) will bring its hot meal programme to additional Ebola treatment centres in Ituri and other provinces, UN spokesperson Daniela Gross said on Friday.
Civilians in the North Kivu and South Kivu provinces are simultaneously dealing with Ebola and the ongoing conflict between the Congolese military and Rwanda-backed M23 militia.
Ituri province remains the heart of the outbreak; of the more than 4,660 cases total, Ituri has recorded over 3,400.
Across eastern DRC, 2.6 million people are seriously malnourished, with more than half located in Ituri.
Since the end of May, WFP has provided more than 260,000 hot meals at treatment and isolation centres in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces.
Following Friday’s meeting of the UN’s Inter-Agency Standing Committee, Mr. Fletcher said the world’s largest humanitarian organisations had agreed to scale up the global Ebola response.
More support needed
Still, Ms. Gross said that civilians’ needs in the DRC far outpace the Ebola response, and that more support is needed.
In order to protect lives across the region, Mr. Fletcher said the UN and its partners responding to Ebola must double the number of teams ensuring safe and dignified burials, triple the treatment capacity, improve contact tracing, and deploy more experienced managers.
They also need to keep providing water, hygiene and healthcare assistance to those affected by the both outbreak and the years-long conflict between multiple armed groups and national troops which is complicating the fight against Ebola.
Food insecurity assistance is only 25 per cent funded, highlighting the need for additional funding for lifesaving food aid.
“The world needs to wake up and show up,” Mr. Fletcher said.

articles.title: 900 obstacles and counting: West Bank families trapped as aid access shrinks
articles.body:
900 obstacles and counting: West Bank families trapped as aid access shrinks
Humanitarians continue to provide life-saving assistance to people across the Occupied Palestinian Territory despite facing obstacles such as checkpoints, instability and access restrictions, the United Nations said on Friday.
In the West Bank, aid partners warn that their work “is being delayed and limited by a network of over 900 physical obstacles – including checkpoints, gates, roadblocks and other restrictions,” UN Associate Spokesperson Daniela Gross told journalists in New York.
On Friday, humanitarian and municipal workers were struggling to secure access to three Palestinian families in Qusra village near Nablus who have been trapped since Tuesday following the establishment of a settlement next to their homes and the tightening of access restrictions in the area.
Serve and protect
The UN human rights office, OHCHR, previously warned that “time is running out” before the families are forcibly displaced.
Ms. Gross said UN partners and municipal workers had been trying to deliver food, water, milk formula, medicines and hygiene items to them, without success.
“Our colleagues warn that efforts to protect Palestinians have been ineffective, with settlers reportedly reinstalling a tent that Israeli forces had dismantled yesterday,” she said.
Dire situation in the north
She added that the humanitarian situation in the northern West Bank “remains particularly severe”.
Since January, UN partners have provided psychosocial support, case management, and services for children with disabilities, and other vital assistance.
Nearly 30,000 children and 15,000 adults have been served during this period.
Support in Gaza
Meanwhile, humanitarians in the Gaza Strip continue to provide vital aid to the population despite persistent insecurity and restrictions.
Last week, the UN and partners mobilized rapid support for people who had lost their shelters or were displaced again due to attacks, domestic fires and other incidents.
More than a dozen reported incidents linked to attacks affected nearly 290 households, while two households were affected by domestic fires — a recurring danger in overcrowded shelters where families lack proper energy sources to cook their meals.
Another five households were affected by the placement of new yellow cement blocks, which often signal expanded areas where access is restricted and can trigger further displacement.
Most of the appeals for help last week came from northern Gaza and Deir al Balah, with teams tailoring response to meet families’ specific needs.
Summer school
In other developments, as of last week more than 300,000 children in Gaza continued to participate in summer learning programmes supported by UN partners.
These organizations have also installed shade structures in 10 temporary learning spaces to address the extreme heat in the Strip.

articles.title: Alex Hua Tian completes dressage at Aachen worlds, cross-country test awaits
articles.body:
AACHEN, Germany, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese rider Alex Hua Tian and Chicko completed the dressage phase of the FEI Eventing World Championship at the FEI World Championships Aachen 2026 on Friday, picking up 32.5 penalties ahead of Saturday's cross-country test.
Hua Tian and the 16-year-old Chicko received an average score of 67.50 percent. They were provisionally 23rd on the live leaderboard at 12:28 p.m. local time, with the second day of dressage still underway.
Germany's Julia Krajewski and Uelzener's Nickel led on 22.0 penalties at that point, followed by Britain's Laura Collett and London 52 on 22.8. Overnight leader Tom McEwen and JL Dublin sat on 26.6.
Saturday's cross-country is expected to bring major changes to the standings. Designed by Italy's Giuseppe Della Chiesa, the 5,600-meter course has an optimum time of nine minutes and 50 seconds and features 42 efforts on the direct route. With Aachen's relatively flat terrain, much of the difficulty comes from technical combinations, turns and alternative routes that force riders to balance speed and risk.
Cross-country has been one of Hua Tian and Chicko's strongest phases. The pair finished fourth at the five-star event in Pau in 2024 and sixth there in 2025. They also completed the cross-country at Badminton earlier this year before returning to winning form with a CCI4*-S victory at Aston-le-Walls in July.
The cross-country competition will take place on Saturday, before the championship concludes with show jumping on Sunday. ■

articles.title: Pakistani FM stresses implementation of Islamabad MoU in talks with U.S. official
articles.body:
ISLAMABAD, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar stressed the importance of implementing the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed on June 18 during a meeting with U.S. Charge d'Affaires Natalie A. Baker here on Friday, the foreign office said.
He said that implementation of the Islamabad MoU "in letter and spirit" was the only way forward, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to regional peace and security while safeguarding its national interests, a statement issued by Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.
The meeting focused on Pakistan-U.S. bilateral cooperation and recent regional developments.
Dar appreciated the positive trajectory in Pakistan-U.S. relations and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy for achieving lasting peace.
The U.S. charge d'affaires appreciated Pakistan's constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability and conveyed felicitations to Dar on Pakistan's Independence Day, celebrated on Aug. 14. ■

articles.title: China posts current account surplus in Q2
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's current account surplus reached 1.33 trillion yuan in the second quarter of 2026, preliminary data from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange showed Friday.
In U.S. dollar terms, the current account surplus stood at 195.1 billion U.S. dollars in the second quarter.
The surplus in goods trade stood at 1.91 trillion yuan, while services trade and primary income posted deficits of 358.4 billion yuan and 257.2 billion yuan, respectively.
The secondary income account, which records transfers that involve no direct exchange of goods or services, registered a surplus of 42.8 billion yuan.
The capital and financial account recorded a deficit of 1.33 trillion yuan, with direct investment into China maintaining a net inflow during the period.
In the first half of the year, China recorded a current account surplus of 2.62 trillion yuan. The surplus in trade in goods stood at 3.63 trillion yuan in the first half, while trade in services posted a deficit of 772 billion yuan, the data showed. ■

articles.title: Prabowo says Indonesia can hit 6 pct growth by end of 2026
articles.body:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto gives his annual State of the Nation address in Jakarta, Indonesia, Aug. 14, 2026. Prabowo said Friday that Southeast Asia's largest economy could achieve a 6 percent growth rate by the end of this year despite global economic uncertainties. JAKARTA, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said Friday that Southeast Asia's largest economy could achieve a 6 percent growth rate by the end of this year despite global economic uncertainties.
In his annual State of the Nation address before members of the Parliament in the capital Jakarta, Prabowo said that Indonesia's economy grew 5.61 percent in the first quarter of 2026 and 5.45 percent in the first half of the year, marking the highest first-quarter and first-half growth rates in 13 years.
"With appropriate, rational policies based on common sense, I am confident that our economic growth can reach 6 percent by the end of this year," he said.
He emphasized that investment momentum remains robust despite global challenges. Realized investment reached 1,931 trillion rupiahs (about 108 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, creating more than 2.7 million jobs. In the first half of 2026, investment reached 1,010 trillion rupiahs, generating over 1.4 million additional jobs. ■

articles.body:
BAGHDAD, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Three drones were shot down early Friday over Erbil, the capital of Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region, local authorities said.
The regional Directorate General of Counter Terrorism said in a statement that U.S.-led international coalition forces shot down the drones.

Iraq's Kurdistan region has recently seen a rise in drone and missile attacks amid regional tensions linked to the ongoing confrontation between the United States and Iran. ■

articles.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
articles.body:

Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax.
The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market.
Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r.
Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY
— Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026
The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI).
These will allow investment assets such as shares and investment fund units to be exempt from the 19% capital gains tax up to a limit of 100,000 zloty. Of this amount, up to 25,000 zloty may be held in savings assets such as bonds and deposits.
Assets held in an OKI above those limits will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually.
Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”.
While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”.
“Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added.
Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych.
Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱
— Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026
The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic.
“Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP).
The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt.
Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years.
The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026
Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK).
However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age.
Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%.
By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%).
Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data https://t.co/NJX7MBmy3Z

articles.title: Chinese, Egyptian air forces to hold joint exercises
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese and Egyptian air forces are set to conduct joint exercises in Egypt from mid-August to early September, a Chinese military spokesperson said Friday.
Chen Xi, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, told a press conference that the drills, codenamed "Eagles of Civilization-2026," mark the second joint training between the two air forces.
The exercises will focus on air combat tactics, air superiority operations, combat search and rescue, as well as force employment drills, the spokesperson added.

articles.title: Japan raises eruption alert level for Mt. Aso over increased volcanic activity
articles.body:
TOKYO, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- Japan's weather agency on Friday raised the volcanic alert level for Mt. Aso in Kumamoto Prefecture from Level 2 to Level 3, citing intensified volcanic tremors and a sharp increase in volcanic gas emissions.
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) Fukuoka Regional Headquarters issued the Level 3 warning on Friday afternoon, restricting entry to the mountain.
According to the JMA, the amplitude of volcanic tremors at the mountain has been increasing since around 7:00 p.m. local time Wednesday. A field survey conducted Friday confirmed a rapid rise in volcanic gas emissions, indicating heightened volcanic activity.
The agency urged people within a radius of about 2 kilometers of the Nakadake No. 1 crater to be on alert for large volcanic blocks and pyroclastic flows associated with the eruption.
The JMA said it has found no clear evidence that the recent powerful Kumamoto earthquake has directly intensified volcanic activity at Mt. Aso, but it will continue to closely monitor the situation.
Mt. Aso's alert level had been raised from Level 1 to Level 2 in June this year due to elevated volcanic activity. Friday's upgrade to Level 3 marks the first such increase since February 2022. ■

articles.title: Israeli military says killed Hamas commander in Gaza
articles.body:
JERUSALEM, Aug. 14 (Xinhua) -- The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said in a statement on Friday that it killed a Hamas company commander who allegedly took part in the Hamas attack on southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.
According to the statement, the militant, Muhammad Bassam Muhammad Mushtaha, who served as a company commander in the Shati' Battalion of Hamas' military wing, was struck two weeks ago in the northern Gaza Strip.
The Israeli military said Mushtaha was involved in holding several Israeli hostages captive throughout the war.
The military claimed that Mushtaha had attempted to carry out attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians, prompting the military to target and kill him.
In October 2025, a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel came into effect.
Earlier this month, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu formally rejected the U.S.-backed 15-point plan for ending the Gaza conflict, insisting that Israel will not withdraw its forces from the enclave until Hamas is fully disarmed. ■

articles.title: The Bundeswehr is short of two thousand service members to deploy a German brigade in Lithuania
articles.body:
The Bundeswehr is short of two thousand service members to deploy a German brigade in Lithuania
Kyiv • UNN
The German army has a shortage of around 2,000 service members for the permanent deployment of a brigade in Lithuania by 2027. Only 60% of positions have been filled, and the Defence Ministry is considering compulsory recruitment.
The German army’s key project since the end of the Cold War has faced a personnel shortage. The permanent deployment of a Bundeswehr brigade in Lithuania requires 4,800 servicemen by the end of 2027, but only about 60% of positions are currently filled — approximately 2,000 people are still needed. Bild reports this, writes UNN.
Details
Germany’s Ministry of Defence told the publication that the units already deployed in Lithuania are 92% staffed. However, the main part of the brigade, including the tank battalion and mechanized infantry battalion, will arrive from Germany only in 2027. This is where the main personnel shortage remains.
Defence Minister Boris Pistorius had previously allowed for the possibility of compulsory recruitment of servicemen to carry out this task. Despite information campaigns, trips to Lithuania and other measures to attract volunteers, there are still not enough people willing to serve on NATO’s eastern flank.
A decision on compulsory recruitment must be made by the end of the year, as servicemen will need time to prepare for the relocation together with their families.
Recall
As UNN previously wrote, Germany plans the permanent deployment of nearly 5,000 troops in Lithuania to protect NATO’s eastern flank. Bundeswehr units will be ready by the end of 2027.

articles.title: Israeli PM Netanyahu calls UK ‘the Islamic Republic of Britain’
articles.body:
Israeli PM Netanyahu calls UK ‘the Islamic Republic of Britain’
The Israeli PM’s remark comes amid signs of growing tension between Israel and the UK’s Labour government.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has referred to the United Kingdom as the “Islamic Republic of Britain”, a dig at one of Israel’s historically closest European allies.
Netanyahu made the remark on the Israeli podcast Melech Blitzer Haim that aired on Thursday as he objected to British media coverage of Israel.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Trump says relationship is good even as Netanyahu rejects Gaza peace plan
- list 2 of 3US diplomat calls Israeli settler siege of West Bank homes ‘act of terror’
- list 3 of 3How the US far-right weaponised ‘inshallah’ against Abdul El-Sayed
As an example, Netanyahu pointed to British writer Randolph Churchill, who he praised for his “positive” coverage of Israel during the 1967 Six-Day War. Netanyahu then added sarcastically: “Go find that in Britain today, which you could call the Islamic Republic of Britain,” according to translated comments published by Israeli media.
Later in the podcast, Netanyahu appeared to reference comments made by JD Vance in 2022 that the UK may constitute the first nuclear-armed “Islamist country”.
“Someone said the first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons will be the Islamic Republic of Britain,” Netanyahu said.
“We are making sure there won’t be another one here, in Iran,” he added.
‘Does not speak for British Jews’
A British and Irish Jewish group criticised the Israeli prime minister’s comments as hateful and divisive.
“At a time when antisemitism, anti-Muslim hatred and social division are causing real fear across our country, language of this kind is dangerous and irresponsible,” said Rabbi Charley Baginsky and Rabbi Josh Lev, co-leads of the Movement for Progressive Judaism.
“Prime Minister Netanyahu does not speak for British Jews. His words do not represent us,” they said.
Gavin Barwell, former Downing Street chief of staff to Prime Minister Theresa May, said Netanyahu’s comments amounted to “blatant Islamophobia”.
“Let’s hope everyone will now shed the pretence some still cling to that this man is any friend of Britain,” Barwell wrote in a post on X.
Despite traditionally strong ties, tensions between the Israeli and British governments have grown since the progressive Labour Party took power in the UK in 2024.
Under former Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer, the UK paused free trade talks with Israel and suspended some arms export licences.
Like France, the UK has also imposed sanctions on far-right Israeli cabinet members Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.
Last year, the UK joined allies, including France and Canada, in recognising a Palestinian state.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently apologised for Labour’s initial response to Israel’s actions in Gaza, saying the party was too slow to call for a ceasefire.
“That is why we need to do more, which includes looking at further sanctions on those involved in the violence in Gaza but also looking at measures to ban trading goods with illegal settlements,” said Burnham. “We’ve got to do more to put pressure on the Israeli government.”
Rodwan Abouharb, associate professor in international relations at University College London, said Netanyahu’s jibe marks a “new low” in UK-Israel relations, but also “belies a considerable overlap in policy goals” between the two states regarding Iran.
“Netanyahu’s comments may be more for domestic purposes, to shore up his fractured governing coalition,” Abouharb told Al Jazeera.
A spokesperson for the Muslim Council of Britain (MCB) told Al Jazeera the comments highlight the UK’s need to reassess its relationship with Israel.
“Amplifying conspiracy theories about Britain is yet more evidence – if any was needed – that the UK Government needs to urgently re-evaluate its relationship with Israel as these are not the words of a reliable ally and partner (by the way, Britain is not a republic, we’re a constitutional monarchy),” said the MCB spokesperson.

articles.title: Zambia suspends election vote counting over reports of violence
articles.body:
Zambia suspends vote count nationwide amid reports of violence, ballot theft
Zambia's electoral commission on Friday suspended vote counting from Thursday's presidential and parliamentary elections for at least 24 hours due to “violence targeted at poll staff” and reported instances of theft of marked ballot papers. Former minister Brian Mundubile, the main challenger to President Hakainde Hichilema, claimed a first-round victory and said his camp viewed "the continued delay ... with grave concern".
Zambia suspended vote counting nationwide on Friday following reports of violence in some districts, the electoral commission said.
The copper-rich southern African nation went to the polls on Thursday in an election focused on economic hardship.
President Hakainde Hichilema, who has been in power since 2021, faced off against his main challenger among the 14 contenders – Brian Mundubile, a 55-year-old former minister in the previous Patriotic Front (PF) government.

"The violence is targeted at poll staff, and in some instances has resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers in ballot boxes," chief electoral officer Brown Kasaro said. The commission would review the suspension within 24 hours, he added.
Mundubile claimed a first-round victory on Friday.
"We have won this election both at presidential level and majority seats in parliament," said Mundubile.
"We therefore view the continued delay in the transparent announcement and verification of presidential results with grave concern," he added.
Read moreWho are the main contenders in Zambia's presidential vote?
Hichilema said his team was receiving "encouraging results".
Posting on social media, he urged citizens to "remain peaceful, patient and patriotic as we await the official outcome from those entrusted with managing the vote".
Official presidential results were expected on Monday.
Concerns over rights
Hichilema, a 64-year-old tycoon, won the presidency on his sixth attempt and was betting on job creation and an ambitious infrastructure drive to secure a final five-year term.
Backed by an alliance of opposition parties, Mundubile was running under the newly formed NRPUP party which draws much of its political base from the former ruling party.
He entered the race in May, injecting uncertainty into a contest that had long appeared to be Hichilema's to lose.
Some 8.7 million people were registered to vote. They were also electing 226 seats in parliament.
Counting in the parliamentary vote was also suspended.
Read moreZambia heads to polls with President Hichilema expected to win second term
Zambia has a long record of transferring power through the ballot box, with every change of president since the return to multiparty politics in 1991 achieved through elections.
The country has come under scrutiny over concerns that Hichilema's government has narrowed the space for dissent even as it promises stronger economic recovery.
On the eve of the election, Zambia's Human Rights Commission said it was "actively monitoring arrests and detentions involving political candidates, supporters, journalists and other actors".
Arrests
Earlier, the interior ministry said security agencies had arrested several suspects accused of plotting to interfere with the electoral system.
The ministry did not say how many people were arrested but said they included three former senior government officials accused of "providing technical services aimed at disrupting the electoral system".
A 56-year-old Kenyan national was also taken into custody, it said.
Three other people, including a former provincial minister, were found in possession of more than 7.3 million kwacha ($388,000) and summoned to assist with the investigation.
Despite also having significant potential in cobalt, nickel and manganese, the country continues to struggle with persistent poverty, unemployment and rising food prices.
More than 70 percent of its population of 22 million lives on less than three US dollars a day, according to the World Bank.
The previous government of late former president Edgar Lungu left Zambia in sovereign default after years of heavy borrowing.
Hichilema's administration has since secured a landmark debt restructuring deal, restored an International Monetary Fund programme and returned the economy to a growth path, winning praise from international lenders and investors.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

articles.title: The United States says that lowering oil prices, not Iran's nuclear program, is now the main priority in the war
articles.body:
The United States says that lowering oil prices, not Iran's nuclear program, is now the main priority in the war
Kyiv • UNN
U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance said that the main priority is lowering fuel prices, not Iran's nuclear program. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added that new economic measures against Tehran are inevitable.
The United States' main priority in the war with Iran right now is not the nuclear program but lowering fuel prices for American consumers, U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance said on Thursday, while the country's Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added that new economic measures to weaken Tehran are inevitable, UNN writes, citing AFP.
Details
The comments by Vance and Treasury Secretary Bessent illustrate the powerful leverage Tehran has gained by closing the Strait of Hormuz, the outlet notes.
Preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, which U.S. President Donald Trump has consistently called the main reason for the war, is now taking a back seat to restoring the free flow of oil through the strait, Vance said on Fox News.
Vance's comments underscored the stark reality that the war is now focused on control of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical fuel supply route that was open until Trump launched the war together with Israel in late February, the outlet notes.
Iran claims control over the Strait of Hormuz following Trump's remarks13.08.26, 13:09 • 4642 views
"Iran effectively closed it in response and thereby found a decisive bargaining chip against Trump, who is trying to find a way out of the war and is avoiding the resumption of large-scale attacks," the outlet notes.
The approval rating of the 80-year-old U.S. president is plummeting, the war is unpopular among Americans, and the November midterm elections are approaching, the outlet writes.
Republicans, as noted, fear that Trump and the war, which caused a sharp increase in gasoline prices, will cost them control of Congress.
"I know oil fell today, and it's significantly below the highs at the beginning of the conflict," Vance said on Fox News. "That's the number one goal—to keep oil and gas cheap for Americans across our country."
"And then, obviously, number two is to ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon," he added.

articles.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Key Units at Syzran Oil Refinery
articles.body:
Ukrainian drones struck key facilities at the Syzran Oil Refinery, which is part of the Russian company Rosneft.
This was discovered jointly by the monitoring platform Exilenova+ and the OSINT channel world.militares.
Damage was reported to two existing atmospheric-vacuum oil distillation units—AVT-5 and AVT-6.
They are intended for the initial distillation of crude oil and its separation into basic fractions (gasoline, kerosene, and diesel) for the subsequent production of fuel.
The 43-102 catalytic cracking unit (Unit II), which converts heavy oil fractions into lighter ones, including gasoline and gas components, was struck.
Ukrainian drones struck the PGI-DIG/280 unit, designed for the production of a high-octane gasoline component, and the L-35/11-600 unit, which is used for the catalytic reforming of gasoline fractions and the production of high-octane components. The drones also struck the CAS unit – a processing and stabilization facility for hydrocarbon streams.
In addition, a smokestack was reported to have fallen onto the L-35/11-600 unit after being struck by a drone. It fell directly onto the equipment, which likely caused damage to it.
Consequently, the damage affected the primary and secondary oil refining facilities, as well as the production of high-octane fuel components.
This is the second similar strike on a Russian oil refinery in August. This time, Ukrainian Defense Forces targeted not just a single primary processing unit but the entire production chain of the facility.
The first was the Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery.
The attack on the oil refinery in Syzran took place on the night of August 7–8 as part of efforts to reduce Russia’s military and economic capabilities. The strike caused several fires on the refinery grounds. Local residents reported several dozen explosions.
The refinery is part of the Rosneft Oil company and has a technical capacity of processing between 8.5 and 8.9 million tons of oil per year, which accounts for more than 3% of Russia’s total output. Its products include automotive gasoline, K5/Euro-5 diesel fuel, jet fuel, fuel oil, and bitumen.
The facility is located more than 800 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. The refinery supplies fuel to Russia’s Samara, Saratov, and Penza regions, as well as parts of the country’s central regions. It also supplies fuel to airfields and military units of Russia’s Central and Southern Military Districts. The complex has been targeted by Ukrainian attacks before.

articles.title: Ukraine will hand over trophy Russian T-72 tanks to museums in five European countries – defence ministry
articles.body:
Ukraine will hand over trophy Russian T-72 tanks to museums in five European countries – defence ministry
The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the creation of a mechanism for handing over destroyed trophy Russian equipment to museums in other countries. Under the mechanism, captured T-72 tanks are to be handed over to museums in five countries.
Source: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence
Details: The ministry said this concerns trophy military equipment captured or obtained while repelling Russian aggression. It will be handed over free of charge to foreign museums for use as museum exhibits or for organising exhibitions.
Quote: "In particular, museums in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Denmark and the Netherlands will receive captured T-72 tanks for exhibition use."
More details: The ministry added that the equipment lost its combat capability, contains no explosive elements and can be safely displayed to visitors. The decision was adopted on the initiative of the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Culture of Ukraine.
Quote: "Such exhibitions abroad will help communicate objective information about Ukraine's ongoing struggle for independence and present the international community with tangible evidence of the war."
The Defence Ministry also expects such exhibitions to help develop cultural diplomacy and cooperation with foreign museum institutions.
Background: Earlier, the Ministry of Defence launched the state platform TrophyLab, through which manufacturers, engineers, scientists, laboratories and international partners can gain access to trophy Russian equipment for weapons research.

articles.title: EU is in no position morrally to talk about human rights

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis discussed bilateral issues and the latest international and regional developments in a phone call on Thursday.

articles.title: FIA Lifts Restrictions on Russian and Belarusian Drivers, Restores Flags and Anthems
articles.body:
- Category
- World
FIA Lifts Restrictions on Russian and Belarusian Drivers, Restores Flags and Anthems
The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile, or FIA, has lifted restrictions on Russian and Belarusian drivers and teams, allowing them to compete internationally under their national flags, colors, and anthems again, according to an internal FIA circular dated August 13.
The decision effectively ends the neutrality requirements that had governed participation by competitors from Russia and Belarus.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The FIA’s World Motor Sport Council, or WMSC, approved the changes on August 3 following consultations, according to the document.
Under the revised rules, Russian and Belarusian drivers, national teams, and individual competitors may now participate in international and regional motorsport events without the previous restrictions.
Competitors are also no longer required to sign neutrality commitments before taking part.
The rules once again permit the display of Russian and Belarusian national symbols and colors on racing suits, equipment, and vehicles. Their national flags may also be shown at competitions, while the countries’ national anthems can once again be played.
The decision marks a significant rollback of the restrictions that had separated Russian and Belarusian competitors from their national representation in international motorsport.
One major limitation, however, remains in place.
The FIA continues to prohibit international and regional competitions from being held on the territory of Russia or Belarus “until further notice.”
That means Russian and Belarusian competitors can return under their own national identities abroad, but neither country is currently permitted to host FIA-sanctioned international or regional events.
The organization said it would continue “closely monitoring developments in Ukraine” and reserved the right to take additional measures in the future.
The new policy therefore restores most of the sporting and national representation previously denied to Russian and Belarusian participants while keeping the geographical ban on FIA competition inside the two countries.
Earlier, World Boxing cleared Russian boxers across all age categories to participate in international tournaments using their national flag and anthem.
The Netherlands previously decided to cancel its hosting of the 2026 European Paralympic Swimming Championships due to the participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes under their own flags.

articles.title: Ukraine Strikes 29 Energy Facilities in Temporarily Occupied Territories During “Crimean Switch Off” Operation
articles.body:
- Category

Ukraine Strikes 29 Energy Facilities in Temporarily Occupied Territories During “Crimean Switch Off” Operation
Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) struck 29 energy infrastructure facilities in Russian-occupied parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions and Crimea overnight on August 13 as part of the “Crimean Switch Off” operation.
According to the commander of the USF, Robert “Madyar” Brovdi on August 14, the targets included the Balaklava Thermal Power Plant in Sevastopol, as well as multiple electrical substations and a gas distribution station.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
“Occupational noir: +29 energy nodes in the south of the temporarily occupied territories were visited by the Bird of the Unmanned Systems Forces as part of the ‘Crimean Switch Off’ operation,” Brovdi said.
The commander said that between July 1 and August 13, Ukrainian forces had successfully struck 240 energy infrastructure facilities as part of the operation.
The latest strikes targeted facilities in the temporarily occupied parts of Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions, including substations in Berdiansk, Mariupol, Prymorsk, Chernihivka, Mykolaivka, and other settlements.
The Unmanned Systems Forces also struck the GRS-1 Mariupol gas distribution station in the occupied Donetsk region.
Brovdi said the operation also aims to disrupt Russian air defense infrastructure by cutting power to stationary radars and other elements of the system.
“De-energizing stationary radars and other elements of the enemy’s air defense disrupts the system protecting the sky and opens the way for the freedom-loving Ukrainian bird,” he said.
Among the facilities targeted overnight was the Balaklava Thermal Power Plant in Sevastopol, Crimea.
Several days earlier, Russia’s largest liquefied petroleum gas producer has suspended operations indefinitely following a Ukrainian drone strike on the ZapSibNeftekhim petrochemical complex in Tobolsk, more than 2,200 kilometers (1,370 miles) from the front line.

articles.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sets Russia’s Ust-Luga Port Ablaze Overnight
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Ukrainian Drone Attack Sets Russia’s Ust-Luga Port Ablaze Overnight
A fire broke out at the Ust-Luga port in northwestern Russia overnight on August 14 following a reported drone attack.
Leningrad Region Governor Alexander Drozdenko said the fire was caused by damage sustained during the attack and that emergency crews were working to extinguish the blaze.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
“Following the damage, a fire was reported at the Ust-Luga port. Specialists have begun extinguishing it. Combat operations are ongoing,” Drozdenko said.
By 6:21 a.m. local time, he claimed that 51 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region.
The attack also affected air traffic in the region. According to Fontanka, St. Petersburg’s Pulkovo Airport began operating under restrictions from around 3 a.m., with delays reported for some flights.
About Ust-Luga port
Russia’s Ust-Luga is the Baltic Sea’s second-largest and most technologically advanced seaport, and ranks among the largest ports in Europe.
Although the facility handles a range of cargo, its main role is the export of crude oil and petroleum products. Ust-Luga also serves as the endpoint of the Baltic Pipeline System-II (BPS-II).
The port is situated in Luga Bay on the Gulf of Finland, about 110 kilometers from St. Petersburg and close to the Estonian border.
The August 14 incident was not the first reported attack on infrastructure at Ust-Luga. On the night of March 24–25, strike drones targeted the Gazprom Ust-Luga gas processing plant in the Leningrad region, according to Militarnyi.
The facility, located roughly 1,000 kilometers from Ukraine’s border, was reportedly hit by at least 10 explosions. Local residents described a large glow in the night sky, followed by a column of black smoke visible after dawn.

CJI Surya Kant said his 'cockroach' remark was 'misquoted and misused' through clipped court videos, warning against misleading social media posts.
NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has said that his oral remarks during a Supreme Court hearing were “misquoted” and later used with “malicious intent” to mislead the country’s youth, amid controversy over a comment that sparked the satirical online movement “Cockroach Janta Party”."My comment was misquoted and misused. Therefore, I would urge them to keep their responsibilities in mind; we must all make tireless efforts to ensure that harmony prevails in society," he added.
On May 15, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, Kant had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to “cockroaches” who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system.
The remarks triggered widespread backlash among young people and inspired the satirical “Cockroach Janta Party” (CJP) movement.The CJP later led protests at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. articles.title: Chad's president pardons main rival and opposition leader in jail
articles.body:
Chad's president pardons main rival and opposition leader in jail
N'DJAMENA, Aug 14 - Chad's presidency said in a statement that President Mahamat Idriss Deby has pardoned his main rival and opposition leader Succes Masra, who has been in jail for more than a year for inciting violence and complicity to murder.
• Masra, a former prime minister, was sentenced to 20 years and fined 1 billion CFA francs ($1.77 million) last year in a trial that was criticized by human rights activists as politically motivated.
• Masra will be released in the coming days, the statement said, after the presidency agreed to a request for a pardon submitted by his attorneys.
• Masra was internationally recognized as the most vocal figure in the opposition. He will be freed along with eight other political figures, the statement said.
• "These nine individuals will be released as soon as the Ministry of Justice makes the necessary arrangements in the coming hours and days," the presidency said.
• "They have been pardoned by the Head of State. However, the pardon does not waive the civil penalties, which remain enforceable." REUTERS

articles.title: Erdoğan: Türkiye now shapes its future through own will
articles.body:
President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on Aug. 14 hailed his ruling Justice and Development Party’s (AKP) 25-year journey, saying it had transformed Türkiye into a country that “shapes its future by its own will.”
In an article marking the party’s 25th founding anniversary, Erdoğan said his movement was founded with the aim of reshaping Türkiye’s future, strengthening the bond between the state and citizens and ensuring that the country could make its own decisions.
“Nothing will ever be the same in Türkiye again,” Erdoğan recalled saying when the party was founded, adding that its “greatest source of confidence was the will of the people.”
He said the party emerged as a “common hope” for millions who faced restrictions on their rights, carried the burden of crises and sought a more prosperous future for their children.
“Looking back today, we see that the AK Party’s quarter-century corresponds to a historic transformation... Türkiye has evolved into a country that sets its own goals, believes in its capabilities and shapes its future through its own will,” Erdoğan said.
He said democratic legitimacy had been strengthened, the state’s capacity to deliver public services had improved and participation in public life had expanded.
Referring to the 2016 coup attempt as one of the “most severe tests” of democratic legitimacy, Erdoğan said the Turkish people had demonstrated that no power outside the ballot box could determine the country’s future.
“This determined stance was a historic turning point in leaving the era of tutelage behind, strengthening civilian politics and consolidating our democracy,” he said.
Erdoğan highlighted investments in education, health care, transportation, energy, social policies and urban development, saying public services had been expanded across the country and economic and social participation had been strengthened.
He also pointed to advances in the defense industry and high technology, saying Türkiye had significantly reduced its dependence on foreign suppliers in strategic areas.
He cited unmanned aerial vehicles, the indigenous Kaan fighter jet, warships and air defense systems, as well as the Togg electric vehicle, the country’s space program, nuclear energy investments and natural gas discoveries in the Black Sea as symbols of Türkiye’s “new confidence.”
“Going forward, we will turn this accumulated experience into a new leap in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, energy technologies and high value-added production,” he said.
Erdoğan said Türkiye had become an influential actor in an increasingly multipolar international system, pursuing a foreign policy based on national interests, diplomacy, dialogue and humanitarian responsibility.
He said Türkiye had strengthened its ties with the Turkic and Islamic worlds while advocating for the rights of the oppressed on international platforms.
He described Türkiye as “a strong NATO ally, an active G20 member, a leading member of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and a key actor in Europe’s security architecture.”
“From the Black Sea to the Middle East, the Caucasus to Africa, we are contributing to peace and stability across a broad geography,” he said.
Meanwhile, lawmaker Ömer Karakaş resigned from the İYİ (Good) Party, reducing the nationalist organization’s number of seats in parliament to 27. He was expected to join the AKP at an event later on Aug. 14.

articles.title: Some 20,610 cases of deportation or forced displacement of children verified in Ukraine – Justice Ministry
articles.body:
Minister of Justice Denys Maslov and UNICEF Representative in Ukraine Anne-Claire Dufay discussed the return of Ukrainian children deported or forcibly displaced as a result of Russia’s armed aggression, of whom 20,610 cases have been confirmed to date, the Ministry of Justice reports.
This was stated in a message published on the official website of the Ministry of Justice on Thursday. The working meeting between Maslov and Dufay took place on August 11.
"Currently, 20,610 cases of deportation or forced displacement of Ukrainian children have been confirmed. This figure is not final, as information continues to arrive, and each case requires individual verification," the message reads.
The parties also discussed the further development of child-centered justice, the sustainability of existing child protection mechanisms, and new areas of cooperation between the Ministry of Justice and UNICEF.
"Today, Ukrainian children are going through difficult trials as a result of Russia’s armed aggression against Ukraine. Our task is to ensure their access to fair justice and the necessary legal and psychological support. Despite all the challenges, Ukraine continues to develop a child-centered justice system, and we look forward to a further systemic partnership with UNICEF in this area," Maslov noted.
He emphasized that protecting children’s rights and developing juvenile justice remain among the Ministry’s priorities and are an important component of Ukraine’s European integration commitments. He emphasized that cooperation with international partners should be focused primarily on achieving practical results for every child and ensuring the sustainability of mechanisms that have already proven their effectiveness.
Special attention was paid during the meeting to the protection of children deported or forcibly displaced due to Russia’s armed aggression against Ukraine. The Ministry of Justice noted that the return of every Ukrainian child begins with their identification and reliable information about their fate. Russia does not provide Ukraine with information on deported or forcibly displaced children. Therefore, documentation, verification, and information exchange are crucial for establishing the whereabouts of children and their return.
"The Ministry of Justice maintains the Registry of Information on Children Deported or Forcibly Displaced in Connection with Russia’s Armed Aggression against Ukraine, as well as provides organizational support for the work of the Interdepartmental Commission for the Verification of Relevant Information," the Ministry of Justice website states.
Following the meeting, the parties confirmed their commitment to deepening their strategic partnership and focusing future cooperation on solutions that will ensure concrete and long-term results for Ukrainian children.

articles.title: Assad-era officer convicted in Austria returns to Syria amid ongoing appeal: sources
articles.body:
A former Syrian security officer sentenced to prison in Austria for abusing detainees during Bashar al Assad’s regime left the country while appealing against his sentence and returned to Syria earlier this month, according to four sources and messages reviewed by Reuters.
Lieutenant Colonel Musab Abu Rukba was handed an eight-year prison sentence last month by a Vienna court that found him guilty of bodily harm, aggravated coercion and sexual assault against detained opponents of Assad while he headed the police's criminal investigations department in the city of Raqqa more than a decade ago.
The Syria Justice and Accountability Centre, a Syrian human rights organisation, said the case exposed shortcomings in the Austrian judicial system after authorities allowed Abu Rukba to remain at liberty throughout proceedings and while challenging his prison sentence on appeal.
Abu Rukba had pleaded not guilty. In early August, he arrived in his hometown of Nawa in southern Daraa province.
The invitation said he had been granted "release from prison," according to a message sent to local dignitaries and seen by Reuters.
A spokesperson for the Austrian court that convicted him told Reuters on Friday that ahead of the trial, he was found not to pose a flight risk because he had been living in Austria since 2014 and was seeking asylum there along with his family.
He was not remanded in custody during the trial and was also not subject to other restrictions. Until the appeals process is included, his departure from Austria does not constitute a breach of any Austrian laws or rulings, the spokesperson said.
“The escape of a lieutenant colonel accused of torture, sexual coercion and serious bodily harm demonstrates a failure by the Austrian authorities to assess the danger posed by this defendant and their failure to place him in pre-trial detention,” Mohammad al-Abdallah, executive director of the Syria Justice and Accountability Centre said.
Syria’s new authorities have pledged to hold former Assad officials accountable for abuses committed during his rule. A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced Assad to death in absentia for killings, torture, arbitrary arrest and crimes against humanity.
Assad fled to Russia in December 2024.

articles.title: Drone crashes in Romania near border with Ukraine
articles.body:
Drone crashes in Romania near border with Ukraine
A drone crashed in Romania's Tulcea County, about five kilometres from the Ukrainian border, after flying too low to be detected by radar surveillance systems.
Source: European Pravda, citing Romania's Ministry of National Defence
Details: On Friday 14 August, Romania's Ministry of National Defence received a report via the 112 emergency number that a drone had crashed near Luncavița in Tulcea County, five kilometres from the Ukrainian border.
According to the information available so far, the aerial target was not detected by the Ministry of National Defence's radar surveillance systems because it was flying at a very low altitude.
The drone crashed in a wooded area and, according to preliminary information, caused no casualties or property damage.
"A team of specialists from the Ministry of National Defence will survey the area aboard an IAR 330 PUMA SOCAT helicopter. We will provide further information as the situation develops," the ministry said.
Background:
- On 26 July, Romania shot down a drone that had violated its airspace from a fighter jet for the third consecutive day.
- The first combat use of aircraft over Romania to shoot down such a UAV – later confirmed to have been a Shahed-type drone – took place on 24 July.
- This followed numerous incidents in which Russian drones entered Romanian territory and crashed there, mostly in areas along the Danube near the border, during Russian attacks targeting Ukrainian ports.

articles.title: In Kherson region, the occupation authorities registered 2,700 Ukrainians for military service in the Russian army
articles.body:
In Kherson region, the occupation authorities registered 2,700 Ukrainians for military service in the Russian army
Kyiv • UNN
The occupation authorities have registered at least 2,700 residents of Kherson region for military service, and some have already been drafted into the Russian army. Six officials involved in this were notified in absentia that they are suspected of criminal wrongdoing.
In the temporarily occupied part of the Kherson region, at least 2,700 residents were registered for military service with a view to subsequently recruiting them into the occupiers’ army, while some of them have already been conscripted into the armed forces of the Russian Federation. This was reported by the Office of the Prosecutor General, UNN reports.
The occupation authorities registered at least 2,700 residents of the temporarily occupied Kherson region for military service with a view to subsequently recruiting them to serve in the Russian army. According to investigators, some of them have already been conscripted into the armed forces of the aggressor state
According to the investigation, those involved in organizing this system include the so-called "governor of the Kherson region," four heads of occupation military enlistment offices, and an official of the occupation administration responsible for mobilization efforts. Prosecutors from the Kherson Regional Prosecutor’s Office notified them in absentia that they were suspects.
All six are charged with violating the laws and customs of war, committed by a group of persons. The Ukrainian citizen who worked in the occupation administration is additionally charged with collaboration activities.
According to the investigation, the system was coordinated by the so-called "governor." On the basis of his orders, conscription commissions were established, the procedure for mobilization measures was determined, and cooperation between the occupation authorities and military structures of the Russian Federation was organized
According to available information, in July 2023, the so-called "Military Commissariat of the Kherson Region" was established in Henichesk. Through its subordinate structures in the occupied territory, data on men of conscription age were collected, they were registered for military service, medical examinations were organized, and conscription campaigns were conducted.
Separately, an official who assumed a leadership position in the occupation administration and was responsible for mobilization efforts coordinated military registration in the captured communities, the work of military registration offices, and cooperation between the occupation "military enlistment offices" and the administration.
Men were forced to undergo conscription procedures under threat of violence, unlawful deprivation of liberty, restrictions on leaving the territory, loss of access to social services, and deportation. In some cases, torture was used. In this way, the occupation authorities created a mechanism for systematically coercing Ukrainian citizens who remained in the occupied territory to serve in the army of the aggressor state

articles.title: "Islamic Britain": Netanyahu's remarks ignite political storm in UK
articles.body:
ALBAWABA - U.S. and Turkish intelligence agencies did not confirm repeated Israeli warnings that Iran was preparing to kill U.S. President Donald Trump, according to a Reuters report citing current and former American officials.
The article said last year that Israeli intelligence began passing the warnings to U.S. agencies, including direct briefings to senior White House officials. The purported threats included a sniper attack, a knife attack at a public gathering, and subsequently a probable shoulder-fired missile strike on Trump’s plane.
The starkest warning came ahead of last month's NATO summit in Ankara, where Israeli officials said Iran could try to hit Air Force One following Trump's visit to Turkey, Reuters said.
But U.S. sources said the CIA could not independently corroborate the purported plots to assassinate, despite intelligence provided by Israel. Turkish intelligence allegedly came to the same conclusion in its own evaluation and told Washington it had no evidence to back the Israeli accusations.
Although the intelligence was not verified, the White House and the U.S. Secret Service are said to have implemented extra security precautions during Trump’s visit to Turkey, including a bizarre decoy maneuver in which the president was transferred from Air Force One to a different plane before leaving.
The episode has raised attention over the role of Israeli intelligence in molding U.S. policy toward Iran, especially as tensions between Washington and Tehran continue to escalate.
Reuters said numerous U.S. intelligence officials have questioned the credibility of the Israeli findings, which depended heavily on Israeli sources and could not be independently validated thru American intelligence channels.
The controversy also exposes deeper differences between U.S. and Israeli intelligence assessments of Iran. Former U.S. officials told Reuters that until they can be independently corroborated, unsubstantiated allegations are routinely given a low trust rating by U.S. agencies, considering that Washington often relies on Israeli intelligence in the Middle East.
Israeli officials have been bypassing the usual intelligence channels and instead have been giving briefings directly to senior White House officials over the past year, the report said. Some U.S. analysts said the move was intended not only to share intelligence, but also to influence American policy toward Iran and the broader region.

articles.title: Tourists beat the heat with ‘magical’ Colosseum night tours
articles.body:
Tourists beat the heat with ‘magical’ Colosseum night tours
Rome - The Colosseum has extended opening hours at night this summer to allow more visitors to see the famous Roman amphitheatre in cooler temperatures after sunset.
The night tours, which run until 11pm, are sold out and tourists on one visit this week spoke of a “magical” and “romantic” atmosphere in the illuminated monument.
“After sunset is a lot more comfortable,” Victor Li, 52, told AFP as he toured the arena and the underground passages where animals and gladiators were once held.
“It’s a good idea because it’s really hot in the morning and during the day,” said Svetlana Spielberg, visiting from the United States, adding that it was “really beautiful” and “more romantic” at night.
The Colosseum was already offering tours two nights a week but doubled that number to four this summer. Officials said some tourists were staying away because of the intensifying heatwaves in the Italian capital.
“The idea of doubling the night tours and doing them also on Fridays and Saturdays was mainly to give access to visitors that prefer cooler hours,” said Simone Quilici, director of the Colosseum complex.
The extended opening had been made possible thanks to a grant from the Italian culture ministry and the initiative could be extended into September, he added.
The tours are all guided and numbers have been kept low – at just 275 people a night. The monument gets up to 20,000 visitors a day at peak times.
The Colosseum, the largest amphitheatre in the world, was built in the first century and was used to host events like animal hunts and gladiatorial games.
It could hold around 50,000 spectators.
Marco Pravini, who was visiting from Cremona, said he had also visited the amphitheatre during the day but “at night the light, the atmosphere is much more magical”. AFP

articles.title: Britain defends decision to seize shadow fleet ship; Putin threatens
articles.body:
After Russian dictator Vladimir Putin threatened to retaliate, the British government has defended its decision to seize a Russian shadow fleet tanker in the English Channel, the BBC reports.
The tanker Smyrtos has been anchored off Weymouth since being seized by a Royal Navy special forces unit in June. The ship’s captain, Ajay Pant, has been accused of violating sanctions on Russia by directly or indirectly supplying Russian oil.
While watching naval exercises in the Pacific, Putin lashed out at Western countries that intercept Russian ships, saying such actions were nothing more than banditry and piracy.
Western countries believe Russia is using a shadow fleet of hundreds of ships to circumvent sanctions on oil exports. These ships have a complex ownership structure and use a range of tactics to conceal the origin of their cargo, masking their links to Russia. The British Ministry of Defence has said that the shadow fleet could include more than 700 tankers, carrying around 75% of the sanctioned oil. The ministry added that the oil trade is critical to the Kremlin and allows it to continue financing its aggression against Ukraine.
Putin warned Western countries on the 12th of August not to seize tankers,
saying that if they did, Russia would respond in kind. Moreover, this would happen not only in places where raids were carried out against Russian ships, but anywhere it was deemed necessary and acceptable – in other words, everywhere. Viktor Liina, commander of the Russian Pacific Fleet, accused Western countries, including Britain and France, of having their own “shadow fleets.” Liina added that the Russians have sufficient capacity to intercept and inspect ships of unfriendly countries, and an interagency operation has been launched to deal with these challenges.
The British government, responding to Putin’s comments, said that British forces and law enforcement officers boarded the Smyrtos in full compliance with international law. The government spokesman added that, unlike the Russian shadow fleet, British forces and commercial vessels operate in accordance with international maritime law.
The Smyrtos will continue to be in the port of Weymouth, where it is monitored by British authorities. The ship’s owner is responsible for the maintenance of the ship, including providing the ship’s crew with necessary products.
22 of the 25 crew members returned to their homes in July.
Putin’s comments came as the European Union seeks to increase pressure on Russia’s shadow fleet. Speaking to Russian sailors, Putin singled out the EU for violating international shipping laws and seeking to restrict the movement of ships owned by Russian businessmen.
EU foreign policy chief Anitta Hipper said European countries would not be intimidated by Russian threats. She said the key for Europe was to limit Russia’s ability to make profits that are then used to finance the war, including by restricting the activities of the shadow fleet.

articles.title: Russia Dismisses Calls for Black Sea Ceasefire
articles.body:
Russia's Foreign Ministry on Friday dismissed the idea of a ceasefire with Ukraine in the Black Sea, saying it saw no grounds for "half-measures" that would offer a respite to Ukrainian forces.
Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks against commercial ships in the Black Sea in recent weeks, which has driven world grain prices higher.
In a statement, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of "brazen acts of terrorism" against shipping while making no mention of Russia's own attacks.
"We view these attacks as a deliberate policy aimed at destabilizing civilian shipping in the Black Sea region, to escalate tensions further and prolong the conflict, all with the blatant acquiescence of regional neighbors," Zakharova said.
"At the same time, we see no signs of improvement in the situation and, consequently, no grounds for half-measures that merely grant the Kyiv regime temporary breathing space," she added.
Zakharova was responding to remarks by Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, who told media outlets that Ankara had put forward proposals to both sides for a moratorium on military operations in the Black Sea.
She said Russia has received no formal proposal from Turkey.
Reuters reported on Thursday that Ukraine had passed an offer to Russia through a third party to halt attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea.
Zakharova also ruled out returning to the 2022-23 Black Sea Grain initiative brokered by Turkey and the UN. That arrangement allowed Russia and Ukraine — both major grain exporters — to safely ship grain through the Black Sea.
The agreement, which Zakharova called one-sided, collapsed after Russia pulled out, claiming Western commitments regarding its own exports were never fulfilled.
